name: Linear Coding Agent Harness (coleam00)
one_line: Minimal Claude Agent SDK harness on a Claude Code OAuth token: an initializer session turns app_spec.txt into ~50 Linear issues with test steps plus a META issue; each subsequent fresh coding session queries Linear for the top Todo issue, re-runs verification of previously completed features, implements, tests via Puppeteer MCP, comments notes, and marks Done.
why_relevant: (1) A subscription-seat two-agent pattern with the tracker as the shared task list and session-handoff memory (no local files). Re-verifying prior features at the start of every session is a cheap regression guard for long unattended builds.
claimed_results: none stated

name: Continuous Claude
one_line: Bash conductor that loops Claude Code: new branch -> commit -> open PR via gh -> wait on CI checks and reviews -> merge on green, close and discard on red -> pull main -> repeat, with one markdown handoff file as relay-race memory between iterations.
why_relevant: (3) Uses the repo's own CI as the external verifier with discard-on-failure, so the agent never grades itself. (2) Documents the failure mode of cross-iteration memory (verbose logs harm) and the prompt discipline that fixed it ('make meaningful progress on one thing, then leave clear notes').
claimed_results: README (2025-11): built to take a codebase with 'hundreds of thousands of lines of code' from '0% to 80%+ coverage in the next few weeks'; gives a production example of a failure note picked up and prioritised by the next iteration; no aggregate numbers

name: CORAL
one_line: Infrastructure for multi-agent self-evolution: Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor/Kiro agents each run in their own git worktree, share attempts/notes/skills via .coral/public/, a grader daemon scores every commit, a manager interrupts with heartbeat prompts (reflect/consolidate/pivot), and multi-island runs partition agents with migration; Docker mode runs agents as an unprivileged user so they cannot read .coral/private/ (grader venv, answer keys).
why_relevant: (3) OS-level separation of grader from agents mirrors the owner's held-out half enforced by sandbox rules. (2) Shared-state evolution with island isolation and heartbeat interventions is a template for the learning corpus and in-run healing. (1) Subscription CLIs as workers.
claimed_results: README News: accepted to COLM 2026 (2026-07-08); arXiv 2604.01658 (2026-04-03); no headline numbers in README

name: LIFT (Loaded Impact on Final Task)
one_line: Evaluation framework for agent self-evolution: warmup tasks run in one container to trigger memory/skill/self-rewrite, the delta is captured as a Docker image, then every holdout task runs twice (clean baseline vs evolved) reporting delta turns, delta tool calls and delta tokens; live TUI/dashboard and a cross-runtime leaderboard sorted by delta-turns%.
why_relevant: (2)+(3) Exactly the measurement the owner's self-maintaining tier needs: whether the learning corpus improves held-out tasks, with symmetric baseline/evolved containers so the comparison is not self-graded.
claimed_results: README (Chinese): leaderboard hosted at feizhuniu-infja.github.io/LIFT/leaderboard.html ranking 'evolution impact' (each row minus its own base); leaderboard values not captured in this sweep

name: CoEvoSkills
one_line: A Skill Generator and a Surrogate Verifier co-evolve reusable multi-file Skill packages without access to protected answers; a fresh ground-truth agent periodically tests the Skill in isolation (task + Skill only, never the background document or the evolution conversation); canonical reward 1.0 ends evolution; 85 SkillsBench-derived Docker tasks.
why_relevant: (2)+(3) Information isolation between the thing that learns and the thing that grades, plus an independent transfer test by a fresh agent, is a template for validating exemplars/skills in the owner's learning corpus before injecting them into prompts.
claimed_results: README: 62/85 (72.9%) bundled Skills validated at canonical reward 1.0 in fresh Skill-only runs, remaining 23 retained as candidates; 'Accepted at COLM 2026'; arXiv 2604.01687

name: Tripwire
one_line: Four-layer adversarial correctness oracle for AI code-optimization loops: L1 canonical check on visible inputs, L2 metamorphic/property invariants, L3 differential check on withheld adversarial inputs the candidate never saw, L4 isolated speedup measured only after correctness; ships as a drop-in OpenEvolve evaluator.
why_relevant: (3) The withheld-input layer is the owner's held-out suite idea applied to optimisation loops, and `tripwire demo` exits non-zero if any hack ever ships, a built-in negative control. Tiny repo but unusually on-brief for reward-hack detection.
claimed_results: README (2026-07): across 20 labelled candidates (3 correct, 4 correct-up-to-FP, 13 reward hacks): naive bitwise 'ships 9 of 13 hacks and discards every floating-point-correct win (keeps only 43% of valid candidates)'; naive tolerance 'ships every single hack, 13 of 13'; Tripwire 'ships 0 hacks and keeps 100% of valid wins'
last_activity: pushed 2026-07-29; 2 stars; 1 fork; MIT; PyPI tripwire-oracle

name: swebench-pro (kimjune01) - oracle-access correction
one_line: A one-person SWE-bench Pro harness run (recon -> craft -> audit loop on a Claude subscription plus EC2) that resolved 694/728 under the official grader, then published a correction that the gate had iterated against the visible FAIL_TO_PASS tests, making the figure an oracle-availability ceiling rather than a harness lift.
why_relevant: (3) A quantified demonstration of why the builder must never see the held-out half: the author estimates ~46 of 96 points came from the answer key. Direct justification for the owner's sealed split and the falseFinish metric; also shows a subscription-seat loop can drive a full benchmark.
claimed_results: README (2026-06, Zenodo DOI): 'resolved 694 of them, 95.3%' re-graded by the official grader; open-weight models '93.1% under the same visible-test-gated setup'; correction: 'An implement-only loop with no oracle access floors near 50% on the same instances; gate access to the visible tests raises it to about 96%, so roughly 46 of the points are bought by the answer key'

name: Darwin Godel Machine (DGM)
one_line: Self-improving coding agent that edits its own code, keeps an archive of all variants (children can branch from any archived parent), and empirically validates each change on SWE-bench and Polyglot inside Docker; no fine-tuning.
why_relevant: (2) Foundational prior art for offline self-repair of a pipeline's own code behind a frozen benchmark, with an archive rather than hill-climbing to avoid dead ends; benchmark is the sole fitness signal. Older than 18 months at the edge (May 2025) and the repo is idle since 2025-08, but heavily built upon (weill-labs/hgm, many re-implementations).
claimed_results: arXiv 2505.22954 abstract (submitted 2025-05-29): 'increasing performance on SWE-bench from 20.0% to 50.0%, and on Polyglot from 14.2% to 30.7%'

name: Self-Improving Coding Agent (SICA)
one_line: Agent framework that evaluates the current agent version on benchmark tasks, archives results, runs the agent on its own codebase to make an improvement, and iterates; includes an overseer and an event-bus call-graph visualiser; always run inside Docker.
why_relevant: (2) Prior art for the owner's offline self-diagnosis and repair of the orchestrator's own code behind a gate; documents the need for an overseer and sandboxing when the agent edits itself. Unmaintained since 2025-04.
claimed_results: arXiv 2504.15228 abstract (submitted 2025-04-21, v2 2025-05-16): 'performance gains from 17% to 53% on a random subset of SWE Bench Verified, with additional performance gains on LiveCodeBench'

name: SE-Agent
one_line: Trajectory-level self-evolution (revision, recombination, refinement across parallel reasoning paths) layered on SWE-agent-style scaffolds so failed attempts inform each other instead of being retried blindly; NeurIPS 2025 poster.
why_relevant: (2) Test-time self-improvement without training by exchanging information across trajectories, adjacent to the owner's fix seat: recombine prior failed attempts rather than fingerprint-and-retry.
claimed_results: README (2025-09): '80% Top1 performance on SWE-bench Verified', 'ranks Top1 among open-source frameworks'; arXiv 2508.02085; accepted NeurIPS 2025 (2025-09-19)

name: Augment SWE-bench Verified Agent
one_line: Small Claude-driven bash/file-edit/sequential-thinking agent plus SWE-bench Docker harness with a majority-vote ensembler (OpenAI o1) selecting among multiple candidate patches; repo description calls it 'The #1 open-source SWE-bench Verified implementation'.
why_relevant: (3) Candidate ensembling by an independent vote is a cheap non-self-graded selection step usable in the owner's fix lane; also a clean minimal scaffold to compare against. Adjacent rather than core.
claimed_results: README: '65.4% success rate on our first-ever SWE-bench submission' using Claude Sonnet 3.7 as driver and o1 as ensembler (repo created 2025-03-28)

name: The Fable Method
one_line: Claude Code plugin distilling a workflow (classify the ask, define done with a named verification, gather evidence in parallel, change the smallest correct thing, verify by observation, report outcome first) into four skills (think/act/prove/grow), with an adversarial eval where blind LLM judges verify by diffing and executing, never by reading reports.
why_relevant: (3) A judge seat that executes rather than reads reports, with planted-fraud fixtures as negative controls for the judge itself; (2) evidence that forced artifacts beat prose rules (INTENT line: v1 0/4 -> v3 4/4). Every claim links to committed transcripts.
claimed_results: README Results (2026-07, 15 eval rounds, >260 agent runs): Haiku surfacing a spec-vs-test conflict '0 of 4' -> '4 of 4' (round 3); Haiku catching planted frauds in a lying work-complete report '4 and 3 of 5' -> '5 of 5, both runs' (round 8); Sonnet 'ties or out-ranks' a bare frontier model on 3 of 4 (rounds 4-5); 'Ordinary small tasks on capable models: fine / fine (no lift)'

name: Kapso (Leeroo)
one_line: 'Self-improving AI software factory for measurable objectives': runs experiment campaigns through Claude Code and Codex CLIs (no direct-API fallback) with tree search over candidates scored by a metric; learn() mines finished campaigns into evidence-priced knowledge cards and learn_knowledge() ingests repos/papers into a knowledge graph reused by later campaigns.
why_relevant: (2) Evidence-priced lessons from the system's own campaigns injected into later runs, on subscription CLIs. (4) Strong public results, but the objective must be a scalar score, so it maps to the owner's system only where heldOutPass can serve as the metric.
claimed_results: README (2026): IOAI2 2026 AI Model Track 'Outscored all 471 humans - 536.07 total', 'IOAI2 Grand Master Trophy - top 3 among all AI systems'; RelBench '81.2 vs 79.6 AUROC over 12 tasks' and '0.2476 vs 0.2912 NMAE over 9 tasks'; '#1 on MLE-Bench' among open-source systems; '#1 on ALE-Bench'; technical report arXiv 2601.21526

name: karpathy/autoresearch
one_line: An agent edits a single file (train.py), trains for a fixed 5-minute budget, checks val_bpb, keeps or discards, and repeats overnight; the human edits only program.md, 'the research org code'.
why_relevant: (2) The minimal keep/discard loop with a fixed budget and one frozen metric that the owner's offline self-repair tier should copy: the human tunes the program, not the code. Massively replicated (pi-autoresearch 7,965 stars, codex-autoresearch, autokernel, darwin-skill), which is the adoption evidence.

name: Boundary-Bench
one_line: Runs Claude Code, Codex and Grok Build on Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks inside Daytona sandboxes hardened to NIST-derived policy levels and measures how much capability an agent loses as the environment is restricted; Inspect AI task with official Harbor verification.
why_relevant: (3)+(4) Quantifies what sealed sandboxes like the owner's --network=none gate and permission rules cost in builder capability, with a vendor-independent leaderboard; useful for sizing per-seat budgets under restriction.
claimed_results: README leaderboard, strictest level (High-NIST), Aug 2026, Terminal-Bench 2.1, 89 tasks x 3 trials: Grok Build (Grok 4.5) 74.9% +/-1.4 at $123.5; Codex (GPT-5.6 Sol) 74.2% +/-2.4 at $58.9; Claude Code (Fable 5) 67.8% +/-1.4 at $375.3; arXiv 2608.02670

name: AIDev (The Rise of AI Teammates in SE 3.0)
one_line: Dataset and replication package tracking PRs authored by OpenAI Codex, Devin, GitHub Copilot, Cursor and Claude Code across GitHub, with merge-rate and turnaround analyses; the MSR 2026 Mining Challenge dataset (HuggingFace hao-li/AIDev).
why_relevant: (4) The production-adoption evidence base for unattended agent PRs and the trust gap the owner's held-out verification is meant to close; complements logic-star-ai/insights (live tracker of agent PRs since 2025-05-15).
claimed_results: README overview table (refreshed to 2025-08-01): 932,791 PRs across 116,211 repos (Codex 814,522; Copilot 50,447; Cursor 32,941; Devin 29,744; Claude Code 5,137). arXiv 2507.15003 abstract (2025-07-20): over 456,000 PRs, 61,000 repos, 47,000 developers; agents 'often outperform humans in speed, their PRs are accepted less frequently'

name: TDDev (Automatically Generating Web Applications from Requirements via Multi-Agent Test-Driven Development)
one_line: Three-agent pipeline (test-generation agent derives executable tests from the NL requirement, development agent builds full-stack app, testing agent simulates user interactions) that iterates until all derived tests pass; evaluated on a WebGen-Bench derivative.
why_relevant: (1) ticket-in -> web app out with cooperating agents; (3) tests are authored from the requirement BEFORE code by a separate agent and executed by a separate testing agent that drives the UI -- this is the closest published analogue to the spec-seat -> builder -> Playwright gate design. Test derivation uses requirement decomposition -> elaboration (JSON specs incl. DB schema) -> 'soap opera' persona test cases.
claimed_results: arXiv 2509.25297 v1 2025-09-29, v2 2025-10-01: '14.4% improvement on overall accuracy compared to state-of-the-art baselines'; Table 6 on Req-to-App-MM (101 instructions): TDDev+GPT-4.1 accuracy 78.2 / appearance 4.0 / fail-to-start 0.0; TDDev+Claude-4-Sonnet accuracy 70.2 / appearance 3.7.
last_activity: repo has 13 stars, 8 commits, real code present (bolt.diy + client dirs); commit date not shown on page; paper v2 2025-10-01

name: WebGen-Agent / WebGen-Bench
one_line: Website-generation agent that gets two independent feedback signals per step: a VLM screenshot score and a GUI-agent that executes checks derived from the original spec, with backtracking/selection; plus a benchmark of 101 website instructions with 647 test cases.
why_relevant: (3) verification is not self-graded: an LLM turns the original spec into GUI-agent test instructions (one-shot prompt), a separate GUI agent executes them and a scoring model grades the trajectory 1-5; (1) ticket-in website out. WebGen-Bench is the de-facto benchmark for 'build me this website' and is reused by TDDev -- a candidate target for the console's own heldOutPass metric.
claimed_results: arXiv 2509.22644 (2025-09-26): 'increases the accuracy of Claude-3.5-Sonnet from 26.4% to 51.9% and its appearance score from 3.0 to 3.9'; Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct 38.9% -> 45.4%, appearance 3.4 -> 3.7 via Step-GRPO; WebGen-Bench: 101 instructions, 647 test cases; WebGen-Instruct 6,667 training instructions.
last_activity: repo 24 stars, 9 commits, date not shown; paper 2025-09-26

name: TDFlow: Agentic Workflows for Test Driven Development
one_line: Four sub-agent workflow (patch proposer, debugger, patch reviser, optional test generator) that treats SWE as a test-resolution task; quantifies the gap between human-written and LLM-written tests and manually audits every run for test hacking.
why_relevant: (3)+(4): hard numbers on why held-out human/spec tests beat builder-written tests (94.3% vs 68.0%) and on how often agents game tests (7 of 800 runs, found by 3 human reviewers with a rubric: modified/disabled tests, weakened assertions, altered data, env manipulation, hardcoded outputs). The rubric is directly reusable for the falseFinish audit.
claimed_results: arXiv 2510.23761 v1 2025-10-27, v2 2026-01-22, EACL 2026: '88.8% pass rate on SWE-Bench Lite (an absolute improvement of 27.8% over the next best system)'; '94.3% on SWE-Bench Verified' with human-written tests at $1.01/issue vs 68.0% at $4.12/issue with LLM-generated tests; 93.3% when generated tests have 0 Bad Test Rate; 'only 7 instances of test hacking' across 800 runs (4 Lite, 3 Verified), counted as failures.
last_activity: paper v2 2026-01-22; no code URL found on arXiv page

name: CoHarden (Beyond Fail-to-Pass: Iterative Hardening of Co-Generated Bug Reproduction Tests and Fixes)
one_line: Alternates between mutation-hardening a generated test against surviving incorrect patches and refining the fix, so the in-loop fail-to-pass check stops accepting 'lax' patches.
why_relevant: (3) this is the adversarial-audit seat mechanised: tests are hardened against mutants before they are trusted as a gate. Directly adoptable for the spec-suite audit step before freeze/seal.
claimed_results: arXiv 2607.19843 (2026-07-22): '69.4% Resolved' and '78.9% F->P' on SWE-bench Verified; '+9.6 percentage points' over fix-only baselines in Resolved; '+7.9 percentage points' over cogeneration baselines.
last_activity: paper 2026-07-22; no code URL in abstract

name: SWE-Mutation: Can LLMs Generate Reliable Test Suites?
one_line: Benchmark that measures whether LLM-written test suites catch systematically mutated (including agent-generated) wrong solutions across 9 languages.
why_relevant: (3)+(4): quantifies how weak LLM-authored suites are as a gate -- exactly the risk in a spec seat that writes the held-out Playwright suite from the ticket alone. Agentic mutants are much harder to catch than classical ones.
claimed_results: arXiv 2605.22175 (2026-05-21), ACL 2026 Findings: 2,636 mutated variants from 800 instances; 'even DeepSeek-V3.1 achieves only 10.20% verification and 36.15% detection rates'; agentic mutation reduces detection from 71.04% to 39.81% vs conventional mutation.
last_activity: paper 2026-05-21; no code URL in abstract

name: Rethinking the Value of Agent-Generated Tests for LLM-Based SWE Agents
one_line: Empirical study of six models on SWE-bench Verified showing builder-written tests are mostly observational (print statements, not assertions) and changing test-writing frequency does not change outcomes.
why_relevant: (3)+(4): evidence that a builder's own tests are not a verification signal, supporting the decision to hold out an independently authored suite rather than trust builder-side testing.
claimed_results: arXiv 2602.07900 v1 2026-02-08, v2 2026-04-09: 'resolved and unresolved tasks within the same model exhibit similar test-writing frequencies'; 'value-revealing print statements appearing much more often than assertion-based checks'; prompt interventions on four models 'produced no significant impact on final results'.

name: Agentic Rubrics as Contextual Verifiers for SWE Agents
one_line: A separate expert agent explores the repo and writes a context-grounded rubric checklist; candidate patches are scored against it without executing tests.
why_relevant: (3): an independent critic that is grounded in the repo rather than the builder's trajectory -- a pattern for the judge / human-factors adversary seats when tests cannot run. Caveat: rubric self-preference bias was covered in the earlier round.
claimed_results: arXiv 2601.04171 (2026-01-07): Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B 54.2% and Qwen3-32B 40.6% on SWE-Bench Verified; 'at least +3.5 percentage-point improvement over baseline methods'.

name: RepoZero (with ACE: Agentic Code-Test Evolution)
one_line: Repository-from-scratch benchmark verified by strict black-box output equivalence against the original implementation in a sandbox, with cross-language constraints to block shortcuts.
why_relevant: (3)+(4): non-self-graded verification of whole-repo generation via output equivalence in a sealed sandbox; the proposed ACE loop (iterative test generation + error-driven refinement) mirrors spec->build->fix. Shows even top agents only reach 30-55%.
claimed_results: arXiv 2605.07122 v1 2026-05-08, v3 2026-05-20: 'Even the strongest LLM agents achieve only limited pass rates (30% - 55%)'.
last_activity: paper v3 2026-05-20; no code URL in abstract

name: SWE-Exp: Experience-Driven Software Issue Resolution
one_line: Multi-faceted experience bank distilled from both successful and failed trajectories, retrieved and injected into prompts so the agent stops re-exploring failed paths.
why_relevant: (2): a learning corpus of failure->repair pairs injected into prompts with no fine-tuning -- the same design as the console's self-maintaining tier. Code is public.
claimed_results: arXiv 2507.23361 v1 2025-07-31, v2 2026-02-02: '73.0% Pass@1 resolution rate' on SWE-Bench Verified with Claude 4 Sonnet.
last_activity: repo 45 stars, 28 commits, last commit 2025-10-17 ('Delete supplementary.pdf') -- research artifact, not maintained

name: ReasoningBank
one_line: Memory of generalisable reasoning strategies distilled from self-judged successes AND failures, plus memory-aware test-time scaling (MaTTS); implemented for SWE-Bench and WebArena.
why_relevant: (2) run-to-run self-improvement without fine-tuning; explicit warning for the owner: success/failure labels are self-judged (LLM-as-judge), so it inherits the self-grading problem unless the label comes from a held-out gate.
claimed_results: arXiv 2509.25140 v1 2025-09-29, v2 2026-03-16, ICLR 2026: abstract states 'ReasoningBank consistently outperforms existing memory mechanisms' (no numbers in abstract/README I opened).
last_activity: repo 554 stars, 6 commits, last commit 2026-05-19 ('Update BibTeX'); Apache-2.0; not an official Google product

name: STAIR: Reusing Past Repairs Through Hierarchical Trajectory Abstraction
one_line: Converts past repair trajectories into multi-level plan trees and injects tailored plans into prompts; raw trajectories transfer much worse than abstracted ones.
why_relevant: (2): concrete finding for the exemplar corpus -- abstract the failure->repair pairs into hierarchical plans rather than pasting raw transcripts; works as a drop-in on mini-SWE-agent without code changes.
claimed_results: arXiv 2607.29658 (2026-07-31): '81.2% Pass@1' on SWE-bench Verified (MiniMax M2.5 + Lingxi), '79.2%' with GPT-5; mini-SWE-agent v2 '75.8% -> 81.0%' without code modifications.

name: Agent KB: Leveraging Cross-Domain Experience for Agentic Problem Solving
one_line: Shared knowledge base with two-stage retrieval (planning seeds workflows; feedback applies diagnostic fixes) and a 'disagreement gate' to stop bad transfer across frameworks.
why_relevant: (2): the disagreement gate is a mechanism against corpus-induced drift; shows measurable gains on OpenHands without training.
claimed_results: arXiv 2507.06229 v1 2025-07-08, v5 2025-10-27: OpenHands on SWE-bench '24.3% -> 28.3% at pass@1'; smolagents '55.2% -> 73.9% at pass@3'.
last_activity: paper v5 2025-10-27; no code URL on page

name: Confucius Code Agent (CCA)
one_line: Meta-agent that builds, regression-tests and refines agent scaffolds (build-test-improve), plus persistent 'hindsight notes' of failures/stack traces reused across sessions.
why_relevant: (2): the meta-agent loop over a fixed regression suite is the offline self-diagnosis/repair tier for the pipeline's own code; hindsight notes are a learning corpus keyed on failure signatures.
claimed_results: arXiv 2512.10398 v1 2025-12-11, v6 2026-02-03: SWE-Bench-Pro Resolve@1 GPT-5.2+CCA '59.0%' vs OpenAI 56.0%; Claude 4.5 Sonnet CCA 52.7% vs Live-SWE-Agent 45.8%. README (updated 2026-05-21): 'SWE-bench-pro score: 71%'.

name: EvoDev: Iterative Feature-Driven Multi-Agent End-to-End Software Development
one_line: Decomposes a requirement into a Feature Map (dependency DAG of user-valued features) and propagates business/design/implementation context along it, instead of a waterfall PRD->code pipeline.
why_relevant: (1): ticket-in whole-app-out with cooperating agents; direct comparison against Claude Code on the same tasks.
claimed_results: arXiv 2511.02399 v1 2025-11-04, v3 2026-06-05, ISSTA 2026: 'outperforms Claude Code by 57.3%'; 'improves single-agent performance by 16.0%-58.5%' across base LLMs on Android development tasks.

name: CLARITI (Asking What Matters: Reward-Driven Clarification for SE Tasks)
one_line: Defines effective clarifying questions by two properties -- task relevance (predicts success) and user answerability -- and trains an 8B question module that matches GPT-5 with fewer questions.
why_relevant: (1): the plan seat's clarifying-question step; the two selection criteria are adoptable as a prompt rubric even though the paper's module is RL-trained.
claimed_results: arXiv 2604.14624 (2026-04-16): 'matches GPT-5's resolution rate on underspecified issues while generating 41% fewer questions'.

name: zeroshot
one_line: 'Independent executor-verifier orchestration for software changes': conductor classifies the task, executor implements in isolation, validators with no access to the executor's session must reproduce reported failures; validator count scales with task tier.
why_relevant: (3): design principle stated verbatim -- 'The agent that wrote the code shouldn't be the one that says it works'; validators 'do not share the executor's session or reasoning context' and 'must reproduce reported failures'. Tiering (TRIVIAL: no verifier; SIMPLE/STANDARD: 1-2 validators; CRITICAL: meta-coordinator + 4 validators staged) is a per-seat budget policy.
claimed_results: none stated

name: Ralph for Claude Code
one_line: Autonomous Claude Code loop with dual-condition exit, circuit breaker and rate/token budgets; inspired by Geoffrey Huntley's Ralph technique.
why_relevant: (1) unattended long-running loop on subscription Claude Code; anti-loop mechanics to copy: exit requires 'completion_indicators >= 2' AND 'EXIT_SIGNAL: true'; circuit breaker opens after 3 loops with no progress or 5 loops with repeated errors, half-open recovery, 30-min cooldown; 100 calls/hour; detects the 5-hour usage limit. Caveat: completion is self-declared -- the falseFinish risk the console is built to catch.
claimed_results: README: '784 comprehensive tests across 34 test files with a 100% pass rate' (about its own test suite, not task outcomes).

name: LoopTroop
one_line: LLM Council (several independent models draft plans, score each other on a weighted rubric, vote) produces atomic 'beads' with acceptance criteria that run in isolated git worktrees; failed beads reset the worktree and restart with fresh context plus a compact error note.
why_relevant: (1)+(3): multi-model council for planning; bead success is test-driven ('all tests pass or retry limits are reached'); the reset-worktree + discard-contaminated-session + carry-forward-note retry is a concrete fix-seat pattern; designed for 10+ hour unattended runs with human approval only at critical transitions.
claimed_results: README: context performance 'can drop severely when reaching just 40% of the maximum context window'; retries 'can take hours (sometimes 10+ hours) by design'; self-described 'early alpha'.
last_activity: 129 stars, 10 forks, MIT, 1,300 commits, last commit 2026-09-01

name: Claude Code Harness
one_line: Plan -> Work -> Review harness where review runs separately from implementation and major findings block completion; optional Critic on a different model; non-overridable runtime floor plus configurable guardrails.
why_relevant: (3) reviewer separated from implementer, Critic on a different model family (Codex 'gpt-5.6-sol' vs workers 'gpt-5.6-luna'); risky operations collected at plan time and approved once; runtime floor of 5 denial categories (billing, network egress, secrets, prod deploys, worktree destruction) and guardrails R01-R15 -- a permission model for sealed seats.
claimed_results: README cites CooperBench: 'two agents editing the same file succeed about half as often as one agent working alone, and 63% of the failures trace to a false belief about what the other one changed'.

name: gstack (Garry Tan)
one_line: 23 Claude Code role-skills (Office Hours, CEO/Eng/Design review, QA, Ship, Land-and-Deploy, Canary, Learn, CSO, Codex second opinion) covering ideation to production.
why_relevant: (3) /qa 'opens real browser, clicks through flows' and 'auto-generates regression tests for every fix'; /ship runs tests and audits coverage; /land-and-deploy waits for CI and 'verifies production health'. (2) /learn persistent per-project memory; taste profile 'Decays 5%/week'; per-site domain skills 'Quarantined -> active after 3 successful uses' -- a quarantine rule for corpus entries. Adoption is enormous but it is single-user, interactive and self-reviewed.
claimed_results: README (2026): 'my 2026 run rate is ~810x my 2013 pace' (11,417 vs 14 logical lines/day); 'Year-to-date (through April 18), 2026 has already produced 240x the entire 2013 year'; last 60 days '3 production services, 40+ shipped features'.

name: Agentic Context Engine (kayba-ai) -- ACE implementation
one_line: Open implementation of the ACE paper: Agent / Reflector / SkillManager curate a Skillbook from execution traces; 'Recursive Reflector' runs sandboxed Python over traces to mine patterns.
why_relevant: (2) system built ON ACE + Dynamic Cheatsheet (both covered papers) with Claude Code numbers; shows a practical no-fine-tuning learning loop and its cost. Labels still come from the model's own reflection unless an external reward is wired in.
claimed_results: README: Tau2 with Claude Haiku 4.5 'doubles pass consistency at pass^4 with 15 learned strategies'; Claude Code translation '~14,000 lines' to TypeScript, 'zero build errors, all tests passing', learning cost '~$1.50'; '49% token reduction' on browser automation over 10 runs.

name: Claudexor
one_line: Multi-harness control plane (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode) with best-of-N races, independent reviewers, arbitration, and typed 'evidence' for every cost/quota claim.
why_relevant: (3) best-of-N candidates judged by reviewers from 'at least two distinct observed provider families' with a 'clean verified review/apply gate'; quota-aware rotation across multiple Claude/Codex subscriptions is directly relevant to a subscription-only seat model; 'unknown cost is never $0'.
claimed_results: none stated

name: Hivemoot
one_line: GitHub-native agent team: roles propose/discuss/vote on issues, up to 3 competing PRs per issue, 'CI green, reviews pass -> auto-merged. Breaks main -> auto-revert'; agents run in Docker.
why_relevant: (1)+(3): unattended multi-agent shipping with a CI-gated merge and automatic revert on main breakage; competing PRs is a cheap best-of-N. One live demo project (Colony) run 'completely independently'.
claimed_results: config defaults only: 'maxPRsPerIssue: 3', 24h discussion / 24h voting

name: Greywall
one_line: Deny-by-default sandbox for coding agents without containers: bubblewrap/Landlock/seccomp/eBPF on Linux, Seatbelt profiles on macOS, all traffic through a transparent proxy (greyproxy) with a live dashboard and learning mode.
why_relevant: (3) sealed builder environment on macOS (the console's platform) with network control the Docker --network=none gate currently provides only at gate time; project memory notes the current builder sandbox does not block egress.
claimed_results: none stated
last_activity: 289 stars, 33 forks; commit date not shown on page

name: MetaGPT / MGX
one_line: 'Given one line Requirement, return PRD, Design, Tasks, Repo' via Product Manager / Architect / Project Manager / Engineer roles ('Code = SOP(Team)'); commercial MGX launched 2025-02-19.
why_relevant: (1) the canonical requirement-in repo-out multi-agent SOP pipeline; useful as the waterfall baseline EvoDev argues against. No verification beyond role review; no learning loop.
claimed_results: README news: MGX '#1 Product of the Day' ProductHunt 2025-03-04, '#1 Product of the Week' 2025-03-10; AFlow ICLR 2025 oral 'top 1.8%'. No task-success numbers on README.
last_activity: 70,160 stars, 8,921 forks; last push 2026-01-21 (7 months ago -- slowing, not dead)

name: L2MAC (LLM Automatic Computer)
one_line: Stored-program-computer framing for generating large codebases with unbounded output length (ICLR 2024).
why_relevant: (1) early whole-codebase-from-spec system listed in e2b awesome-ai-agents; included only to flag it as dead.
claimed_results: none opened (paper arXiv 2310.02003, Jan 2024 on list)

name: OpenHands (formerly OpenDevin) + OpenHands Cloud GitHub integration
one_line: Open-source coding-agent platform; README now fronts 'Agent Canvas', a self-hosted control center that runs OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini or any ACP agent; the Cloud GitHub app turns labelled issues into PRs.
why_relevant: Q1: unattended issue->PR path: label `openhands` or comment '@openhands' -> agent works -> 'Open a pull request if it determines that the issue has been successfully resolved' (docs.openhands.dev cloud/github-installation). Docs specify no test/CI step, i.e. success is agent-determined (self-graded) in the product path. Q3: the leaderboard result came from a separately trained critic doing best-of-N selection, not from the builder grading itself. Q4: most-cited open-source system, with a dogfooding claim.
claimed_results: SWE-bench Verified '60.6%' single trajectory, '66.4% with five attempts' using critic (openhands.dev blog, Apr 17 2025); recorded as 65.8% ('best@4' per John Yang) in SWE-bench/experiments PR #209, merged May 11 2025. 'Around 20% of commits to the OpenHands codebase are authored or co-authored by OpenHands agents' (openhands.dev blog 'AI Coding Benchmarks Explained', Jun 25 2026). 85,920 stars (GitHub API, 2026-09-02). No production/customer numbers published; secondary sites cite $18.8M Series A.

name: OpenHands Software Agent SDK (agent-sdk, Agent Server, experimental Critic)
one_line: Python/TypeScript SDK behind OpenHands V1: agent loop, tools, local or remote Docker/Kubernetes sandboxed workspaces via Agent Server, and an experimental API-based Critic that scores a trajectory 0-1 and triggers retries below threshold.
why_relevant: Q3: Critic gives 'Probability scores between 0.0 and 1.0 indicating predicted success', computed 'during agent execution, not just at completion'; defaults `success_threshold` 0.6, `max_iterations` 3 (docs.openhands.dev/sdk/guides/critic, marked 'highly experimental'). That is an independent scorer gating a fix loop, though the critic model is hosted by OpenHands and undisclosed. Q1: README describes 'multiple coordinated agents performing system refactors'; remote ephemeral sandboxes mirror our sealed Docker gate.
claimed_results: README badge 'SWEBench-77.6' links to a Google Sheet (no date, unverified). Tech report arXiv 2511.03690 (Nov 5 2025, rev Apr 22 2026) abstract states only 'strong agent performance'. README adopter list: 'TikTok, VMware, Roche, Amazon, C3 AI, Netflix, Mastercard, Red Hat, MongoDB, Apple, NVIDIA, and Google' (no numbers). 1.0k stars.

name: A Rubric-Supervised Critic from Sparse Real-World Outcomes (OpenHands critic v2)
one_line: OpenHands' second-generation critic: 24 behavioural rubric features extracted from interaction traces plus sparse human feedback, trained semi-supervised, used for best-of-N reranking, early stopping and training-data curation (SDK example 34_critic_example.py).
why_relevant: Q2: learns from the system's own noisy, delayed, sparse real-world outcomes with no unit-test reward, a template for our failure->repair corpus. Q3: a critic separate from the builder. The early-stopping result is a direct analogue of our per-seat budget / anti-loop. Predecessor critic (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B, TD objective on SWE-Gym trajectories, Apr 17 2025) is on Hugging Face under MIT.
claimed_results: 'best-of-8 reranking achieved +15.9 improvement on SWE-bench over random selection'; 'early stopping enabled +17.7 gain with 83% fewer attempts' (arXiv abstract, submitted Mar 4 2026; Wang, Chen, Ji, Neubig). Predecessor: 60.6% -> 66.4% best-of-5 on SWE-bench Verified (HF model card openhands-critic-32b-exp-20250417, Apr 17 2025); independently re-scored to 65.8% by SWE-bench maintainers (PR #209, May 11 2025).
last_activity: paper Mar 4 2026; SDK critic docs current

name: SWE-agent
one_line: Princeton/Stanford single-agent issue fixer built around an Agent-Computer Interface (NeurIPS 2024); development effort has moved to mini-swe-agent; v1.1.0 added SWE-smith training trajectories.
why_relevant: Q1 baseline for issue->patch; Q4: the ACI finding (tool-interface design moves the score) is a copyable mechanism. No built-in independent verification: patches are only evaluated by the external SWE-bench harness. Owner asked about a 'SWE-agent GitHub action': none exists in the SWE-agent org (see dead_ends).
claimed_results: README: '65% on SWE-bench verified in 100 lines of python' (mini-swe-agent, Jul 2025); v1.1.0 release notes: 'SWE-agent-LM-32b achieves open-weights SotA on SWE-bench verified' (May 22 2025); main paper arXiv 2405.15793. 20,190 stars (GitHub API, 2026-09-02).

name: mini-swe-agent
one_line: ~100-line bash-only agent with a completely linear history; each action runs via subprocess.run as an independent process (no stateful shell); environments: Local, Docker/Podman, Singularity/Apptainer, Bubblewrap, Modal; has a cost_limit.
why_relevant: Q4: scaffold simplicity does not cost accuracy versus full SWE-agent. Q3-adjacent: stateless per-step execution plus cost_limit is a clean per-seat budget mechanism; recommended by its authors as the scaffold when 'doing FT or RL' so results do not overfit a harness.
claimed_results: 'Scores >74% on the SWE-bench verified benchmark' (README, undated); 'Nov 19 [2025]: Gemini 3 Pro reaches 74% on SWE-bench verified with mini-swe-agent!' (mini-swe-agent.com news). 6.9k stars.

name: Agentless
one_line: Three-phase non-agent pipeline: hierarchical localisation (files -> classes/functions) -> sample multiple candidate patches -> validation by selected regression tests plus LLM-generated reproduction tests -> rerank.
why_relevant: Q3: verification is separated from generation: a generated reproduction test must flip and selected regression tests must hold before a patch is chosen. This is the closest published analogue to our spec seat writing tests from the ticket alone. Q4: independently adopted as the evaluation scaffold in OpenAI's o1 system card.
claimed_results: '82 fixes (27.3%)' on SWE-bench Lite at '$0.34 per issue'; '40.7% and 50.8% solve rate on SWE-bench lite and verified' with Claude 3.5 Sonnet (README, v1.5.0 Oct 28 2024). OpenAI o1 System Card (arXiv 2412.16720, Dec 2024): Agentless used as scaffold, 'o1-preview ... 41.3%' on SWE-bench Verified. 2,108 stars.

name: AutoCodeRover (now Sonar)
one_line: NUS program-structure-aware repair agent: AST-based code-search APIs for context retrieval, patch generation, spectrum-based fault localisation from failing tests, regression testing beyond FAIL_TO_PASS (ISSTA 2024); acquired by Sonar Feb 19 2025 and now the engine of the SonarQube Remediation Agent (beta).
why_relevant: Q3: uses SBFL from failing tests and runs regression suites as part of repair. Q4: commercial validation via acquisition; Sonar publishes a user-rating figure for the resulting AI CodeFix feature.
claimed_results: '46.20% efficacy on SWE-bench Verified', '37.3% tasks (pass@1) in SWE-bench lite', '24.89% on full SWE-bench', 'each task costs less than $0.7' (README). Sonar press release Feb 19 2025 (no SWE numbers). Sonar 2025 year-in-review: '70% rating the quality of fixes as a 4 or 5 out of 5' for AI CodeFix (search snippet, sonarsource.com). 3,101 stars.

name: Trae Agent (ByteDance) with test-time scaling
one_line: Coder agents (Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, GPT-4.1; high-temperature multi-run, round-robin 'Mixture') -> pruning (patch normalisation/dedup + a tester agent that retrieves and executes the repo's regression tests) -> a selector agent that builds static understanding from code and dynamic understanding from auto-generated test traces, with majority vote across N selector runs.
why_relevant: Q1: explicit multi-agent roles (coder / tester / selector). Q3: candidate patches are filtered by executed regression tests and judged by a separate selector, not the coder; ablations quantify what each verification stage buys.
claimed_results: '75.20%' pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified, '10.22%' average improvement over baselines (arXiv 2507.23370, Jul 31 2025). Ablation avg pass@1: full Trae Agent 65.84% vs without pruning 59.95%, without deduplication 61.07%, without regression testing 60.53%, without selector agent 61.05%, without majority voting 60.80% (arXiv HTML v1). 12,066 stars.

name: Nemotron-CORTEXA (NVIDIA, ICML 2025)
one_line: Localisation (NV-EmbedCode file retrieval, entity refinement merged across models/temperatures) -> diverse patch generation -> drop invalid/syntax-error patches -> normalise -> filter by regression tests and LLM-generated reproduction tests -> frequency majority vote -> LLM-as-judge only for ties.
why_relevant: Q3: a fully specified verification funnel where executed tests do the filtering and the LLM judge only breaks ties. Q4: per-problem cost reported and compared.
claimed_results: '68.2%' SWE-bench Verified at '$3.28 in LLM inference calls' per problem (research.nvidia.com/labs/adlr/cortexa, Apr 9 2025); file recall '71.95%' vs Agentless '65.55%' vs BM25 '40.67%'; entity accuracy '34.51%' vs Agentless '17.54%'; cheaper than CodeMonkeys ($4.6) and CodeStory ($20). 26 stars.

name: Augment SWE-bench agent
one_line: Claude Sonnet 3.7 driver with bash, file view/edit and sequential-thinking tools; 8 candidate solutions per problem; OpenAI o1 majority-vote ensembler picks one diff.
why_relevant: Q4 negative results that bear directly on our design: 'adding an initial orientation agent run' and 'a final fix regressions agent' did not help; embedding-based retrieval did not help; Sonnet thinking mode 'not effective'; ensembling judged 'too expensive to use in real-world settings'.
claimed_results: '65.4% success rate' on SWE-bench Verified (augmentcode.com blog, Mar 31 2025, updated Jun 18 2026); '8 candidate solutions to generate for each example' (README). 882 stars.

name: Refact.ai Agent (refact-bench open pipeline)
one_line: Single agent with an enforced four-step protocol (explore -> reproduce with a script -> strategic_planning() -> fix -> re-run reproduction and the full test suite), a debug_script() sub-agent capped at three calls, and guardrail 'guideposts' injected when the model drifts; pass@1 with no retries.
why_relevant: Q3: mandatory issue reproduction and before/after regression runs inside the loop. Q1/anti-loop: hard caps on sub-agent calls and automated corrective prompts are the same shape as our fingerprint anti-loop and per-seat budgets.
claimed_results: '70.4%' (352/500) SWE-bench Verified (refact.ai blog, May 15 2025); '74.40% tasks resolved' Verified (#2 pass@1, 372/500) and '35.59%' Multimodal (#1, 184/517) with Claude 4 Sonnet (refact.ai blog, Jun 25 2025). refact-bench 60 stars.
last_activity: refact-bench archived 2026-04-30; smallcloudai/refact archived 2026-05-30 (dev moved to JegernOUTT/refact)

name: Kimi-Dev (Moonshot)
one_line: 72B open model trained by large-scale RL where the model 'gains rewards only when the entire test suite passes' in Docker; agentless two-stage (file localisation, code edit) used as a skill prior for later agentic use.
why_relevant: Q4 only: evidence that whole-suite-pass is a usable training reward, but it requires fine-tuning we cannot do; no inference-time verification mechanism to copy.
claimed_results: '60.4% performance on SWE-bench Verified' (README; arXiv 2509.23045, Sep 27 2025); '48.6% pass@1' when used as a SWE-Agent. 1,345 stars.

name: PR-Agent / Qodo Merge (with Qodo PR-history learning)
one_line: Open-source PR review bot (/review, /improve, /describe, /ask); AGENTS.md and SKILL.md fed to review by default since v0.39.0; hosted Qodo layer indexes PR history so findings similar to ones the team fixed are boosted and ones the team dismissed are quieted (Rule Miner, Beta).
why_relevant: Q2: documented learn-from-own-outcomes loop with no fine-tuning: 'If similar issues were usually fixed, Qodo treats the new finding as likely relevant. If similar issues were often dismissed, Qodo indicates that the finding may not require attention' and 'learning from accepted suggestions and pull request comments' (docs.qodo.ai/core-concepts/pr-history). Q3: usable as an independent critic seat over the builder's diff.
claimed_results: none stated (no benchmark or adoption numbers on README, release notes or docs pages opened). 12.8k stars.

name: Tembo (agent orchestration control plane)
one_line: Agent-agnostic control plane that runs 'Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Amp, OpenCode, Pi, and other agents' in isolated cloud environments, triggered from GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket, Linear/Jira, Slack, Sentry/PagerDuty; runs builds, tests and Playwright before the PR.
why_relevant: Q1/Q3: closest commercial shape to our console: ticket in, PR out, with 'Full builds, test suites, Playwright end-to-end tests, security scans' and a 'Feedback Loop [that] turns reviewer feedback into automatic revisions'. Their Mar 4 2026 architecture post lays out the same layers (orchestration, execution sandbox, LLM backbone, context engine, feedback loop, integration).
claimed_results: none stated (homepage and tembo.io/blog/background-coding-agents, Mar 4 2026, give no PR, merge or customer numbers).

name: Charlie Labs (coordination layer for dependable agents)
one_line: Autonomous TypeScript engineer on Linear/GitHub/Slack with a published coordination layer: durable task record, persisted execution state (phase, turn, transcript, pending-tool state), task tree for delegation with scoped child objectives, scheduler as lifecycle authority, mailbox for follow-ups at safe boundaries, operation-specific recovery policies.
why_relevant: Q1: unattended multi-step work with delegation to child tasks and crash recovery (e.g. when unsure whether a PR was created it 'searches by the known branch, finds PR-88, reads it back, and records the artifact'). Q3: treats 'Required CI checks pass' as evidence that 'does not establish semantic correctness by themselves'; 'Higher-impact actions may still require explicit human approval after automated checks pass'. Recap notes feedback loops of 'running tsc, linting, tests' plus browser/visual context and Sentry signals.
claimed_results: 'Charlie built all of Charlie (~90% of PRs)' and Charlie wrote '95% of his own production TypeScript code' since Aug 1 2025 (charlielabs.ai 2025 recap, Jan 3 2026). Coordination-layer post (Jul 6 2026) gives no numbers. No customer counts.

name: Codegen (Linear-native agent with child agents)
one_line: Agent activated when assigned or tagged on a Linear issue; 'can spawn child agents by creating sub-issues and assigning itself to those sub-issues'; parent provides 'scaffolding in the form of a git branch' and children notify the parent on completion.
why_relevant: Q1: a concrete lead-plus-teammates pattern that uses the issue tracker itself as the shared task list, which is what Claude Code agent teams do in-process.
claimed_results: none stated; no CI/test/review step documented; 'only available on the Team Plan'.

name: Linear Agent Interaction SDK and Agent Interaction Guidelines
one_line: Agent sessions are created on assignment or @mention; agents emit thought / action / elicitation / response / error activities over webhooks; AIG principles: clear identity, native platform integration, immediate feedback ('Emit a thought activity within 10 seconds').
why_relevant: Q1: a vendor standard for how an unattended agent reports progress and asks clarifying questions (elicitation), which maps onto our plan seat's dashboard questions and status surfacing. Integrated agents named on Linear docs: Charlie, ChatPRD, Codegen.
claimed_results: none stated; changelog Jul 30 2025; still 'Developer Preview' as of the docs fetched.

name: GitLab Duo Agent Platform (Developer flow, foundational and custom flows)
one_line: 'A flow is a combination of one or more agents working together'; flows run in GitLab CI/CD on your or GitLab-hosted runners; Developer flow (@duo-developer mention or assignment) produces 'a draft merge request from an issue'; 11 foundational flows incl. Fix CI/CD Pipeline, SAST Vulnerability Resolution, Security Review; LLM Claude Sonnet 4.
why_relevant: Q1: multi-agent flows executed on CI runners with the tracker as the UI. Q3: 'the Developer Flow can run tests and verify its own changes before committing' (config-dependent, self-run), and 'the flow never approves a merge request on its own; a person still makes the final call' (InfoQ on 19.2).
claimed_results: GA Jan 15 2026 (GitLab 18.8, press release); Custom Flows GA in 19.2 (Jul 16 2026, InfoQ). No MR or customer counts; InfoQ cites a Forrester study claiming '400% ROI with payback in under six months'.

name: Atlassian Rovo Dev (CLI)
one_line: Jira/Confluence/Bitbucket/Compass-integrated agent and CLI with an 'adaptive memory system' that retains project knowledge and adapts behaviour; MCP extensible.
why_relevant: Q2 (weak): persisted per-project memory claimed to change behaviour across tasks. Q4: the only vendor citing a full-SWE-bench (2,294) number; no verification or review mechanism disclosed.
claimed_results: '41.98% resolve rate across 2,294 tasks in the full dataset' SWE-bench full, #1 (Atlassian blog, Nov 21 2025). No adoption numbers.

name: GitHub Copilot coding agent (Project Padawan)
one_line: Assign an issue -> ephemeral GitHub Actions VM boots, clones, configures -> research/plan/edit, runs 'automated tests and linters' -> draft PR with every step a commit and logs viewable -> tags requester for review; hard 59-minute session limit.
why_relevant: Q3 guardrails worth copying verbatim: 'The agent can only push to branches it created', 'The developer who asks the agent...cannot be the one to approve it', 'GitHub Actions workflows won't run without your approval', internet 'tightly limited to a trusted list' (github.blog, May 19 2025). Verification is builder-run tests only; no independent critic documented.
claimed_results: none stated for merge rates or task counts; 'Maximum session duration: 59 minutes' (docs). Launch post May 19 2025.

name: Google Jules (Critic Agent, Planning Critic, CI auto-fix)
one_line: Async cloud-VM agent with a separate Critic Agent ('an internal peer reviewer, challenging every proposed change'), a Planning Critic that reviews auto-approved plans before execution, web-app rendering to screenshots for self-check, and auto-repair of failing GitHub Actions checks.
why_relevant: Q3: two independent critic seats (code and plan) with a measured effect on failure rate. Q1: unattended issue->PR including a CI-failure repair loop ('When a check fails in GitHub Actions, Jules receives the error, works through a fix, and resubmits the PR', Feb 19 2026). Adjacent to our taste critic: 'verify its work and it'll render the website and send you back a screenshot' (Aug 7 2025).
claimed_results: 'over 140,000 code improvements shared publicly' during beta (blog.google, Aug 6 2025); Planning Critic 'reducing failure rates by 9.5%' (changelog, Jan 26 2026; measurement method not stated); Critic Agent Aug 8 2025; 'Improved Jules Critic' Sep 3 2025.

name: Sentry Seer Autofix
one_line: Error-triggered pipeline: root cause -> fix plan -> code -> automatic PR, gated per project by an 'actionability score'.
why_relevant: Q1 adjacent: production-signal-triggered repair lane (our continuation/repair lane). Q4: rare published downstream PR metrics, including a negative one. No verification step before PR is described.
claimed_results: 'identified root causes with 94.5% accuracy', 'helped fix 38,000+ issues' (changelog, Jun 17 2025; method unspecified); 'About a 21% increase in the action rate on PRs', 'About a 13% increase in the 48-hour response rate', 'About a 12.5% increase in close-without-merge PRs' (blog.sentry.io, Aug 6 2026).

name: Lovable Build mode (formerly Agent mode)
one_line: Autonomous app-builder mode with browser testing, frontend tests, edge-function verification and log/network inspection; iterates on fixes 'until the issue is resolved or clarified'; a Build message can run 'up to 10 hours'.
why_relevant: Q1: same ticket->web-app product shape and similar run lengths. Q3 caveat: verification tools exist but 'most of these tools run only when you ask for them' and are self-run by the builder; no held-out or independent check is documented.
claimed_results: none stated.

name: SWE-ABS: Adversarial Benchmark Strengthening
one_line: Hardens SWE-bench Verified tests via coverage-driven augmentation (program slicing to find untested regions) plus mutation-driven adversarial testing (plausible-but-wrong patches that must be rejected).
why_relevant: Q3 directly: quantifies how often 'held-out tests pass' is a false positive and gives a recipe for our adversarial audit of the spec suite: generate plausible wrong builds and require the suite to reject them before sealing.
claimed_results: 'approximately one in five passing patches from top agents contain semantic errors'; 'rejected 19.71% of previously passing patches'; strengthened '50.2% of instances' (500), '25.1x improvement over prior approaches'; top agent dropped 'from 78.80% to 62.20%' and fell to fifth place (arXiv, Feb 28 2026).

name: UTBoost: Rigorous Evaluation of Coding Agents on SWE-Bench
one_line: UTGenerator writes additional unit tests per task so patches that pass the original PR tests without fixing the issue are caught (ACL 2025).
why_relevant: Q3: shows the official held-out tests were too weak and a second generated test layer reorders the leaderboard; supports having the spec seat over-generate tests and the audit seat prune, rather than trusting one suite.
claimed_results: '36 task instances' with insufficient coverage; '345 erroneous patches ... incorrectly labeled as passed'; affects '40.9% of SWE-Bench Lite and 24.4% of SWE-Bench Verified leaderboard entries'; rank changes '18 ... Lite, 11 ... Verified' (arXiv, Jun 10 2025).

name: Dissecting the SWE-Bench Leaderboards
one_line: Profiles all 147 SWE-bench Lite/Verified entries (80 unique approaches) by submitter type, product availability, LLM usage and architecture (seven groups G1-G7).
why_relevant: Q4: the only systematic map of what actually sits on the leaderboards: single-LLM systems dominate, industry supplies most entries, open-source held parity on Verified in 2025; useful for deciding which architectures have replication depth.
claimed_results: Verified: open-source '38 entries (16 unique solutions)' vs closed '40 entries (22 unique solutions)'; 'Industry: 81 entries (~55%)', academia 36 (~24%); 'most entries from both leaderboards rely on a single LLM, while approximately ten use two' (arXiv, Jun 20 2025, rev Feb 5 2026).

name: From Plan to Action: How Well Do Agents Follow the Plan?
one_line: 21,120 SWE-agent trajectories across four LLMs and eight plan variants (no plan, standard, periodic reminders, subpar, extra early phases) measuring plan compliance and resolution.
why_relevant: Q1: our frozen plan -> builder handoff. Findings: 'Providing the standard plan improves issue resolution'; 'periodic plan reminders can mitigate plan violations'; 'inserting additional task-relevant phases in the early stage can degrade performance', i.e. re-inject the plan during the run and keep early phases lean.
claimed_results: '21,120 trajectories', 4 LLMs, 8 plan variations (arXiv, Apr 13 2026, rev Aug 7 2026); no headline percentage in abstract.

name: SWE-bench/experiments submission verification protocol
one_line: Leaderboard intake requires reasoning traces, per-instance logs with patches and test output, and all_preds.jsonl; maintainers re-run a random subset; `swebench submit verify` regrades every instance from recorded test output and flags disagreements.
why_relevant: Q3/Q4: a working sealed-audit protocol (independent re-execution plus regrade-from-logs) that we can mirror for our held-out gate's audit trail; the Nov 2025 policy change explains why most recent vendor numbers are unverified.
claimed_results: 'As of November 18, 2025, SWE-bench Verified and Multilingual now only accepts submissions from academic teams and research institutions with open source methods and peer-reviewed publications' (README).

name: Anthropic: Harness design for long-running application development
one_line: Planner -> Generator -> Evaluator harness where the evaluator drives the running app via Playwright MCP and generator+evaluator negotiate a 'sprint contract' before code is written.
why_relevant: Closest published analogue to the owner's pipeline (spec seat + builder + sealed gate + taste critic). (3) 'By separating frontend generation from frontend grading, we can create a feedback loop that drives the generator toward stronger outputs'; evaluator 'uses the Playwright MCP to click through the running application the way a user would, testing UI features, API endpoints, and database states'. (1) 'the generator and evaluator negotiated a sprint contract: agreeing on what done looked like for that chunk of work before any code was written' (27 contract requirements for one level editor sprint). (4) Cost/time numbers published, including the 20x cost overhead of the full harness vs a solo run.
claimed_results: Published 2026-03-24: Retro Game Maker solo run $9 / 20 min vs full harness $200 / 6 hours ('over 20x more expensive'); DAW app 3h50m, $124.70; Sprint 3 contract had 27 requirements.

name: Anthropic: Demystifying evals for AI agents
one_line: Grader taxonomy (code-based fail-to-pass/pass-to-pass, model-based rubric, human), 'grade what the agent produced, not the path', and pass@k vs pass^k for consistency.
why_relevant: (3)(4) Direct guidance for the owner's two metrics: code-based 'Binary tests (fail-to-pass, pass-to-pass)' as the primary grader, LLM judges only after calibration ('should be closely calibrated with human experts'). pass^k is the right statistic for an unattended pipeline that must succeed every run: '75% per-trial success rate and you run 3 trials, the probability of passing all three is (0.75)^3 ~ 42%'.
claimed_results: Published 2026-01-09; worked example: 75% per-trial -> 42% pass^3. No system benchmarks.

name: Anthropic: Quantifying infrastructure noise in agentic coding evals
one_line: Measured how much of agentic-coding eval variance is container resource limits/timeouts rather than the model; recommends a 3x resource ceiling and per-task dual specs.
why_relevant: (3) Bears directly on the owner's sealed Docker (--network=none) gate: a held-out failure can be an infra failure. 'the gap between the most- and least-resourced setups on Terminal-Bench 2.0 was 6 percentage points (p < 0.01)'; 'infra error rates dropping monotonically ... from 5.8% at strict enforcement to 0.5% when uncapped'; 'a 3x ceiling over the per-task specs cut infra error rates by roughly two-thirds (5.8% to 2.1%, p < 0.001)'. Implies falseFinish must be split from infra-caused red before it counts against the builder.
claimed_results: Published 2026-02-05: 6pp gap (p<0.01); infra errors 5.8% -> 0.5%; 3x ceiling 5.8% -> 2.1% (p<0.001); 'leaderboard differences below 3 percentage points deserve skepticism'.

name: Claude Code on the web + Routines + Auto-fix PRs
one_line: Anthropic-hosted cloud sessions (isolated VM, restricted network, credentials proxied outside sandbox), routines triggered by schedule/API/GitHub events with no permission prompts, and per-PR auto-fix that reacts to CI failures and review comments.
why_relevant: (1) Unattended ticket-in: routines 'run autonomously as full Claude Code cloud sessions: there is no permission-mode picker and no approval prompts during a run', triggered by cron, POST /fire, or pull_request events; 'claude --cloud' runs parallel independent sessions. (3) Auto-fix loop: 'when a check fails or a reviewer leaves a comment, Claude investigates and pushes a fix if one is clear', asks on ambiguous ones. Sandbox design to copy: 'git credentials and signing keys stay outside the sandbox, and a proxy authenticates on the session's behalf'. Caveat for run-status semantics: 'A green status in the run list means the session started and exited without an infrastructure error. It does not mean the task in your prompt succeeded.' Routines doc: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/routines
claimed_results: none stated. Docs reference v2.1.248 and beta header experimental-cc-routine-2026-04-01; agent teams can be enabled in cloud sessions via CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1.

name: Claude Code ultrareview (/code-review ultra)
one_line: Cloud fleet of reviewer agents over a diff/PR where 'every reported finding is independently reproduced and verified'; runnable headless via `claude ultrareview --json` with exit codes.
why_relevant: (3) An Anthropic-shipped independent-critic design: many parallel reviewers, then a verification pass that reproduces each finding before reporting, explicitly to cut style noise. Non-interactive `claude ultrareview 1234 --json --timeout 30` returns bugs.json and exit 0/1/130, so it can be a seat in the owner's judge stage. Size limits (500 files / 8,000 lines) and 5-10 minute runtime are useful budget lines.
claimed_results: none stated beyond: 'A review typically takes 5 to 10 minutes'; cost 'typically $5 to $25 in usage credits'; 500 changed files / 8,000 changed lines default limit.

name: OpenAI Symphony (Codex orchestrator)
one_line: Spec + Elixir reference impl that polls Linear on a cadence and dispatches Codex workers with bounded concurrency, one persistent workspace per issue, exponential retry backoff, prompt template in WORKFLOW.md.
why_relevant: (1) Ticket-in, PR-out, unattended: 'turns project work into isolated, autonomous implementation runs, allowing teams to manage work instead of supervising coding agents'; 'Engineers do not need to supervise Codex'. One agent per ticket in parallel (default max_concurrent_agents 10), not a cooperating team. (3) Proof is external: 'CI status, PR review feedback, complexity analysis, and walkthrough videos'; success may end at a 'Human Review' handoff state. Architecture choices to copy from SPEC.md: orchestrator state deliberately in-memory, 'Restart recovery is tracker-driven and filesystem-driven'; retry 'delay = min(10000 * 2^(attempt - 1), max_retry_backoff_ms)' capped 300,000 ms; 'agent.max_turns' default 20; 1-second continuation retry after normal exit; WORKFLOW.md hot-editable. (4) No outcome numbers; 'low-key engineering preview'.
claimed_results: none stated (no benchmarks). Repo 27,000 stars, 2,800 forks, 44 commits on main (fetched 2026-09-02). SPEC: https://github.com/openai/symphony/blob/main/SPEC.md

name: OpenAI: Harness engineering (Codex-built internal product)
one_line: Internal product built with '0 lines of manually-written code': AGENTS.md as ~100-line table of contents into docs/, custom linters as taste invariants, Codex reviewing Codex, background 'garbage collection' tasks that open refactor PRs.
why_relevant: (2) A no-fine-tuning self-improvement loop at the repo level: recurring background Codex tasks scan for architectural drift and open PRs (the owner's drift-detection tier). (3) Verification by mechanical guardrails ('custom linters and structural tests', fixed dependency layers Types -> Config -> Repo -> Service -> Runtime -> UI) plus agent review; Codex 'requests additional specific agent reviews both locally and in the cloud' before merge. (4) Real throughput numbers from production use. Note: openai.com returned 403 to WebFetch; content read via r.jina.ai reader proxy of the same URL.
claimed_results: ~5 months from first commit late Aug 2025 (so post ~Feb 2026; exact date not visible in fetch): 'roughly 1,500 pull requests have been opened and merged with a small team of just three engineers' (team grew to 7); 'on the order of a million lines of code'; '3.5 PRs per engineer per day'; '0 lines of manually-written code'.

name: Claude Squad
one_line: TUI that runs N Claude Code/Codex/Gemini/Aider instances, each in its own tmux session and git worktree, with an experimental --autoyes.
why_relevant: (1) One-agent-per-task parallelism, not a cooperating team; unattended only via '--autoyes ... all instances will automatically accept prompts'. (3) Verification is human: 'Review changes before applying them, checkout changes before pushing them.' Useful only as the worktree-isolation baseline.
claimed_results: none stated. 8.4k stars, 619 forks, 222 commits (fetched 2026-09-02).

name: ccswarm
one_line: YAML-declared workflow engine: plan -> Sangha consensus -> implement -> review -> fix, with planner/reviewer/qa/coder agents in git worktrees and NDJSON audit trails.
why_relevant: (1) `ccswarm auto --watch` runs with no y/n prompts, auto-commits and opens PRs. (3) 'Sangha consensus' has multiple agents independently evaluate and only advances on quorum, a cheap independent-critic pattern; NDJSON trails allow replay/diff/rollback of a run (useful for the owner's failure->repair corpus). (2) No cross-run learning. (4) No results.
claimed_results: none stated. 149 stars, 153 commits (fetched 2026-09-02).

name: claude-flow / Ruflo (ruvnet)
one_line: Large 'agent meta-harness' for Claude Code claiming 100+ agents, queen-led swarms with Raft/Byzantine/Gossip consensus, AgentDB+HNSW memory, 'agents learn from every task'.
why_relevant: (1)(2) Claims exactly the owner's targets (self-organising swarms, cross-session learning, autopilot loops) but README provides no task-level outcome evidence; the only measured numbers are vector-search micro-benchmarks. Prior SWE-bench/token-reduction claims are no longer in the README. Treat as a feature-idea list, not evidence.
claimed_results: README (fetched 2026-09-02): 'measured ~1.9x faster at N=20k, ~3.2x-4.7x at N=5k vs brute force (recall@10 ~0.99)'; 'ruflo wins cold start, single turn, RSS by 1.3x-1953x'; '~210 tools'. No SWE-bench, '84.8%', or '32.3% token reduction' strings found in current README. 70.2k stars, 7,402 commits, 603 open issues.
last_activity: release v3.38.20 on 24 Aug (year omitted on page; current year => 2026)

name: Ralph Wiggum loop (Geoffrey Huntley) + official Claude Code plugin
one_line: `while :; do cat PROMPT.md | claude-code; done` with tests/typecheck/compile as 'backpressure'; official plugin re-implements it as a Stop hook with --max-iterations and an exact-string --completion-promise.
why_relevant: (2)(3) The single-agent loop that the owner's fix seat generalises: repeated fresh-context runs against a fixed prompt, where the only thing that stops the loop is external backpressure (tests, static analysis, compilation). Plugin caveat matters for the owner's anti-loop design: '--completion-promise uses exact string matching, so you cannot use it for multiple completion conditions ... Always rely on --max-iterations as your primary safety mechanism.' Merged into anthropics/claude-code as plugins/ralph-wiggum. Plugin: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins/ralph-wiggum
claimed_results: ghuntley.com post dated 2025-07-14 (author-reported): '$50k USD contract' delivered as MVP for '$297'; '6 repositories overnight' at a YC hackathon; CURSED language built over ~3 months. Plugin README repeats the same three claims.
last_activity: post 2025-07-14; plugin added to anthropics/claude-code 2025-11-16, last commit 2026-01-06

name: Beads (bd) - Steve Yegge
one_line: Dolt-backed graph issue tracker for agents: hash IDs (bd-a1b2) to avoid merge collisions, `bd ready` / `bd update --claim` atomic claims, `bd remember` + `bd prime` project memory with 'memory decay'.
why_relevant: (1) Shared task list for multiple agents with atomic claiming ('Atomically claim a task (sets assignee + in_progress)') and dependency graph; v1.3.0-rc.1 adds 'work leases' and 'compare-and-set updates' for multi-agent coordination. (2) Persistent cross-session memory without fine-tuning: `bd remember "insight"` injected by `bd prime`; 'Semantic memory decay summarizes old closed tasks to save context window'. (4) Adoption by stars only; no outcome data.
claimed_results: none stated (no benchmarks). 26.8k stars, 1.8k forks (fetched 2026-09-02).

name: Gas Town - Steve Yegge
one_line: Multi-agent workspace manager: Mayor coordinator, Polecat workers with persistent identity/ephemeral sessions, git-worktree 'hooks' for state, Witness/Deacon/Dogs watchdogs, Refinery Bors-style bisecting merge queue.
why_relevant: (1) Explicitly unattended multi-agent over Beads tickets: 'Instead of losing context when agents restart, Gas Town persists work state in git-backed hooks'. (3) Merge is gated, not self-graded: 'Polecat runs gt done -> branch pushed, MR bead created. Refinery batches pending MRs. Runs verification gates on the merged stack. If green: all MRs in batch merge to main. If red: bisects to isolate the failing MR, merges the good ones.' Agents never push to main. Self-maintenance tier analogue: 'three-tier watchdog' (Witness per-rig, Deacon patrols, Dogs for maintenance), 'GUPP Violation - Hooked work with no progress for an extended period'. (4) No outcome numbers.
claimed_results: none stated. 17.9k stars, 343 open issues, 108 PRs (fetched 2026-09-02). Requires Go 1.26.2+, Beads 0.57.0+.
last_activity: v1.2.1 released 06 Jun (year omitted on page; current year => 2026)

name: Vibe Kanban (BloopAI) - sunset 2026-04-10
one_line: Kanban of issues -> isolated workspace per task (branch, terminal, dev server) -> diff review with inline comments -> PR; 10+ agents supported; company shut down, project now community-maintained.
why_relevant: (1) Ticket->workspace->PR with a human review gate, not unattended. (4) Cautionary market evidence: 'Thousands of software engineers use Vibe Kanban every day' yet 'the vast majority are free users and we couldn't find a business model'. Useful for the owner's dashboard UX (kanban + per-workspace preview browser) but not for verification or learning.
claimed_results: Shutdown post 2026-04-10: 'Thousands of software engineers use Vibe Kanban every day to ship more with coding agents.' 28,000 stars, 3,000 forks (fetched 2026-09-02). Announcement: https://www.vibekanban.com/blog/shutdown

name: oh-my-opencode / oh-my-openagent (code-yeongyu)
one_line: Plugin for OpenCode/Codex CLI: Sisyphus orchestrator delegates to Hephaestus (deep worker), Prometheus (planner interviews), Oracle/Librarian/Explore specialists; `ultrawork` mode; Todo Enforcer; Hashline hash-anchored edits.
why_relevant: (1) Lead+specialists with background parallel agents, driven to completion by a 'Todo Enforcer preventing idle agents'. (3) Hashline validates content hashes before edits ('the harness problem') - a mechanism analogous to the owner's frozen-artifact hashing. (4) Only user anecdotes; no benchmark.
claimed_results: README (fetched 2026-09-02) user quotes: 'Knocked out 8000 eslint warnings ... just in a day'; converted 'a 45K-line app overnight'. 68.6k stars, 5.6k forks, 509 open issues.
last_activity: unknown (active dev branch per README, fetched 2026-09-02)

name: Backlog.md
one_line: Markdown-native task board in-repo with acceptance criteria and a reusable Definition-of-Done checklist per task; agents work one task per context window via CLI or MCP.
why_relevant: (1)(3) Encodes the owner's 'acceptance criteria from the ticket' step as data: 'verifiable scope per task, plus a reusable DoD checklist for every new task', with three human checkpoints (spec review, plan review, code review). One task = one context window is a budget-per-seat rule. Dogfooded: 'nearly all of Backlog.md's own code is written by AI agents working through Backlog.md itself.'
claimed_results: none stated. 6.6k stars, 398 forks, 1,353 commits (fetched 2026-09-02).

name: Agent Orchestrator (ComposioHQ)
one_line: Desktop IDE: task -> isolated git worktree/branch -> one of 26 agents -> PR -> CI/review feedback routed back to the same worker -> merge; project-aware orchestrator plans and delegates.
why_relevant: (1) Ticket->PR with an orchestrator that can 'break it into focused tasks, spawn or redirect workers, pass each worker the relevant context, follow their progress, and coordinate follow-up work'. (3) Feedback loop is CI + PR review, with 'requested changes to the same owner' (claims to 'autonomously handle CI fixes, merge conflicts, and code reviews'). No held-out tests, no learning.
claimed_results: none stated. 10.8k stars, 1.5k forks (fetched 2026-09-02).

name: Cursor cloud agents (background agents)
one_line: Isolated cloud VMs that clone the repo, work on a branch, and push 'merge-ready PRs with artifacts' (screenshots, videos, logs) showing how the agent verified its work.
why_relevant: (1) 'run as many agents as you want in parallel, and they do not require your local machine'. (3) Evidence-of-verification artifacts attached to the PR ('screenshots, videos, and logs so you can see exactly what changed and how the agent verified its work') is a cheap addition to the owner's verdict stage. Docs stress 'Agents are only as capable as the environments they run in.' Long-running not available for multi-repo yet.
claimed_results: none stated (fetched 2026-09-02).

name: GitHub Copilot coding agent
one_line: Assign an issue -> ephemeral GitHub Actions environment -> plan -> branch -> draft PR; can run tests/linters; strictly one branch and one PR per task; 59-minute session cap.
why_relevant: (1) The most widely deployed issue->PR unattended flow; one agent per task, no teammates ('Copilot can only work on one branch at a time and can open exactly one pull request to address each task'). (3) Verification = repo CI + human review; no held-out tests. Budget line to copy: 'maximum execution time of 59 minutes'.
claimed_results: none stated on page; hard limit 59 minutes per session (fetched 2026-09-02).

name: Factory: droid exec + Software Factory
one_line: Headless one-shot runner with tiered autonomy (--auto low/medium/high), fail-fast on over-privilege with non-zero exit and 'no partial changes', JSON/stream-jsonrpc output; Software Factory (private preview) chains triage -> code-gen -> validate -> release -> monitor.
why_relevant: (1) Designed for ticket/CI-driven unattended runs with worktree isolation for parallel jobs. (3) Explicit permission tiers and fail-fast semantics ('stops immediately with a clear error message, returns a non-zero exit code, and performs no partial changes') map onto the owner's per-seat permission rules; Software Factory's 'Validate' stage runs code review, security review, and QA as separate steps. Overview: https://docs.factory.ai/software-factory/overview
claimed_results: none stated; Software Factory 'currently in Private Preview' (fetched 2026-09-02).

name: Cognition: Multi-Agents: What's Actually Working (+ Devin manages Devins, scheduled Devins)
one_line: Devin's position: multi-agent works when 'writes stay single-threaded and the additional agents contribute intelligence rather than actions'; Devin Review with clean context; manager Devin delegates to child Devins in isolated VMs and reads their full trajectories.
why_relevant: (1)(3) Direct architectural answer to the owner's question: keep one writer per workspace, use extra agents as reviewers/planners. 'Devin Review ... catches an average of 2 bugs per PR, of which roughly 58% are severe', attributed to reviewer isolation from 'Context Rot'. Manager-child delegation (2026-03-19): each child 'independently run[s] shell commands, execute[s] tests, and verif[ies] its own changes before reporting back'; coordinator 'can read the full trajectories of its managed Devins'. (2) Scheduled Devins (2026-03-20) 'reads and writes its own notes across sessions' - cross-run memory without training. Context: 'Don't Build Multi-Agents' (2025-06-12) argued 'Share context, and share full agent traces, not just individual messages'. Related: https://cognition.com/blog/devin-can-now-manage-devins , https://cognition.com/blog/devin-can-now-schedule-devins , https://cognition.com/blog/dont-build-multi-agents
claimed_results: 2026-04-22: Devin Review 'catches an average of 2 bugs per PR, of which roughly 58% are severe'; enterprise usage '~8x growth over 6 months' (chart). 2026-03-19: no numeric limits; audit example '10 at a time'.

name: Warp Oz (cloud agent platform)
one_line: Fleet of cloud agents triggered by @warp mentions or events, routing across Claude Code/Codex/Warp agent, with 'persistent memories ... shared across your team's agent fleet' and 'automatic self-improvement' of the outer loop.
why_relevant: (1)(2) Marketing-level description of exactly the owner's targets (event-triggered unattended agents plus a self-improving outer loop) but no mechanism detail and no benchmark; one customer case study. Include for the 'fleet memory' framing only.
claimed_results: Page (fetched 2026-09-02): Rectangle Health's AI teammate 'wrote 35,000 lines of code each week', '54% of its own code' self-generated; headline metrics rendered as placeholders ('0K', '0%'). No dates.

name: Cline
one_line: IDE/CLI agent with 'Multi-Agent Teams' (coordinator delegates subtasks to specialist agents), headless JSON mode for CI, and cron-scheduled agents.
why_relevant: (1) Coordinator->specialists plus headless: 'Run Cline with zero interaction for scripting and automation. Pipe input, get JSON output, chain commands, integrate into CI/CD pipelines' and 'Run agents on cron schedules'. (3)(2) No verification or learning mechanism documented. Adoption evidence only.
claimed_results: none stated. 67.3k stars, 7.3k forks (fetched 2026-09-02).

name: Roo Code Orchestrator (Boomerang) mode
one_line: Orchestrator mode (no file read/write tools) spawns subtasks via new_task with fully isolated context; 'only this summary returns to the parent'; each subtask creation/completion requires approval unless auto-approved.
why_relevant: (1) Cheap mechanism to copy for context hygiene between seats: subtasks 'do not automatically inherit the parent's context', return only an attempt_completion summary, orchestrator deliberately cannot edit files to avoid 'context poisoning'. (3) Verification is human approval per subtask by default.
claimed_results: none stated. Doc last updated 2026-05-15.

name: OpenHands (main app + Cloud GitHub integration)
one_line: 85.9k-star open-source SWE agent platform; issue-labelled-to-PR via Cloud/GitHub app; Agent Server runs multiple agents on one machine; opens a PR only if the agent 'determines that the issue has been successfully resolved'.
why_relevant: (1) ticket-in -> PR-out unattended, Agent Canvas/Agent Server = 'REST API for running multiple agents on a single machine' (same shape as the owner's console). (3) weak: PR-open decision is self-judged by the agent; no held-out test gate in the Cloud docs. (4) leaderboard-checked pass@1 rows. Architecture notes: browsing disabled for benchmark runs; 500 max iterations; temperature 0 single run.
