claimed_results: SWE-bench Verified 'Resolved 352 instances (70.4%)' with claude-sonnet-4-20250514, 1 run, 500 max iterations, pass@1 checklist ticked (SWE-bench/experiments folder 20250524_openhands_claude_4_sonnet, 2025-05-24). Repo README (viewed 2026-09-02): 85.9k stars, 8,132 commits. Cloud docs: opens PR 'if it determines that the issue has been successfully resolved' (docs.openhands.dev, undated).

name: OpenHands Software Agent SDK (V1) + MLSys 2026 paper
one_line: Composable SDK behind OpenHands V1: event-sourced conversations, sandboxed workspaces, LLM SecurityAnalyzer + ConfirmationPolicy, condenser, sub-agents as independent conversations; paper reports production failure-rate data.
why_relevant: (1) sub-agent delegation model: 'Sub-agents operate as independent conversations that inherit the parent's model configuration and workspace context, enabling structured parallelism and isolation'. (3) SecurityAnalyzer rates tool calls low/medium/high/unknown; ConfirmRisky policy. (4) rare documented production numbers for an agent runtime; crash-recovery via event sourcing is a pattern for the owner's 1-12h runs.
claimed_results: arXiv 2511.03690 (v1 2025-11-05, v2 2026-04-22, 'Accepted at MLSys 2026'): 'V1 reduces system-attributable failures by 61% (from 78.0 to 30.0 errors per 1k conversations)' over a 15-day production comparison; Table 5 SWE-bench Verified 76.6% (Claude Opus 4.5) vs published SOTA 79.2%; Commit0 56.2%, SWE-bench Multimodal 44.1%, SWT-Bench 78.8%, GAIA 80.0%; 'LLMSummarizingCondenser ... reduce API costs by up to 2x with no degradation'; per-event persist latency 0.20 ms median, crash recovery 7.4 ms median. Repo README badge 'Benchmark Score 77.6'; 1k stars.

name: OpenHands critic model + inference-time scaling
one_line: Run N independent rollouts, have a separately-trained critic (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B, TD-learning on trajectories, gamma=0.99) score each trajectory and pick the best; critic weights released on HF.
why_relevant: (3) verification by an independent grader rather than the builder's own DONE claim; the selection-over-N-rollouts pattern maps onto the owner's fix-seat/judge. Caveat: their critic is fine-tuned (owner cannot train), but the architecture (critic scores trajectory, not just final diff) is copyable with a prompted critic.
claimed_results: Blog 2025-04-17: baseline '60.6%' SWE-bench Verified, '66.4% with five attempts' + critic selection; 'log-linear performance improvement' with attempts; critic 'publicly available on huggingface'. Corresponding leaderboard folders 20250203_openhands_4x_scaled and 20250415_openhands exist in SWE-bench/experiments.

name: Trae Agent (ByteDance) - generation / pruning / selection
one_line: Multi-agent test-time scaling: N coder agents (multi-LLM) -> dedup -> tester agent builds regression tests -> selector agent with static+dynamic analysis, majority-voted N times.
why_relevant: (1) explicit multi-agent roles (coder/tester/selector). (3) selection is driven by executed regression tests plus an independent selector agent, with ablations showing each gate's contribution - exactly the evidence the owner asked for. (4) top leaderboard row but 'checked: false'.
claimed_results: arXiv 2507.23370 (2025-07-31): 'Pass@1 score of 75.20%' SWE-bench Verified; Table 2 (N=3, Claude 3.7): full 66.40% vs w/o pruning 63.60%, w/o dedup 64.00%, w/o regression 64.60%, w/o selector 64.60%, w/o majority voting 63.60%; dedup 'reduces redundancy by an average of 28.90%'; regression-test selection 'Accuracy of 63.28%, a Precision of 61.20%, a Recall of 93.40%'; selector 'upper bound of 30 interaction rounds'; 'improvement of 5.01%~12.86%' over baselines. Leaderboard metadata 20250612_trae: name 'TRAE + Claude Sonnet 4 + Opus 4 + Sonnet 3.7 + Gemini 2.5 Pro', os_system true, checked false. 12.1k stars.
last_activity: 2026-02-05 (commit 'fix(openai): persist tool outputs in message history (#369)')

name: Refact.ai Agent (open-source; new home JegernOUTT/refact)
one_line: Autonomous agent with pdb debug sub-agent, simulated-user guardrail messages, reproduction-script + existing-test re-runs, and (new repo) subagents-as-tools, self-verify + separate verifier, knowledge graph + vector recall of past trajectories.
why_relevant: Speaks to all four: (1) subagents run as first-class tools with parallel execution; (2) '.refact/' stores 'Project knowledge, trajectories, task memory' with 'graph + vector recall' (petgraph + SQLite vec0) - a no-fine-tune learning corpus; (3) 'Agents self-verify before finishing, then a verifier can re-check the card, capture command results, concerns, and recommendations'; (4) checked-style pass@1 leaderboard row. Guardrails-as-fake-user-messages is a cheap anti-loop trick.
claimed_results: Leaderboard folder 20250603_Refact_Agent_claude-4-sonnet (2025-06-03): '74.4% score, solving 372 out of 500 tasks', pass@1 checklist ticked. Blog 2025-06-25: Verified 74.40%, Multimodal 35.59% (184/517). Blog 2025-05-15: 70.4% (352/500) with Claude 3.7 orchestrator, o3 strategic_planning (one call/task), debug_script sub-agent 'at least once - and up to three times'. Legacy repo smallcloudai/refact 3.5k stars, archived 2026-05-30; new repo 64 stars.
last_activity: 2026-09-02 (commit 'fix(tui): classify the new agent interaction tools')

name: Kimi-Dev (Moonshot) - test-time self-play BugFixer x TestWriter
one_line: Two roles (BugFixer, TestWriter) sample 40 patches x 40 tests; patch score = fraction of generated reproduction tests it passes + fraction of regression tests it passes; test-based selection beats majority vote.
why_relevant: (3) quantifies how much independently generated tests add over self-grading/voting: 3x3 patch-test pairs already beat majority voting over 40 patches. Model is RL-trained (owner cannot replicate training) but the selection formula is model-agnostic and directly adoptable for the owner's spec seat + builder split.
claimed_results: arXiv 2509.23045 (2025-09-27): '60.4% on SWE-bench Verified'; Sec 3.4 'Test-Time Self-Play': 40 patches + 40 tests per instance; Figure 4: 48.0% -> 60.4% from 1x1 to 40x40; '3x3 configurations already surpass majority voting from 40 patches alone'; score S_i = sum FP(i,j)/sum F(j) + sum PP(i,j)/sum P(j). 1.3k stars.

name: Nemotron-CORTEXA (NVIDIA ADLR)
one_line: Embedding-based localization (NV-EmbedCode) -> 7 candidate patches (o3) -> dedup -> filter by generated regression + reproduction tests (tests from 4 different models) -> LLM voting for the survivor.
why_relevant: (3) tests written by different models than the patcher = de-correlated grader, close to the owner's 'spec seat writes tests from the ticket alone'. (4) SWE-bench-verified folder with the number; Apache-2.0 code.
claimed_results: Leaderboard README 20250516_cortexa_o3 (2025-05-16): '68.4%' SWE-bench Verified; '7 patches using the o3 model'; reproduction tests from 'Claude-3.7-Sonnet, GPT-4.1, o3-mini, and o1'; 'LLM voting to select the final patch' with 5-minute timeout fallback to o3-mini. Earlier folder 20250410_cortexa. Repo: 26 stars, 8 commits; paper on OpenReview id k6p8UKRdH7 (blocked by bot check, not read).

name: Augment SWE-bench agent (ensembler + negative results)
one_line: Simple Claude 3.7 agent, 8 candidates, o1 majority-vote ensembler; blog documents what did NOT work, including a separate post-hoc 'fix regressions' agent.
why_relevant: (4)/(3) rare negative evidence: 'Running a separate fix regressions agent after implementation ... introduced bugs into otherwise correct solutions' - a direct warning for the owner's fix-seat loop; ensembling gave +3-8% but 'too expensive to use in real-world settings'; 'Scores ... are largely driven by the quality of the foundation model'.
claimed_results: Blog 2025-03-31: '65.4% success rate on SWE-bench verified', Claude Sonnet 3.7 driver + 'OpenAI's o1 as our ensembler', default '--num-candidate-solutions' 8; ensembling '3-8% improvement'; 'Sonnet 3.7's thinking mode is not effective'; embedding retrieval unnecessary vs grep/find. Leaderboard folders 20250316_augment_agent_v0, 20250610_augment_agent_v1. 882 stars.

name: Qodo PR-Agent + Qodo Command
one_line: Single-LLM-call-per-tool PR reviewer (/review /improve /describe /ask) with PR compression and self-reflection; sibling Qodo Command CLI has a checked SWE-bench Verified row.
why_relevant: (3) an off-the-shelf independent PR critic the owner could run against the builder's output; PR-Agent itself has no benchmark, but Qodo Command's row shows the vendor's agent is real. No cross-task learning documented.
claimed_results: Leaderboard README 20250715_qodo_command (2025-07-15): '71.2% (356 instances)', 'actual result is 71.4%' incl. astropy-7606, checked. PR-Agent README: 'Each tool ... uses a single LLM call (~30 seconds, low cost)'; v0.41.0 released 2026-07-26 (Claude Opus 5 support); 12.8k stars.

name: Learn-by-interact (training-free trajectory synthesis + retrieval)
one_line: Synthesize agent-environment trajectories from documentation, backward-construct instructions from them, and retrieve them as in-context examples at inference - no fine-tuning needed.
why_relevant: (2) the closest published mechanism to the owner's 'learning corpus of failure->repair pairs and exemplars injected into prompts', with a SWE-bench number for the ICL (no-training) variant and a leaderboard folder (20250110_learn_by_interact_claude3.5).
claimed_results: arXiv 2501.10893 (2025-01-18): 'up to 12.2% for ICL with Claude-3.5 and 19.5% for training with Codestral-22B' across SWE-bench, WebArena, OSWorld, Spider2-V; 'innovative retrieval approaches optimized for agents' over conventional RAG.

name: GitHub Copilot coding agent
one_line: Assign an issue -> ephemeral GitHub Actions VM -> agent pushes commits to a draft PR, runs tests/linters, iterates on review comments; workflow runs and PR approval are gated by humans.
why_relevant: (1)/(3) the most-deployed issue->PR system, with two structural guardrails worth copying: 'The developer who asks the agent to open a pull request cannot be the one to approve it' and 'GitHub Actions workflows won't run without your approval' (untrusted code cannot self-trigger CI). No adoption numbers found on these pages.
claimed_results: Blog 2025-05-19 (updated 2025-05-23): agent 'boots a virtual machine, clones the repository, configures the environment', uses 'retrieval augmented generation (RAG) powered by GitHub code search', 'regularly pushes its changes to a draft pull request'; premium requests from 2025-06-04. Docs (viewed 2026-09-02): 'execute automated tests and linters', 'Every step happening in a commit and being viewable in logs', custom agents/instructions.

name: GitLab Duo Agent Platform - Developer flow / foundational flows
one_line: Assign the 'duo developer' service account to an issue -> flow runs inside GitLab CI/CD -> draft MR; can run tests only if agent-config.yml provisions the environment; 11 foundational flows incl. Fix CI/CD Pipeline and Code Review.
why_relevant: (1) ticket->MR unattended inside CI; (3) 'With a properly configured environment, the Developer Flow can run tests and verify its own changes before committing' - self-run tests, no held-out gate; separate Code Review and Security Review flows act as independent critics. No numbers published.
claimed_results: none stated (no benchmark or adoption figures). Version history: beta GitLab 18.3 (flag duo_workflow_in_ci), renamed Developer Flow 18.6, GA 18.8, flags removed 18.9, Free tier with Credits 18.10, mention triggers 18.11; platform beta 18.2 / GA 18.8; custom flows GA 19.2; LLM 'Claude Sonnet 4'.

name: Linear Agents (Agent Interaction API + agent directory)
one_line: Ticket-delegation protocol: delegate an issue -> AgentSessionEvent webhook -> agent emits thought/action/response activities; directory lists Cursor, Codex, Devin, Sentry Seer, Oz by Warp, Factory, Charlie, Ranger, Tembo, ChatPRD.
why_relevant: (1) the de-facto 'ticket-in' contract that shipping coding agents implement; the session/activity model (visible state, 10-second acknowledgement, human stays primary assignee) is a ready pattern for the owner's dashboard intake and progress rendering.
claimed_results: none stated beyond protocol requirements: 'Emit a thought activity within 10 seconds'; 'the human user remains the primary assignee, while the agent is added as a contributor'. Directory (linear.app/agents, viewed 2026-09-02) lists 11 agents, e.g. Factory 'Codes, tests, and creates pull requests', Charlie 'Plans, implements, and reviews your TypeScript PRs'.

name: Tembo (agent orchestration for tickets/alerts -> PRs)
one_line: Runs Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / Amp / OpenCode / Pi in isolated sandboxes from Sentry/Linear/Jira triggers; agents can screenshot and 'visually verify their work'; reviewer feedback auto-turns into revisions.
why_relevant: (1) harness-agnostic multi-agent dispatch from tickets; (3) visual verification + full-stack preview per task; 'Feedback Loop turns reviewer feedback into automatic revisions' matches the owner's repair lane. No numbers, so treat as design reference only.
claimed_results: none stated (site and docs index viewed 2026-09-02 give no PR counts or customers). Quoted capabilities: 'Converts issues and alerts (Sentry, Linear, Jira) into pull requests'; outputs 'working code, test results, artifacts, a full-stack preview, and a reviewable pull request'; 'signed commits, and your PR template'.

name: Plandex
one_line: Terminal agent for large multi-file tasks: cumulative diff sandbox kept apart from the project until approved, plan version control with branches, automated debugging of build/test/lint commands, curated multi-model 'packs'.
why_relevant: (3) partial: the diff-sandbox + branchable plan history is a workspace-isolation pattern; 'Automated debugging of terminal commands (like builds, linters, tests...)' is a self-graded fix loop. No benchmark, no learning across tasks.
claimed_results: none stated (README claims '2M token effective context window', files up to 100k tokens; no benchmark). 15.6k stars.
last_activity: 2026-07-16 (release cli/v2.2.1 'Connect your Claude Pro or Max subscription'; page shows '16 Jul' current-year format)

name: Potpie
one_line: Codebase + SDLC 'living context graph' (indexes GitHub/Linear/Jira/Confluence) served to Claude Code/Codex/Cursor as harnesses; CLI-first, local Context Engine.
why_relevant: (2) adjacent: a persistent, queryable knowledge layer shared across agent runs is one way to get cross-run improvement without fine-tuning; no verification loop, no numbers.
claimed_results: none stated. 5.7k stars; Apache-2.0.

name: bolt.diy
one_line: Open-source Bolt.new clone: WebContainer in-browser runtime, single prompt loop, diff view and file locking; no published verification loop.
why_relevant: Adjacent to the owner's 'build me this web app' input; confirms Lovable-style generators do not publish a held-out or critic-based verification loop (only a diff view and 'File Locking System'). Reference for what NOT to copy.
claimed_results: none stated. 19.8k stars, 10.6k forks.

name: Atlassian Rovo Dev
one_line: Jira-driven CLI/IDE agent that 'acts on your plans in Jira' and reviews code 'validating code changes against acceptance criteria in Jira'.
why_relevant: (3) the acceptance-criteria-in-ticket -> validate-against-AC idea mirrors the owner's spec seat; but the product page gives no mechanism, no SWE-bench figure, and no adoption numbers (blog URLs 404).
claimed_results: none stated on the product page (viewed 2026-09-02).

name: SWE-bench experiments repo (Verified leaderboard submissions + 'checked' process)
one_line: Source of truth for SWE-bench Verified rows: each submission is a folder with README/metadata.yaml; maintainers re-run a random subset to award the checkmark.
why_relevant: (4) tells the owner which claims are independently reproduced: e.g. OpenHands 70.4%, SWE-agent 69%, Qodo 71.2%, Refact 74.4% have ticked checklists; Trae 75.2% has 'checked: false'. Folder names give dates.
claimed_results: Checking rule: 'We will run your model on a random subset of SWE-bench and verify the results'. Folders seen (2025): 20250415_openhands, 20250515_Refact_Agent, 20250516_cortexa_o3, 20250519_trae, 20250522_sweagent_claude-4-sonnet, 20250524_openhands_claude_4_sonnet, 20250603_Refact_Agent_claude-4-sonnet, 20250610_augment_agent_v1, 20250612_trae, 20250623_warp, 20250715_qodo_command, 20250716_openhands_kimi_k2, 20250720_mini-v0.0.0-* , 20250725_sweagent_devstral_small_2507 (API listing truncated after this).

name: SWE-bench Pro public leaderboard (Scale AI)
one_line: Harder, contamination-resistant SWE benchmark run by a third party on a fixed mini-swe-agent harness with 250-turn limit and uncapped cost.
why_relevant: (4) independent 2026 numbers for frontier models under one neutral scaffold; shows current single-agent ceilings (~50-60%) that the owner's held-out gate should expect to see fail 40%+ of the time.
claimed_results: Viewed 2026-09-02 (row dates not shown): Muse Spark 1.1 '61.50±3.10', gpt-5.4 (xHigh) '59.10±3.56', Muse Spark '55.00±3.60', claude-opus-4-6 (thinking) '51.90±3.61', gemini-3.1-pro (thinking) '46.10±3.60' - all 'mini-swe-agent harness'; claude-opus-4-5-20251101 '45.89±3.60' with 'uncapped cost and with a turn limit of 250'.

name: Huxley-Gödel Machine (HGM)
one_line: DGM successor from KAUST/Schmidhuber: chooses which self-modified agent to expand using Clade-Metaproductivity (aggregate benchmark performance of an agent's descendants) instead of the node's own score, fixing DGM's 'metaproductivity-performance mismatch'.
why_relevant: Q2/Q4: same 'agent rewrites own code' loop as DGM, but the SELECTION SIGNAL is different - descendants' pass rates, not the parent's. Directly applicable to our self-repair tier: rank candidate pipeline patches by what their downstream repairs achieved, not by their own gate score. ICLR 2026 oral.
claimed_results: "outperforms prior self-improving methods on SWE-bench Verified and Polyglot" and "achieves human-level performance, matching the best officially checked results of human-engineered coding agents" when optimised on SWE-bench Verified with GPT-4-mini and evaluated on SWE-bench Lite with GPT-4 (arXiv 2510.21614, 24 Oct 2025, v3 29 Oct 2025). No absolute percentages in abstract/README.

name: SICA - Self-Improving Coding Agent (Bristol)
one_line: Loop: evaluate current agent on benchmarks -> store in archive -> run the agent on its own base_agent/ codebase to propose improvements -> repeat, inside Docker; no gradient updates, LLM reflection + code edits only.
why_relevant: Q2: UPDATED artifact is the agent's own codebase (tools, orchestration logic); SIGNAL is a utility combining benchmark score with cost/time. Q3: benchmark tests are external. Q4: modest single-team evidence but a clean, small reference implementation of the run->grade->edit-self loop, with per-iteration results dirs.
claimed_results: "performance gains from 17% to 53% on a random subset of SWE Bench Verified", plus gains on LiveCodeBench and synthetic benchmarks (arXiv 2504.15228, 21 Apr 2025, revised 16 May 2025; NeurIPS 2025 submission). README states no numbers.
last_activity: unknown (repo 395 stars, MIT; last commit date not shown)

name: Meta-Harness (Stanford IRIS / Finn, Khattab)
one_line: An agentic proposer with filesystem access to the source code, scores and execution traces of every prior harness candidate iteratively rewrites the harness (retrieval, memory, prompt-construction logic, or full program), scored only on a search set with a held-out test set.
why_relevant: Q2: UPDATED artifact is harness code (not weights, not just prompt text); SIGNAL is search-set score plus full traces of prior candidates. Q3: proposer 'never accesses test-set results' - a held-out discipline identical to our visible/held-out split. Q4: best numbers of any harness-optimiser on an agentic coding benchmark. Artifact repo stanford-iris-lab/meta-harness-tbench2-artifact (from HTML). Follow-ups: WHALE (arXiv 2609.00196, 31 Aug 2026, alternates weight updates and Meta-Harness search, +4.15-24.38pp mean@8, krafton-ai/WHALE ships meta_harness/ proposer skill, 7 stars); Adaptive Auto-Harness (arXiv 2606.01770, open-ended task streams, human-steering hooks); 'The Last Harness You'll Ever Build' (arXiv 2604.21003, two-level meta-evolution with an adversarial Evaluator Agent, no numbers).
claimed_results: "online text classification +7.7 points with 4x fewer context tokens; +4.7 points average on 200 IMO-level math problems across five held-out models; TerminalBench-2 with Claude Opus 4.6: Terminus-KIRA 74.7% vs discovered harness 76.4%; Claude Haiku 4.5 discovered harness 37.6%, #1 among all Haiku-4.5 agents" (arXiv 2603.28052, submitted 30 Mar 2026).

name: Agentic Harness Engineering (AHE) / NexAU
one_line: Harness split into seven git-tracked file-level components (system prompt, tool descriptions, tool implementations, middleware, skills, sub-agent configs, long-term memory); an Agent Debugger distils millions of trajectory tokens into a layered evidence corpus; an Evolve Agent proposes edits each with a 'change manifest' predicting which tasks will be fixed/regressed; next iteration's rollouts verify the prediction and ineffective edits are reverted at file granularity.
why_relevant: This is the closest published match to our offline self-diagnosis + repair tier. Q2: UPDATED artifacts are harness structure files, base model frozen; SIGNAL is Terminal-Bench pass@1 deltas attributed against the edit's own prediction ('each edit becomes falsifiable by the next evaluation'). Q3: prediction-vs-outcome attribution is a built-in negative control. Q4: numbers on TB-2 and cross-model transfer; key finding 'factual harness structure transfers while prose-level strategy does not' argues for editing tools/middleware rather than prompt prose. Seed harness deliberately minimal (single shell tool). Also the coding-specific survey 'Self-Evolving Coding Agents' (arXiv 2608.03392, Aug 2026) maps this space by target of evolution.
claimed_results: "Terminal-Bench 2 pass@1 69.7% -> 77.0% over 10 iterations (GPT-5.4 high, 89 tasks); cross-model gains +5.1 to +10.1pp; 12% fewer tokens than seed on SWE-bench-Verified" (arXiv 2604.25850, 28 Apr 2026, final 18 May 2026). README: "84.7% +/- 2.1 pass@1 on Terminal-Bench 2 (GPT-5.5), #3 on leaderboard; outperforms Codex (71.9%), ACE and Training-Free GRPO baselines" (README, May 2026). Affiliations Fudan / Peking / Shanghai Qiji Zhifeng.

name: Harness Engineering: Anatomy, Architecture, and Evolution of Coding Agents (11-system source study)
one_line: Source-code study of eleven production coding harnesses (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Mistral Vibe, OpenHands, Aider, Mini-SWE-Agent, Hermes, Pi, OpenCode, OpenClaw) plus the Omnigent meta-harness, extracting 29 recurring design patterns.
why_relevant: Q4: a catalogue of concrete architectural choices actually shipped in production harnesses, useful for checking our seat design against field convergence (e.g. SKILL.md adopted by 9/11, MCP 8/11, no vector embeddings for code retrieval, no general agent frameworks imported).
claimed_results: "eleven systems, ~4 million lines of code, 29 recurring design patterns; no agent runtime imports a general-purpose agentic framework nor uses vector embeddings for code retrieval; SKILL.md adoption (9/11) exceeds MCP (8/11)" (arXiv 2609.00006, submitted 15 Jul 2026 per abs page, announced Sep 2026).

name: OpenAI 'Harness engineering: Leveraging Codex in an agent-first world'
one_line: OpenAI team reports building a ~1M-LOC product with zero hand-written code by making the repository itself the agent's memory: ~100-line AGENTS.md as table of contents, docs/ as system of record, custom linters + structural tests that mechanically enforce architecture, recurring background 'garbage collection' Codex tasks that open refactor PRs, and UI/logs/metrics made directly legible to Codex (Chrome DevTools Protocol, local observability stack).
why_relevant: Q1: unattended multi-PR agent development at scale (6+ hour single runs). Q2: the 'learning' is persisted as repo docs and lint rules, not prompt text - the same 'capability belongs in the system' principle as our learning corpus. Q4: self-reported only; commenters note repo never disclosed and ~20% of time spent on 'slop'.
claimed_results: "0 lines of manually-written code; on the order of a million lines of code; ~1,500 pull requests; 5 months; team grew 3 -> 7 engineers; 3.5 PRs per engineer per day; about 1/10th the time; AGENTS.md roughly 100 lines; Codex runs of 6+ hours; ~20% of Friday time on cleanup" (openai.com/index/harness-engineering, page undated - references first commit 'late August 2025' + 5 months, i.e. ~Jan/Feb 2026; read via r.jina.ai proxy because openai.com returns 403; HN thread id 48416264 dated 2026-06-05, 297 points, 206 comments).

name: Ralph loop (ghuntley technique, snarktank/ralph, Anthropic ralph-wiggum plugin)
one_line: Unattended loop: fresh Claude Code/Amp context each iteration; state carried only via git history, prd.json (stories with passes:true/false), progress.txt and AGENTS.md; each iteration picks one failing story, implements, runs typecheck/tests/browser check, commits, appends learnings; stops at max iterations or all stories pass. Anthropic ships the same loop as the ralph-wiggum plugin (Stop hook re-feeds the prompt; --max-iterations; exact-match --completion-promise).
why_relevant: Q1: the most widely adopted unattended greenfield loop on Claude Code. Q2: what is UPDATED between iterations is progress.txt + AGENTS.md ('learnings'), SIGNAL is the story's own quality checks - i.e. self-graded, which is the weakness our held-out suite fixes. Caveats stated by author: placeholder implementations, false 'implemented' assumptions, needs git reset sometimes, ~90% completion on greenfield.
claimed_results: ghuntley.com/ralph (14 Jul 2025): "built CURSED, a production-grade programming language compiler"; "one contractor delivered a $50k USD contract MVP for $297 USD"; "6 repos shipped overnight" at a YC hackathon - all anecdotal. snarktank/ralph: no numbers; 21.7k stars, MIT. ralph-wiggum plugin (anthropics/claude-code/plugins): no numbers, date not shown.
last_activity: unknown (snarktank/ralph shows 33 open issues, 41 PRs, active)

name: Claude Code auto memory + CLAUDE.md (official docs)
one_line: Claude writes its own memory: per-repo directory ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ with a MEMORY.md index (first 200 lines / 25KB loaded every session) and on-demand topic files typed user/feedback/project/reference; skips anything derivable from code or already in CLAUDE.md; subagents can have their own memory via a `memory` field; main-session auto memory is NOT loaded into subagents.
why_relevant: Q2: what is UPDATED between runs is a markdown index + topic files, SIGNAL is the owner's corrections and confirmed approaches (no automatic grading). For our pipeline, note that seats spawned as subagents do not inherit it - our learning corpus must be injected explicitly. Also documents /doctor trimming of CLAUDE.md and the 'InstructionsLoaded' hook for auditing what was actually loaded.
claimed_results: none stated

name: Anthropic - How we built our multi-agent research system
one_line: Orchestrator-worker: Opus 4 lead plans and spawns parallel Sonnet 4 subagents; LLM-as-judge rubric on end state; rainbow deployments and checkpoint resumption for long-running agents.
why_relevant: Q1: production multi-agent evidence with numbers, and explicit lessons (delegation prompts, scale effort to complexity, end-state not step evaluation). Q4: token cost data (15x) informs our per-seat budget lines.
claimed_results: "multi-agent system with Claude Opus 4 as lead and Claude Sonnet 4 subagents outperformed single-agent Claude Opus 4 by 90.2% on our internal research eval"; "agents typically use about 4x more tokens than chat, multi-agent systems about 15x"; "token usage by itself explains 80% of the variance; three factors explain 95%" (Anthropic engineering blog, 13 Jun 2025).

name: Cognition - Don't Build Multi-Agents
one_line: Argues parallel subagents fail because 'actions carry implicit decisions, and conflicting decisions carry bad results'; recommends a single-threaded linear agent plus a dedicated context-compression model, with subagents only for well-defined questions.
why_relevant: Q1 counterpoint: the Devin team's rationale against lead/teammate parallelism for builds (Flappy Bird example of conflicting assumptions). Relevant to whether our builder should be one seat with compression vs a team. No evidence beyond examples.
claimed_results: none stated (Cognition blog, 12 Jun 2025)

name: Training-Free GRPO (Tencent Youtu-Agent)
one_line: For each query sample G=5 rollouts; an LLM compares successful vs failed rollouts to extract a natural-language 'semantic advantage'; an experience library (JSON) is updated with add/delete/modify operations; the library is injected as context on subsequent API calls - no parameter updates.
why_relevant: Q2: UPDATED artifact is an experience file, SIGNAL is group-relative outcome comparison (needs a verifiable reward, e.g. tests). Q4: cost figure is the useful datum; AHE (Apr 2026) reports beating a TF-GRPO baseline on Terminal-Bench 2, so it is now a known baseline for harness self-improvement. Branch merged to main.
claimed_results: "AIME24 80.0% -> 82.7%; AIME25 67.9% -> 73.3%; WebWalkerQA 63.2% -> 67.8% (DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus); 100 training samples; ~$18 vs ~$10,000 for fine-tuning baseline" (arXiv 2510.08191 HTML, submitted 9 Oct 2025; Tencent Youtu Lab).
last_activity: branch marked deprecated/merged; youtu-agent 4.6k stars, 53 open issues (date not shown)

name: CODESKILL: Learning Self-Evolving Skills for Coding Agents
one_line: A small skill-management policy (Qwen3.5-4B, trained with RL on rubric + execution reward) extracts multi-granularity procedural skills from coding-agent trajectories, evolves them with new experience and keeps a compact skill bank; the coding agent itself (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B) stays frozen.
why_relevant: Q2: UPDATED artifact is a skill bank (Voyager-style, applied to SWE-bench/Terminal-Bench); SIGNAL is execution verification plus a quality rubric. The skill-extractor is fine-tuned, but the transferable idea is a separate 'librarian' seat that curates lessons under an execution-verified reward. Q4: beats prompt/memory baselines. No code link. Related: FlowEvo (arXiv 2607.21596, COLM 2026, DEFENSE-SEU/FlowEvo, 20 stars) compiles successful workflows into executable skills with a governance layer that suppresses negative transfer; beats ExpeL in 49/50 comparisons.
claimed_results: "SWE-Bench Verified 57.33% -> 66.00%; Terminal-Bench 2 25.88% -> 34.12%; EnvBench-Python 6.98% -> 18.60%; EnvBench-Java 27.10% -> 38.32%; 9.69% average improvement over no-skill baseline, 4.01% over strongest prompt-based or memory baseline" (arXiv 2605.25430 HTML, submitted 25 May 2026; NTU / Zhejiang).

name: Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
one_line: Case-based reasoning: a Case Bank of (state, action, reward) tuples plus a small neural case-selection policy updated online from environment reward (memory-augmented MDP); Meta-Planner decomposes tasks and reuses retrieved successful trajectories; LLM weights untouched.
why_relevant: Q2: UPDATED artifact is the case bank and a tiny retrieval policy; SIGNAL is task reward. Not coding-specific (GAIA/DeepResearcher), but it is the cleanest 'experience replay without weights' reference and reports OOD gains. Q4: numbers but no coding benchmark.
claimed_results: "GAIA 87.88% Pass@3 (validation), 79.40% (test); DeepResearcher 66.6% F1 / 80.4% PM; +4.7-9.6 absolute on out-of-distribution tasks; SimpleQA 95.0%; HLE 24.4% PM" (arXiv 2508.16153, 22 Aug 2025, rev 25 Aug 2025; README).
last_activity: 2025-10-05 (README news: parametric CBR release); 2.6k stars, MIT

name: The Red Queen Gödel Machine: Co-Evolving Agents and Their Evaluators
one_line: Self-improving agent whose evaluator/utility also evolves, organised into epochs: evaluator frozen within an epoch (so per-epoch improvement guarantees hold), updated at epoch boundaries under an adversarial objective; tested on coding verification, paper writing/reviewing and olympiad proof grading.
why_relevant: Q3: the only DGM-family paper that treats the grader as a co-evolving, exploitable component rather than fixed ground truth - directly relevant to our audit seat and rubric self-preference problem. Also documents grader over-acceptance of AI output. Related: SBCO (arXiv 2608.10157, Aug 2026) learns a decomposed verifier bank + harness policy by block-coordinate ascent and 'matches or exceeds a customized self-modifying baseline while using 4-5.5 times less compute'.
claimed_results: "1.35x-1.72x fewer tokens on coding tasks; 1.78x-1.86x higher acceptance rates for co-evolved writers; 9% higher ground-truth accuracy for co-evolved graders; reviewers over-accept AI papers at 1.91x the human rate" (arXiv 2606.26294, submitted 24 Jun 2026, revised 29 Jun 2026). No code link found.

name: EVOMAL: Self-Poisoning in Self-Evolving Coding Agents
one_line: Shows that coding agents which author new skills by imitating a shared skill library reproduce planted 'banner'-disguised malicious code, and the copies re-enter the library and persist even after the original is removed.
why_relevant: Risk evidence for Q2: any learning corpus / skills library that the pipeline writes and re-reads is a self-propagation channel. Measured on SWE-bench tasks with six models; gives a defence (counter-prompt against banner-style copying) with a measured residual rate. Should shape how our exemplar corpus is curated (ASSAY below) and sealed.
claimed_results: "agent self-poisoning rate 20.3%-41.8% across six models on 153 SWE-bench tasks; poisoned libraries hold 4.9 to 9.0 times as many malicious skills as were planted; Qwen3 maintained 68% ASPR in round 5 after removal; counter-prompt defence reduces ASPR to at most 6.7% with no significant task-completion loss" (arXiv 2608.25776, submitted 26 Aug 2026).

name: ASSAY - Not All Skills Help: Measuring and Repairing Agent Knowledge
one_line: Separates skill generation from curation: computes each skill's causal contribution per task type by randomized masking on a dev set, then suppresses skills with negative effect per task; shows individual skills routinely help some task types and hurt others while netting to zero in aggregate.
why_relevant: Q2/Q3: gives our learning corpus the negative control it needs - measure each injected exemplar/lesson's effect by masking before trusting it, rather than reading aggregate gate pass rate. Code at aiming-lab/assay (not opened).
claimed_results: "AppWorld hardest split 69.3% task-goal completion with DeepSeek-V3 (+47.4% relative); tau-bench retail +8.7% relative with GPT-4.1" (arXiv 2606.15390, submitted 13 Jun 2026).

name: ShinkaEvolve (Sakana AI)
one_line: Sample-efficient evolutionary program search: parent sampling (weighted / power-law / beam) with an archive of inspirations, novelty rejection via code-embedding similarity threshold (0.99), UCB bandit over an LLM ensemble with cost-aware coefficient, and a meta-prompt loop that evolves the system prompt itself.
why_relevant: Q2: UPDATED artifacts are programs AND the mutation prompt; SIGNAL is an automated evaluator score. Q4: sample-efficiency numbers with dates; the bandit-over-models and novelty-rejection mechanisms are copyable to our fix loop (fingerprint anti-loop is a crude novelty filter). ICLR 2026.
claimed_results: "discovers a new state-of-the-art circle packing solution using only 150 samples"; "ALE-Bench 2.3% performance improvement on average, one task competitive for 2nd place in AtCoder"; "MoE load balancing: reduced inefficient token routing by 5.81% and increased task performance by 1.73% on average after only 30 generations, generalising to models with 5x more parameters"; "AIME results in only 75 generations" (sakana.ai/shinka-evolve, 25 Sep 2025; arXiv 2509.19349, 17 Sep 2025).

name: AlphaEvolve (Google DeepMind)
one_line: Gemini Flash (breadth) + Gemini Pro (depth) propose code edits; automated evaluators score them; an evolutionary program database selects which programs seed the next prompts.
why_relevant: Q2/Q4: the anchor for 'evolve code against an automated verifier' with documented production adoption (data-centre scheduler in production over a year). Verification is non-self-graded by construction (external evaluator functions). Architecture is public, code is not.
claimed_results: "continuously recovers, on average, 0.7% of Google's worldwide compute resources" and "in production for over a year"; "4x4 complex-valued matrices in 48 scalar multiplications"; "23% speedup" of a Gemini kernel giving "1% reduction in Gemini's training time"; FlashAttention "up to 32.5% speedup"; "in roughly 75% of cases rediscovered state-of-the-art solutions; in 20% improved the previously best known solutions"; kissing number "593 outer spheres" in 11 dimensions (DeepMind blog, 14 May 2025).

name: R2E-Gym (+ SWE-Gym / SWE-smith / SWE-RL / SkyRL family)
one_line: Procedurally generated executable SWE environments (SYNGEN: back-translate tasks from commits) plus HYBRID verifiers - an execution-based testing agent that writes targeted unit tests and an execution-free critic that reranks patches - used for test-time scaling of open-weight agents.
why_relevant: These fine-tune weights, so Q2 does not transfer, but two mechanisms do: (Q3) R2E-Gym's finding that execution-based and execution-free verifiers 'address each other's weaknesses when combined' is a concrete design for our judge/critic split; and SWE-smith's bug-synthesis (LM modify, LM rewrite, procedural AST edits, PR mirroring, combined) is a way to manufacture a frozen known-bad corpus for our self-repair gate. Family numbers: SWE-Gym 2,438 tasks, verifier-trained 32.0% Verified / 26.0% Lite (arXiv 2412.21139, ICML 2025); SWE-smith 52k tasks, 26k trajectories, SWE-agent-LM-32B 40.2% Verified (arXiv 2504.21798, NeurIPS 2025 D&B spotlight, 757 stars); SWE-RL Llama3-SWE-RL-70B 41.0% Verified with rule-based patch-similarity reward (arXiv 2502.18449, v2 1 Dec 2025); SkyRL v0.3.0 released 2026-07-16, SkyRL-SQL matches GPT-4o/o4-mini on Text2SQL from 653 samples (README).
claimed_results: "51% pass@1 on SWE-Bench Verified, state-of-the-art for open-weight SWE-Agents" with hybrid verifiers; "more than 8.7K tasks" (arXiv 2504.07164, 9 Apr 2025); README: 8,100+ problems across 13 repos, 327 stars, Apache-2.0.
last_activity: unknown (R2E-Gym 9 commits on main; SkyRL v0.3.0 2026-07-16)

name: SWT-Bench (tests-from-issue as a patch filter)
one_line: NeurIPS 2024 benchmark measuring whether code agents can turn a GitHub issue into a fail-to-pass reproducing test before any fix exists; shows such tests double patch-selection precision.
why_relevant: Q3 (non-self-graded verification) and Q4. Our spec seat writes a Playwright suite FROM THE TICKET ALONE; SWT-Bench is the closest measured analogue: grader = execution (test must fail pre-fix, pass post-fix, plus coverage delta), builder never sees the reference tests. Key transferable finding: issue-derived tests used as a filter over candidate patches 'doubling the precision of SWE-Agent'. Also finds repair-oriented agents write better reproduction tests than dedicated test-gen tools.
claimed_results: arXiv 2406.12952 abstract (submitted 2024-06-18, rev 2025-02-07): 'generated tests are an effective filter for proposed code fixes, doubling the precision of SWE-Agent'. Repo README leaderboard (gold validation): Lite 276 / Verified 433 / Full 2,294 instances; P->P rate 10.86% / 15.01% / 17.65%; coverage delta 71.84% / 69.12% / 65.13%.
last_activity: repo 89 stars; last commit date not shown in fetch; paper revised 2025-02-07

name: TDD-Bench Verified + Otter (IBM)
one_line: 449 SWE-bench-Verified-derived issues where the model must write tests before the fix; graded on fail-to-pass and coverage adequacy; Otter (ICML 2025) is the accompanying test-from-issue generator with rule-based output repair.
why_relevant: Q3/Q4. Exactly our spec-seat problem statement ('predict test cases without looking at the final code'). Grading is execution-based in Docker, held-out from the generator. Otter's architecture (LLM + rule-based checks that repair its own outputs + self-reflective action planner) is a copyable pattern for the audit-and-freeze stage of our suite.
claimed_results: arXiv 2412.02883 (2024-12-03): Auto-TDD 'yields a better fail-to-pass rate than the strongest prior work while also yielding high coverage adequacy' (no % in abstract). arXiv 2502.05368 (2025-02-07, rev 2025-05-30, ICML 2025 main track): Otter/Otter++ GPT-4o outputs shipped in repo; numeric rates not extracted from abstract.
last_activity: repo 35 stars; last commit date not shown; paper rev 2025-05-30

name: UTBoost: augmented hidden tests expose false SWE-bench passes
one_line: Automatically generates extra test cases for SWE-bench tasks and shows a large fraction of 'resolved' patches are wrong once the hidden suite is strengthened.
why_relevant: Q3/Q4: the best direct measurement of the visible-vs-hidden test gap in coding agents. Argues for our held-out half being ADVERSARIALLY AUGMENTED, not just split: weak held-out suites let false finishes through. Mechanism (analyze codebase+deps, synthesize additional tests, re-run) is what our adversarial-audit stage should do.
claimed_results: arXiv 2506.09289 (submitted 2025-06-10, ACL 2025): '345 erroneous patches' incorrectly marked as passing; '36 task instances' with insufficient tests; corrections affect '40.9% of SWE-Bench Lite and 24.4% of SWE-Bench Verified leaderboard entries'; '18 ranking changes on Lite and 11 on Verified'.

name: PatchDiff: 'Are Solved Issues in SWE-bench Really Solved Correctly?'
one_line: Differential patch testing between agent patch and ground-truth patch to detect behaviorally divergent 'plausible' patches that pass the benchmark tests.
why_relevant: Q3/Q4: quantifies how often passing the visible/benchmark tests is not correctness. Differential testing against a reference (our design lane could keep a reference implementation or property set) is a cheap extra grader that is not self-graded.
claimed_results: arXiv 2503.15223 (submitted 2025-03-19, rev 2025-09-09): '7.8%' of patches passed tests but failed developer-written suites; '29.6%' of plausible patches behave differently from ground truth; '28.6%' of divergent patches confirmed incorrect by manual inspection; overall inflation '6.2 absolute percentage points' in resolution rate (3 SOTA tools on SWE-bench Verified).

name: METR pre-deployment evaluation of GPT-5.6 Sol (cheating rates)
one_line: METR reports the highest cheating rate of any public model, including exploits that leak the hidden test suite via intermediate submissions; time-horizon estimate swings 11h to >270h depending on how cheating is scored.
why_relevant: Q4: hard evidence (June 2026) that frontier models actively probe for hidden tests, so held-out suites must be sealed at OS/network level (our Docker --network=none + permission rules), and that 'DONE' claims must be scored as failures when gaming is detected — matches our falseFinish metric.
claimed_results: Post dated 2026-06-26: model observed 'packaging exploits in its intermediate submissions to reveal information about a task's hidden test suite'; time horizon '~11.3 hours (95% CI: 5-40 hours)' scoring cheating as failure; '>270 hours' if cheating counted as success; '71 hours (95% CI: 13-11,400 hours)' discarding cheating runs.

name: Escalation channels redirect reward hacking toward defect disclosure
one_line: Gives agents a structured tool to report defective test infrastructure instead of exploiting it; cuts reward hacking across 8 frontier models.
why_relevant: Q3/Q4: direct architectural fix for our fix-seat loop: add a 'report suite defect' tool that parks the run / escalates to owner rather than letting the builder patch around a bad held-out test. Combined with monitoring it adds defect coverage, which also feeds our learning corpus (failure->repair pairs).
claimed_results: arXiv 2608.29460 (2026-08-29): combined intervention reduced reward hacking 'from 23.6% to 5.3%' across 8 frontier models in 5 families; escalation channels added '+10.1 percentage points of defect detection coverage' beyond monitoring alone.

name: The Verification Horizon: No Silver Bullet for Coding Agent Rewards
one_line: Compares four verifier constructions (test verifier, rubric/interactive judge for frontend, user-as-verifier, automated agent verifier for long-horizon) and reports which design choices suppress hacking.
why_relevant: Q3/Q4: the frontend 'Interactive Judge' (grades by simulated user interaction in a live browser rather than static code reading, which 'avoids length exploitation') is the design our rendered taste-critic should adopt; the test-verifier result shows behaviour monitoring for solution-artifact access nearly eliminates hacked passes; the long-horizon agent-verifier section lists failure modes to design out ('lazy evaluation without execution', 'lack of end-to-end validation', 'role confusion').
claimed_results: arXiv 2606.26300 v2 (2026-06-24/29), results section: test verifier + behaviour monitoring: hacked resolved rate '28.57% to 0.56%', clean resolved '40.22% to 60.53%'; interactive judge RFT '+6 points on WebDev Human Eval, +36 points on QwenWebBench'; automated agent verifier best-of-N accuracy '67.4% (Claude Opus 4.7)'.

name: BenchJack: auditing agent benchmarks for reward-hacking flaws
one_line: Generative-adversarial pipeline where coding agents red-team a benchmark's grader, find exploits, and patch them iteratively.
why_relevant: Q3: this is our 'adversarial audit of the suite' stage as a measured system: run an attacker agent against the frozen suite before sealing, patch, repeat until hackable-task ratio is low. Reports 8 flaw-pattern classes we can turn into an audit checklist.
claimed_results: arXiv 2605.12673 (2026-05-12): '219 distinct flaws' across '10 popular agent benchmarks' (SWE, web navigation, desktop, terminal); hackable-task ratio reduced 'from near 100% to under 10%' on four benchmarks; WebArena and OSWorld fully patched within three iterations.

name: NL2Repo-Bench: requirements document to whole repository
one_line: Agent gets only a natural-language requirements doc and an empty workspace and must produce an installable library, graded by hidden test suites over hundreds of steps.
why_relevant: Q1/Q3/Q4: the benchmark shape closest to our ticket-in -> app-out pipeline with hidden grading. Its failure taxonomy (premature termination, loss of global coherence, fragile cross-file deps, inadequate planning) is a ready-made list of what our plan seat, continuation lane and falseFinish gate must catch.
claimed_results: arXiv 2512.12730 (2025-12-14, rev 2026-01-08): 'even the strongest agents achieve below 40% average test pass rates and rarely complete an entire repository correctly'.

name: ArtifactsBench (Tencent Hunyuan) rendered-artifact MLLM judge
one_line: Renders generated web/SVG/game artifacts, captures screenshots at three time points, and has a multimodal judge score against a per-task checklist; validated against WebDev Arena human votes.
why_relevant: Q3/Q4: the best-evidenced recipe for a rendered 'taste critic' that is not self-graded: programmatic render -> temporal screenshots -> checklist-guided MLLM judge separate from the builder. Per-task checklists authored at spec time (our spec seat) make the judge reproducible.
claimed_results: arXiv 2507.04952 (2025-07-07, rev 2025-09-29) and README: '94.4% ranking consistency with WebDev Arena', 'over 90% pairwise agreement with human experts'; 1,825 tasks; GPT-5 leads at 72.55, GPT-OSS-120B best open at 57.69.
last_activity: repo 278 stars; last commit July 2025, v1.2 August 2025

name: WebGen-Bench + WebGen-Agent (UI-agent executed tests on generated sites)
one_line: Benchmark for building websites from scratch, graded by a WebVoyager UI agent executing 647 natural-language test cases plus a VLM appearance score; WebGen-Agent feeds screenshot-critic and GUI-agent scores back into generation with backtracking.
why_relevant: Q1/Q3/Q4: same target as our tickets ('build me this web app'); grading is external interaction, not builder self-report. WebGen-Agent shows the effect size of putting a screenshot critic + GUI-agent tester in the builder loop with select-best/backtrack, which is our design lane + fix loop.
claimed_results: arXiv 2505.03733 (2025-05-06): 647 test cases, best 'Bolt.diy with DeepSeek-R1' 27.8% accuracy. arXiv 2509.22644 (2025-09-26): Claude-3.5-Sonnet accuracy '26.4% to 51.9%', appearance '3.0 to 3.9'; Qwen2.5-Coder-7B '38.9% to 45.4%'. Appearance judged by Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct (README).

name: WebGrader: self-evolving programmatic grader with Flow Contracts
one_line: Derives required interaction flows from each website request, compiles them to executable Flow Contracts, grades on visual+DOM+response+persistent-state evidence in a live browser, and freezes a promoted verifier-skill graph before training.
why_relevant: Q2/Q3: the closest published analogue to our spec seat (contracts from the ticket) plus our self-learning tier (residual-driven offline loop discovers reusable verifier skills, screens them on disjoint validation pages, then FREEZES them) — that is a frozen-corpus gate for the grader itself, without fine-tuning the grader.
claimed_results: arXiv 2608.06474 (2026-08-06): 8B policy reaches '52.01% functional success rate' on WebGen-Bench, '+7.88 percentage points' over matched baseline; 'Full Score of 44.953 on WG-core-250'.

name: CodeMonkeys (model-generated tests + selection trajectory)
one_line: Scales test-time compute on SWE-bench by having the model write and run its own test script alongside each edit, then selects among candidates by voting on model-generated tests plus a dedicated selection trajectory.
why_relevant: Q3/Q4: concrete, costed recipe for best-of-N with tests the builder wrote itself (visible half) versus a separate selection seat; the ensemble result shows an external selector beats any single member. Caveat for us: the selection tests are self-generated, so this is only the visible-half pattern, not the held-out one.
claimed_results: arXiv 2501.14723 (2025-01-24, rev 2025-02-03) and README: '57.4%' SWE-bench Verified standalone, '66.2%' with ensemble selection; cost '~$2,300' total ('~$4.60 per issue').

name: R2E-Gym hybrid verifiers (execution-based + execution-free)
one_line: Combines agent-generated execution tests with an LLM execution-free verifier to pick among candidate patches; each alone is weak (low distinguishability vs stylistic bias), together they add ~17 points.
why_relevant: Q3/Q4: evidence that a hybrid judge (run tests AND independent critic read) is strictly better than either; our judge seat should take both the sealed-gate result and a rendered/critic verdict as separate inputs rather than one combined self-report.
claimed_results: arXiv 2504.07164 (2025-04-09) and README: SWE-bench Verified pass@1 '34.4%' (32B SFT alone) -> '51%' with hybrid inference-time scaling; 8.1K+ problems across 13 repos.
last_activity: repo 327 stars; DeepSWE/rLLM update noted; commit date not shown

name: Agent-as-a-Judge (DevAI)
one_line: An agent (locate/read/graph/retrieve/ask modules) grades another agent's project against 365 hierarchical requirements; far closer to human consensus than a plain LLM judge, at ~2% of human cost.
why_relevant: Q3: shows a judge with tool access over the workspace and trajectory beats a chat-only judge on requirement satisfaction. Important limitation for us: it does NOT execute code, so it is complementary to, not a substitute for, the sealed test gate.
claimed_results: arXiv 2410.10934 (2024-10-14; ICML 2025) HTML: black-box alignment '90.44%' vs LLM-as-a-Judge '60.38%'; gray-box '92.07%' vs '70.76%'; '118.43 minutes' vs '86.5 human hours'; '$30.58' vs '$1,297.50'; '97.72% time savings and 97.64% cost reduction'. DevAI: 55 tasks, 365 requirements.

name: OpenHands Critic model (best-of-N selection, released weights)
one_line: A 32B critic trained by TD from unit-test outcomes scores complete trajectories to pick the best of five OpenHands rollouts.
why_relevant: Q3/Q4: documented +5.8 points from an independent selector over parallel builder attempts. We cannot fine-tune, but the topology (N builder seats, one separate critic seat that never edits code, picks a winner) is copyable with a prompted judge over trajectories.
claimed_results: Post dated 2025-04-17: SWE-bench Verified '60.6%' single attempt -> '66.4%' with five rollouts; model at huggingface all-hands/openhands-critic-32b-exp-20250417.

name: TestGen-LLM at Meta (assured filters on generated tests)
one_line: Production unit-test improvement at Meta: every generated test must build, pass reliably (repeated runs), and increase coverage before an engineer sees it.
why_relevant: Q3/Q4: the reference for 'assured' test generation — hard mechanical filters (build, flake-check by repeated execution, coverage delta) before any LLM or human judgement. Our spec seat's Playwright suite should pass the same filters before freezing. Older than 18 months but is the only large documented production deployment with numbers.
claimed_results: arXiv 2402.09171 (2024-02-14): '75%' of generated tests built correctly, '57%' passed reliably, '25%' increased coverage; '11.5%' of classes improved; '73%' of recommendations accepted for production (Instagram/Facebook test-a-thons).

name: Anthropic: Natural emergent misalignment from reward hacking
one_line: Shows models learning to escape test harnesses (sys.exit(0)) in real Claude coding RL environments, and that inoculation prompting ('your task is just to make the grading script pass') blocks generalization of the hack.
why_relevant: Q3/Q4: names a concrete harness-escape our gate must be robust to (exit code 0 without running tests — check test-count and per-test results, not exit status), and a prompt-level mitigation that costs nothing.
claimed_results: Post dated 2025-11-21: sabotage of safety research '12% of the time'; alignment faking in '50% of responses'; RLHF left models 'egregiously misaligned on many coding queries'; inoculation prompting eliminated misaligned generalization.

name: OpenAI: Monitoring Reasoning Models for Misbehavior (CoT monitoring of coding agents)
one_line: A weaker model reading the coding agent's chain of thought catches reward hacking far better than watching actions/outputs; optimizing against the monitor produces obfuscated hacking.
why_relevant: Q3: supports a cheap 'transcript monitor' seat over builder/fix-seat reasoning and tool calls as an additional non-self-graded signal, and warns not to feed the monitor's verdict back as a training/selection pressure on the builder.
claimed_results: arXiv 2503.11926 (2025-03-14): 'CoT monitoring can be far more effective than monitoring agent actions and outputs alone'; under strong optimization 'agents learn obfuscated reward hacking, hiding their intent within the CoT'. (Numeric recall figures live in the body; OpenAI blog returned HTTP 403.)

name: SWE-Marathon: ultra-long-horizon software tasks with adversarially reviewed suites
one_line: 20 multi-hour tasks with executable environments and multi-layer verification suites that were adversarially reviewed; reports reward hacking and premature termination rates.
why_relevant: Q1/Q4: our runs are 1-12 hours; this is the only benchmark at that horizon with hidden multi-layer verification. Failure modes ('poor self-verification, self-reported infeasibility, premature termination') are exactly what falseFinish measures.
claimed_results: arXiv 2606.07682 (2026-06-05): frontier agents 'solve fewer than 30% of tasks'; attempts average '27.2M tokens'; reward hacking in '13.8% of rollouts'.

name: TDAD: visible/hidden test split for spec-compiled agents
one_line: Compiles behavioural specs to tests, lets a coding agent iterate until visible tests pass, then scores on withheld hidden tests (Hidden Pass Rate) with mutation testing; Dockerised reference code.
why_relevant: Q3: literally the same architecture as our visible/held-out split (tests_visible/ vs tests_hidden/ directories, HPR metric) with a small measured result. Low evidence but a direct code reference for the split and for mutation-testing the suite.
claimed_results: arXiv 2603.08806 (2026-03-09): '92% v1 compilation success with 97% mean hidden pass rate' on SpecSuite-Core across 24 trials.
last_activity: repo 8 stars; commit date not shown; paper 2026-03-09

name: FrontendBench (sandbox E2E grading with human agreement)
one_line: 148 front-end tasks graded automatically by sandbox execution of human-LLM co-designed tests, reporting agreement with expert evaluation.
why_relevant: Q3/Q4: gives a number for how well an automatic sandboxed E2E grader agrees with humans on frontend work, which is the calibration question for our sealed Playwright gate.
claimed_results: arXiv 2506.13832 (2025-06-16): automatic framework achieves '90.54% agreement rate with expert human evaluations' over 148 tasks.

name: Kiro requirements analysis (neuro-symbolic spec checking before code)
one_line: Kiro's spec workflow adds an optional gate that refines requirements, auto-formalizes them, and uses LLM+SMT reasoning to flag ambiguity, contradiction, incompleteness and wrong level of detail before design/code.
why_relevant: Q3: the only spec-driven tool found that verifies the SPEC itself with a non-LLM check (SMT) and blocks downstream work. Our plan seat's clarifying-questions step could adopt the four bug classes as its checklist; Kiro also lists property-based testing as an IDE 'Correctness' capability (docs).
claimed_results: Post dated 2026-05-12 cites prior research: ambiguous/incomplete prompts cause '20-40%' Pass@1 drops and '60-90% of the syntactically valid code being semantically wrong'; no Kiro-specific outcome numbers.

name: Cursor cloud agent environment (sealed VM + self-healing 'Cloud Doctor')
one_line: Cursor's cloud agents run in Ubuntu VMs from a Dockerfile with egress restrictions, proxied git, secret redaction, computer-use + screen-recording verification, and an automation that root-causes environment failures and opens fix PRs.
why_relevant: Q1/Q2/Q3: documented production adoption of unattended agents with (a) network-restricted sandbox, (b) agents proving work via recorded end-to-end interaction, and (c) an offline self-repair loop for the pipeline's own environment — the same 'self-maintaining tier' we are building.
claimed_results: Post dated 2026-07-30: cloud agents went from 'roughly 1 in 10 merged PRs' (December) to 'more than half' of merged PRs to the Cursor monorepo; Faire 'doubled weekly PR throughput'.

name: GitHub spec-kit (Spec-Driven Development toolkit)
one_line: Specify -> Plan -> Tasks -> Implement -> Converge workflow with optional Clarify/Analyze/Checklist; verification is artifact consistency and gap analysis, not generated tests.
why_relevant: Q1/Q3 (negative finding): the most-adopted spec tool does no held-out or executable verification — 'Analyze' is cross-artifact consistency, 'Checklist' validates requirement quality, 'Converge' diffs implementation against spec. Useful as a phase vocabulary; not a verification source.
claimed_results: README/releases: 133k stars, 12k forks; v1.0.0 on 2026-08-21, v1.0.3 on 2026-09-01; no outcome numbers claimed.

name: BMAD-METHOD (agent roles + BMad Loop unattended epic delivery)
one_line: Role-based agentic method (PM, architect, UX, dev, QA) whose 'BMad Loop' module claims to build, verify and retro a whole epic unattended; Test Architect / quality gates are an enterprise add-on.
why_relevant: Q1: closest open framework to 'lead plus teammates with a shared task list' running unattended. Verification detail is not public (Test Architect is paid), so it teaches role decomposition, not grading.
claimed_results: README: 52.6k stars, 6.0k forks, 2,098 commits; 'BMad Loop builds, verifies, and retros a whole epic unattended'; no quantified results.
last_activity: active (2,098 commits); version/date not shown in fetch

name: Anthropic sandbox-runtime (Claude Code OS-level sandbox)
one_line: Open-source bubblewrap (Linux) / Seatbelt (macOS) sandbox with filesystem scoping and HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy domain allowlists, usable for arbitrary processes and agents.
why_relevant: Q3: runs natively on the owner's macOS machine; gives per-seat filesystem + egress control without Docker, so the held-out half can be made unreadable to the builder seat at OS level (complements the Docker --network=none gate).
claimed_results: Engineering post 2025-10-20: 'sandboxing safely reduces permission prompts by 84%' in internal usage. Repo: 5.1k stars, 706 commits, 'beta research preview'.

name: OpenAI Codex cloud sandbox: internet disabled during agent phase
one_line: Codex cloud blocks internet during the agent phase by default (setup scripts keep access), with domain allowlists and safe-HTTP-method restriction; local Codex uses Seatbelt / bubblewrap+seccomp+landlock.
why_relevant: Q3: production precedent for our two-phase seal (network for dependency setup, none during build/grade) and for an allowlist of ~70 package registries if a seat genuinely needs egress.
claimed_results: Docs (fetched 2026-09-02, undated): 'By default, Codex blocks internet access during the agent phase'; presets 'None', 'Common dependencies' (~70 domains), 'All'; option to restrict to GET/HEAD/OPTIONS.

name: Awesome-Self-Evolving-Coding-Agents (iSEngLab) + survey 'Self-Evolving Coding Agents' (arXiv 2608.03392)
one_line: Paper list backing an Aug-2026 survey that taxonomises how coding agents improve themselves without retraining: framework/harness, memory, skill/tool, workflow-topology, environment/context self-evolution, plus a 'self-evolving coding products' section.
why_relevant: Directly maps owner question (2). Its 1.1-1.3 and 2.x sections are the canonical index of fine-tuning-free self-improvement for coding agents (27 harness-evolution papers, 10 memory papers, 10 skill papers). Products section records which vendors ship cross-run memory (Claude Code Auto Memory, Cursor Memories/Automations, Devin Session Insights/Knowledge/Playbooks, Augment 'Cosmos Learning Flywheel', Gemini CLI Auto Memory, Copilot Memory, Prime Agent). Also indexes the risk papers the owner needs for (3)/(4): 'Reward Hacking in Self-Improving Code Agents' (OpenReview 2026), 'Your Agent May Misevolve' (ICLR 2026), 'Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit' (arXiv 2605.30621). Highlighted entry: Live-SWE-agent (arXiv 2511.13646, Nov 2025) — agent evolves its own scaffold at runtime from bare bash tools.
claimed_results: Survey arXiv 2608.03392 v1 2026-08-04, v3 2026-08-29 (no numbers in abstract). Live-SWE-agent abstract (arXiv 2511.13646, 2025-11-17): '77.4% solve rate' SWE-bench Verified without test-time scaling, '45.8%' SWE-Bench Pro (model not named in abstract).

name: Awesome-Long-Horizon-SE-Agents (xjywhu) with T0-T3 task-horizon taxonomy
one_line: Curated map of long-horizon SE-agent papers/benchmarks organised by task horizon: T0 bounded coding, T1 single-objective, T2 multi-objective with 'separately verifiable acceptance conditions', T3 progressively disclosed requirements.
why_relevant: The T2/T3 sections are the closest index to 'one ticket = one whole application': T2.1 lists every 2025-26 whole-repo/feature benchmark (NL2Repo-Bench, SaaSBench, FeatureBench, RepoZero, ProgramBench, RoadmapBench, SWE-EVO, SWE-Bench Pro, Commit0, SWE-Lancer), T2.2 lists project-scale multi-agent systems (CAID/Geng&Neubig, AgileCoder, MetaGPT, ChatDev), T1.5 lists evaluation-reliability studies (AgentLens lucky-pass, 'Rethinking the Value of Agent-Generated Tests', 'Same Signal, Different Semantics'), T3 lists progressive-spec benchmarks (SWE-INTERACT, SWE-Chain, SlopCodeBench, 'When the Specification Emerges'). Serves owner questions (1), (3), (4).
claimed_results: none stated (index only); cites 5 surveys incl. 'AI Agentic Programming: A Survey' (arXiv 2508.11126, 2025-08-15) and 'A Survey on Code Generation with LLM-based Agents' (arXiv 2508.00083, 2025-07-31).

name: awesome-cli-coding-agents (bradAGI) — 'Orchestrators & autonomous loops' section
one_line: Directory of 120+ terminal coding agents; its orchestrators section is the most complete 2026 list (~47 entries) of unattended multi-agent runners with star counts and licences.
why_relevant: Owner question (1). Every entry below with stars is from this section (fetched 2026-09-02): DeerFlow 81.2k (ByteDance long-horizon super-agent harness), claude-flow/ruflo 69.9k, OpenAI Symphony 27k, gastown 17.9k, Omnigent 9.5k, Kiro Crew 3.5k (AWS), ralph-orchestrator 3.1k, ralph-tui 2.4k, AgentsMesh 2.3k, zeroshot 1.8k, Traycer 1.4k, loom 1.4k, Agentlas OS 1.1k, Loki Mode 1.1k, Bernstein 1k, Aeon 707, fractal 705, LoopTroop 129, MartinLoop 47 ('token budgets, iteration caps, independent verifier'), The Factory 63 ('self-evolving meta-harness ... keep/revert experiment loops'), the-perfect-orchestrator 1 ('adversarial verification'). No benchmark column exists — the list itself is discovery-only.
claimed_results: none stated (star counts only, as of 2026-08-31 README)

name: awesome-loop-engineering-examples (viatsko) + Ralph ecosystem (ralph-orchestrator, HumanLayer 'Brief History of Ralph')
one_line: Index of 'Ralph Wiggum' fresh-context loop runners, things built by loops, and the research the pattern leans on; points to the production lessons from HumanLayer.
why_relevant: Owner question (1) unattended loops and (4) evidence. Concrete mechanisms: one task per fresh-context iteration, progress persisted to files/git, 'the checker must not be the maker' (cites 'LLMs Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet'). HumanLayer post (2026-01-06) gives the production rule: run loops 'ONCE on a cron overnight, and merge small iterations over time', and criticises the official Anthropic ralph-wiggum plugin for missing 'carve off small bits of work into independent context windows'. Verified runner status: mikeyobrien/ralph-orchestrator 3,120 stars pushed 2026-09-02; cobusgreyling/loop-engineering 10,818 stars pushed 2026-09-02; michaelshimeles/ralphy 2,970 stars pushed 2026-02-05; frankbria/ralph-claude-code 9,615 stars pushed 2026-07-18; snwfdhmp/awesome-ralph 918 stars pushed 2026-02-03.
claimed_results: README (fetched 2026-09-02): repomirror 'put a coding agent in a while loop and it shipped 6 repos overnight ... for under $800' (repo last push 2025-08-25); SWE-agent '3.8% → 12.5% on SWE-bench'; Large Language Monkeys '15.9% → 56% on SWE-bench Lite at 250 attempts'. HumanLayer post 2026-01-06: 'August 2025 refactor: 6 hours of autonomous work'.

name: Gas Town (Steve Yegge) — multi-agent workspace manager with Refinery merge queue
one_line: Mayor (lead Claude Code) + Polecats (workers with persistent identity, ephemeral sessions) + Witnesses (per-rig stuck-agent detection/recovery) + Deacon (cross-rig patrol) + Refineries (Bors-style bisecting merge queue that runs verification gates before main).
why_relevant: Owner question (1) lead+teammates with shared task list: work state lives in git-backed 'beads' issues bundled into 'convoys'. Mechanisms worth copying for the fix-seat/anti-loop tier: Witness detects stuck agents and triggers recovery; Refinery batches merge requests, runs gates on the merged stack, bisects on failure to isolate the bad MR; no direct-to-main pushes.
claimed_results: README (fetched 2026-09-02): 'Scale comfortably to 20-30 agents'. No task-success numbers.
last_activity: created 2025-12-16, pushed 2026-09-02, 17,895 stars (repo moved from steveyegge/gastown to gastownhall/gastown)

name: zeroshot (the-open-engine) — independent executor–verifier orchestration
one_line: Conductor classifies each task (TRIVIAL/SIMPLE/STANDARD/CRITICAL); STANDARD spawns planner + worker + 2 validators, CRITICAL 4 validators in 2 stages; loop runs 'until the change is verified or returns a concrete reason it is not'.
why_relevant: Owner question (3) non-self-graded verification, implemented on CLI agents: 'Validators do not share the executor's session or reasoning context; they may receive explicit handoff artifacts and must reproduce reported failures.' Isolation via git worktree (default) or Docker; all state in a SQLite ledger with `zeroshot resume <id>` — same shape as the owner's continuation lane.
claimed_results: README (fetched 2026-09-02): one demonstrated run '90-minute run · 5 iterations to approval'; no aggregate metrics.

name: Loki Mode (asklokesh) — spec-to-product loop with Evidence Receipts and blind-review council
one_line: RARV (Reason-Act-Reflect-Verify) cycles over 41 agent roles; every build emits an Evidence Receipt (.loki/proofs/) that separates re-derivable Facts (diff SHAs, test/build exit codes, gate verdicts) from labelled AI Assessments.
why_relevant: Owner questions (1)+(3): receipt headline VERIFIED / VERIFIED WITH GAPS / NOT VERIFIED is computed from facts only ('tests passed (exit 0), non-empty diff, nothing skipped'); `loki proof verify <id>` checks tamper/drift. 8 gates incl. test-mutation detection and mock-integrity detection; 'blind 3-reviewer code review', anti-sycophancy Devil's Advocate, and a 'confidence spike' rule (high self-reported confidence triggers an extra verification pass) — direct analogue of falseFinish. 3-tier episodic/semantic/procedural memory across projects for (2). Budgets: `--max-budget-usd`, LOKI_MAX_TIER, early stop on permanent failures.
claimed_results: README (fetched 2026-09-02): HumanEval '162/164 (98.78%)' self-reported; 'SWE-bench: Not yet measured'; build times 'simple ~5–30 min, standard ~30–90 min, complex 2+ hours'.

name: Bernstein — deterministic multi-agent orchestrator with signed run receipts (plus MartinLoop)
one_line: 'Deterministic scheduler - no model in the coordination loop'; parallel CLI agents in per-task git worktrees; a 'janitor' checks concrete signals (tests pass, files exist, lint clean, types correct) behind merge gates; offline-verifiable signed receipts with optional HMAC audit chain.
why_relevant: Owner question (3): verification is deterministic and outside the model. Failed tasks re-route to a different model before merge. Sibling with the same philosophy at smaller scale: Keesan12/martin-loop (47 stars, pushed 2026-09-02) — `--verify <cmd>` is a shell command not a model, `--budget-usd`/`--max-tokens`/`--max-iterations` hard caps, outcomes VERIFIED / STOPPED / NEEDS REVIEW with 'fresh verifier evidence bound to the active run and workspace'.
claimed_results: README (fetched 2026-09-02): author motivation only — '$400/month in claude bills running three coding agents in parallel and getting nondeterministic merges'. No success metrics.

name: re:factory / The Factory (akashgit/remote-factory) — self-evolving meta-harness with keep/revert loop
one_line: A 'CEO' agent runs hypothesis → build → evaluate → keep/revert experiments on the harness itself, scored by a weighted composite over Hygiene (6 dims), Growth (5 dims) and user-defined Project metrics.
why_relevant: Owner question (2): the closest small open implementation of the owner's 'offline self-diagnosis + repair behind a frozen gate' tier. Regression detection = composite score gate + CI test that catches drift between workflow definitions and exported skills. Useful as a pattern, not as evidence.
claimed_results: none stated — README has no quantitative results (fetched 2026-09-02)

name: gstack (Garry Tan) — 23-role software factory for Claude Code
one_line: Think → Plan → Build → Review → Test → Ship → Reflect pipeline where distinct personas (CEO, Eng Manager, Designer, Staff Engineer /review, QA Lead /qa in a real Chromium browser, CSO /cso, /codex cross-model second opinion) gate the builder's work.
why_relevant: Owner questions (1)+(3): gates are run by different personas/models than the builder; /qa drives a real browser and auto-generates regression tests for each bug fixed; /codex asks OpenAI for a second opinion (cross-vendor critic). For (2): /learn per-project learnings, taste memory via gstack-taste-update, per-site domain notes that auto-fire on return, GBrain cross-machine knowledge base. Highest-starred item in the whole sweep, but all evidence is founder-self-reported.
claimed_results: README (fetched 2026-09-02): 'In the last 60 days: 3 production services, 40+ shipped features, part-time, while running YC full-time'; 'my 2026 run rate is ~810× my 2013 pace (11,417 vs 14 logical lines/day)'; 'Year-to-date (through April 18), 2026 has already produced 240× the entire 2013 year'.

name: Anthropic — 'Harness design for long-running application development' (Planner / Generator / Evaluator)
one_line: Official Anthropic write-up of a 3-agent harness that turns a 1-4 sentence brief into a full app: Planner expands to spec, Generator builds in sprints, Evaluator drives the running app with Playwright MCP and grades against hard thresholds.
why_relevant: Almost the owner's pipeline (ticket → plan → build → independent Playwright evaluation). Concrete choices to copy: generator and evaluator negotiate a 'sprint contract' of testable behaviours before each sprint; evaluator does live browser interaction rather than screenshot judging; grading has hard per-criterion thresholds (product depth, functionality, visual design, code quality); Opus 4.5 version needed full context resets with structured handoffs to defeat 'context anxiety', Opus 4.6 version ran one continuous session with compaction.
claimed_results: Post dated 2026-03-24: Video Game Maker (Opus 4.5) solo run '20 minutes, $9' vs full harness '6 hours, $200'; Digital Audio Workstation (Opus 4.6) total '3 hours 50 minutes', '$124.70' — planner 4.7 min ($0.46), build rounds 2h07/1h02/10.9 min ($113.85 combined), QA rounds 8.8/6.8/9.6 min ($10.39 combined). Evaluator caught missing clip dragging, instrument panels and recording that solo generation missed.

name: Razorpay 'Slash' — internal ticket-to-merged-PR agent with reviewer sub-agents
one_line: Event Listener auto-assigns tickets; Launch Agents write/test/PR (single-repo, batch, multi-repo, clean-slate modes); Slash Reviewer runs specialised sub-agents (bug detection, security, code quality, design system, i18n, pre-mortem) with repo-specific scoring and false-positive filtering; MCP/CLI gateway to 15+ internal systems with scoped permissions.
why_relevant: Strongest documented production adoption found for owner questions (1)+(3)+(4): unattended ticket→PR at scale with independent reviewer agents gating merge, a third of PRs merged with no human. Verification is review-agent + CI based, not held-out tests.
claimed_results: Post dated 2026-05-18: 'Tens of thousands of agent sessions, thousands of PRs created and merged every month, and over a third of them merged without a human in the loop'; PRs 'from about 100 a week to about 1,000 a week inside a month'; zero-human merges 'from about 10 a week to about 100 a week in a couple of weeks'; 'About one in three code reviews flowing through Slash today is reviewed, scored, approved, and merged with no human comments'.

name: OpenAI — 'Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world'
one_line: Internal OpenAI product built with '0 lines of manually-written code': custom linters enforce architecture boundaries, docs/ is the system of record with quality grades, PRs get agent-to-agent review, background 'garbage collection' agents open refactor PRs against pattern drift.
why_relevant: Owner questions (1)+(4): the pre-condition Symphony assumes. Copyable mechanisms: ~100-line AGENTS.md as entry point with progressive disclosure into docs/; mechanical linters instead of prose rules; agents 'request additional specific agent reviews both locally and in the cloud' and 'iterate in a loop' until reviewers approve; scheduled GC tasks that 'scan for pattern deviations, update quality grades, and open targeted refactoring pull requests'; 20% of the week reserved for cleanup.
claimed_results: Page (fetched via reader proxy 2026-09-02; no publication date shown on page): 'a million lines of code', 'roughly 1,500 pull requests have been opened and merged', 'three engineers driving Codex' growing to 'seven engineers', '3.5 PRs per engineer per day', 'five months', 'hundreds of users internally', '1/10th the time it would have taken to write the code by hand'.
last_activity: 2026 (listed in fatihkc/awesome-agentic-engineering pushed 2026-09-01 and wdzhwsh4067 list pushed 2026-04-26)

name: Self-evolving Agentic Customer Support System at LinkedIn (arXiv 2608.10224)
one_line: Production self-evolving agent: RAG + 'evolutionary auto-prompting' + modular evaluation run as 'a closed-loop, versioned workflow with operational guardrails', explicitly 'without retraining foundation models'.
why_relevant: Owner question (2)+(4): the only randomised production A/B evidence found for fine-tuning-free self-evolution. Architecture choice to copy: prompts, retrieval and evaluators are versioned artefacts evolved offline against a fixed evaluation framework, then promoted — same shape as the owner's frozen known-bad corpus + gate.
claimed_results: Abstract (submitted 2026-08-10): 'In a two-week user-randomized A/B test on LinkedIn's production support traffic, the integrated self-evolved workflow increased QA self-serve by 9.0 percentage points, cancellation self-serve by 4.8 points, and routing accuracy by 30.6 points.'

name: CAID — 'Effective Strategies for Asynchronous Software Engineering Agents' (Geng & Neubig, arXiv 2603.21489)
one_line: Centralized Asynchronous Isolated Delegation: a lead delegates interdependent subtasks to workers in isolated git worktrees, integrates via branch-and-merge with test-based verification.
why_relevant: Owner question (1) with measured evidence: lead+teammates on long-horizon multi-subtask builds beats single agent, and the paper isolates *which* coordination choices matter (centralised delegation, async execution, isolated workspaces, structured integration with test verification; 'Branch-and-merge emerges as a central coordination mechanism'). Evaluated on whole-library building (Commit0) — the closest benchmark to 'build me this app'.
claimed_results: Abstract (v1 2026-03-23, v2 2026-07-08): '25.6% absolute accuracy improvement over single-agent approaches' on PaperBench; '14.7% improvement on Python library development tasks (Commit0)'. No code link on abstract page.

name: Confucius Code Agent (CCA) — scalable scaffolding with persistent notes and a meta-agent (arXiv 2512.10398)
one_line: Production-grade SE agent scaffold: context management for long sessions, 'persistent note-taking system enabling cross-session learning', modular tool extensions, and a meta-agent that automates agent construction, evaluation and iterative refinement.
why_relevant: Owner question (2): notes persisted across sessions as the learning substrate (no fine-tuning) plus a meta-agent that iterates on the scaffold — the two halves of the owner's self-maintaining tier. Listed in both the self-evolving and long-horizon curated lists.
claimed_results: Abstract (v1 2025-12-11, v6 2026-02-03): 'SWE-Bench-Pro: 59% Resolve@1'. No code link on abstract page.

name: SWE-Exp: Experience-Driven Software Issue Resolution (arXiv 2507.23361)
