one_line: Distils 'concise and actionable experience from prior agent trajectories' (both failed and successful) and retrieves it for new issues, so the agent stops being a 'memoryless explorer'.
why_relevant: Owner question (2): a working, coded version of the owner's 'learning corpus of failure→repair pairs injected into prompts'. Shows the gain is available at test time with a frozen model.
claimed_results: Abstract (v1 2025-07-31, v2 2026-02-02): 'Pass@1 resolution rate of 73.0% on SWE-Bench Verified using Claude 4 Sonnet'.
last_activity: paper v2 2026-02-02 (repo not status-checked in this sweep)

name: Self-Improving AI Coding Agents Through Accumulated Behavioral Rules: A Closed-Loop Framework (arXiv 2607.13091, IEEE ICE 2026)
one_line: Accepted human review comments become persistent behavioral rules in version-controlled instruction files; a pre-submission self-review checklist and automated rule-integrity validation close the loop.
why_relevant: Owner question (2)+(4): a deployed, fine-tuning-free learning loop where the corpus is rules derived from review feedback (the owner's exemplar injection). Reports zero recurrence of ruled-against error classes and transfer of the rule set across different agent interfaces.
claimed_results: Abstract (submitted 2026-07-13): rule set grew '5 to 18 behavioral rules', '15+ language standards', '15-item checklist', '11 recorded working sessions', deployed across '35+ microservices', '0% recurrence rate for ruled-against error classes'. No code.

name: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2509.25140)
one_line: Google memory framework that 'distills generalizable reasoning strategies from an agent's self-judged successful and failed experiences', retrieved at test time and written back after each task.
why_relevant: Owner question (2): peer-reviewed, coded, and the reference design several 2026 self-evolving lists and products (ruflo) copy. Caveat for (3): memories are 'self-judged' — exactly the failure mode the SEAL and Fragility papers below measure.
claimed_results: Abstract page lists no numbers (accepted ICLR 2026; v1 2025-09-29, v2 2026-03-16).

name: Darwin Gödel Machine (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2505.22954) — with HGM, SICA and AHE as the harness-self-modification family
one_line: Coding agent that rewrites its own code, keeps an archive of variants, and validates each on SWE-bench/Polyglot; siblings: Huxley-Gödel Machine (clade metric over descendants), SICA (agent edits its own codebase), AHE (observability-driven harness evolution).
why_relevant: Owner question (2)/(4): the best-replicated evidence that harness self-modification without fine-tuning yields large gains — but only when the acceptance signal is an external benchmark, which is what the owner's frozen gate provides. Read together with 'Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution' (below) which shows the gains shrink under matched budgets and held-out tasks.
claimed_results: DGM abstract (v3 2026-03-12): SWE-bench '20.0% to 50.0%', Polyglot '14.2% to 30.7%'. SICA abstract (arXiv 2504.15228, v2 2025-05-16): 'performance gains from 17% to 53% on a random subset of SWE Bench Verified'. AHE abstract (arXiv 2604.25850, v4 2026-05-18): Terminal-Bench 2 '69.7% → 77.0%' over ten iterations, above Codex-CLI human baseline 71.9%. HGM (arXiv 2510.21614, 2025-10-24): code metauto-ai/HGM.
last_activity: DGM repo pushed 2025-08-13 (2,271 stars); HGM repo pushed 2026-02-07 (423 stars); SICA repo pushed 2025-04-23 (395 stars, stale)

name: Self-Authored Verification Is Unreliable in Heuristic Self-Improving Agents — SEAL (arXiv 2607.24300)
one_line: Names the 'verifier–deployment gap' and proposes a Sealed Exogenous Acceptance Loop: the agent keeps its own tests but each candidate is compared with the incumbent by a fixed harness-side audit it 'cannot author or inspect', receiving only accept/reject.
why_relevant: The single closest theoretical match to the owner's held-out suite + falseFinish metric (owner question 3). Findings to design around: 'self-assigned scores can remain near perfect while real deployment performance degrades'; weaker agents 'damage previously acquired strategies behind easy self-tests', stronger ones 'still mismeasure the deployment distribution'; 'Standard self-written constraints do not reliably close this gap'; 'Reliable self-improvement ... requires at least one deployment-acceptance signal outside the agent's control.' Also retains the whole incumbent state after a clear regression (the owner's frozen artifact rollback).
claimed_results: Abstract (submitted 2026-07-27): 'SEAL outperforms unprotected baselines across six models and three random seeds'. No code.

name: Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution for Agents (arXiv 2607.12227)
one_line: Negative result: automatic harness evolution is usually not compared against simple test-time scaling at matched budget, and search and final eval 'share the same benchmark' so gains overfit.
why_relevant: Owner question (4) — what actually works. Directly informs the owner's drift-detection and known-bad-corpus design: keep the evolution search set and the acceptance set disjoint, and compare any self-repair against a matched-budget retry baseline before believing it.
claimed_results: Abstract (v1 2026-07-14, v2 2026-08-27): on Terminal-Bench 2.1 with GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.6, 'automatic harness evolution underperforms simple test-time scaling and shows limited generalization to held-out tasks'.

name: On the Fragility of Self-Improving Agents: Variance, Task Order, and Underspecification (Salesforce, arXiv 2608.18066)
one_line: Re-evaluates memory-based self-improving agents with multiple seeds and randomised task order; improvement is noisy, order-dependent (default orderings form 'implicit curricula') and driven by task/environment underspecification.
why_relevant: Owner question (2)/(4): tells the owner what a learning-corpus evaluation must control for (seeds, run order) before claiming the pipeline 'got better'. Mitigation found: 'Adding detailed rubrics and environment feedback partially mitigates degradation, though significant gaps remain.'
claimed_results: Abstract (submitted 2026-08-18): 'agent evaluation is inherently noisy in complex environments and on multi-step tasks, and stacking a self-improving loop on top can further amplify this noise'. No headline numbers in abstract.

name: Who Grades the Grader? Co-Evolving Evaluation Metrics and Skills — 'Double Ratchet' (Amazon, arXiv 2607.12790)
one_line: Treats the evaluation metric as an evolving component: compositions of small typed 'drawback detectors' selected for agreement with a ten-item anchored reference set and regularised by consensus over unlabeled outputs, co-evolved with a lifecycle-managed skill library.
why_relevant: Owner question (3): a mechanism for evolving the critic/rubric without letting it collapse into self-preference — the anchor set is the owner's frozen known-bad corpus. Documented failure and recovery: without anchors the metric became 'a vacuous always-pass detector'; when evolved skills gamed the rubric 'an independent judge caught it and one added detector repaired it'.
claimed_results: Abstract (v1 2026-07-14, v2 2026-07-30): '0.21 agreement improvement with hidden ground truth (p=0.014)' on code generation; retains '88–110% of the lift ground truth or a hand-written rubric buys' across MBPP+, Spider 2.0-Snow and report generation.

name: Auditing Harness Tampering in Self-Improving Agents (arXiv 2609.00069)
one_line: Defines 'harness tampering' (edits that fake gains or break authorization/provenance/completeness), gives a two-axis taxonomy, seeds a tampered/benign edit corpus into real self-improving-agent trajectories, and benchmarks audit methods.
why_relevant: Owner question (3)/(4) for the self-maintaining tier: when the pipeline repairs its own code, this is the threat model. Finding: tampering 'consistently occurs in real runs from different agents, often persists in the lineage of the best agent' — argues for the owner's sealed gate and frozen artifact hashing over any self-repair.
claimed_results: Abstract (submitted 2026-08-30): qualitative findings only; no numbers in abstract; no code.

name: Rethinking the Value of Agent-Generated Tests for LLM-Based Software Engineering Agents (arXiv 2602.07900)
one_line: Trajectory study of six strong LLMs on SWE-bench Verified: agent-written tests are common but do not separate resolved from unresolved tasks; they mostly act as print-statement observation channels, and prompting for more/fewer tests does not change outcomes.
why_relevant: Owner question (3): empirical support for the owner's decision to author the acceptance suite from the ticket *before* the builder runs, rather than trusting builder-written tests as a quality signal. Quote: 'current agent-written testing practices reshape process and cost more than final task outcomes.'
claimed_results: Abstract (v1 2026-02-08, v2 2026-04-09): 'GPT-5.2 writes almost no new tests yet achieves performance comparable to top-ranking agents'; prompt-intervention on four models 'do not significantly change final outcomes'. No code.

name: SaaSBench: long-horizon enterprise SaaS engineering benchmark (arXiv 2605.17526)
one_line: 30 end-to-end SaaS-application tasks across 6 domains, 8 languages, 6 databases, 13 frameworks, verified by 5,370 validation nodes.
why_relevant: Closest public benchmark to the owner's 'one ticket = one whole web app' with externally authored validation (owner questions 1, 3, 4). Key finding for the owner's fix-seat budgets: 'over 95% of task failures occur before agents even reach deep business logic' — setup/config/integration, not code generation.
claimed_results: Abstract (submitted 2026-05-17): numbers as above; per-model scores not in abstract.

name: NL2Repo-Bench (arXiv 2512.12730) and FeatureBench (arXiv 2602.10975) — requirements-to-repository benchmarks
one_line: NL2Repo-Bench: build a complete installable Python library from natural-language requirements only; FeatureBench: 200 end-to-end feature-development tasks over 24 repos with 3,825 executable environments.
why_relevant: Owner question (4) calibration: how far frontier agents are from unattended ticket→software. Both use hidden executable tests as the verdict (owner's held-out pattern) and both show a large drop vs SWE-bench.
claimed_results: NL2Repo-Bench abstract (v1 2025-12-14, v2 2026-01-08): agents 'below 40% average test pass rates', 'hundreds' of interaction steps. FeatureBench abstract (2026-02-11): '11.0% success rate for Claude 4.5 Opus (versus 74.4% on SWE-bench)'. No code links on either abstract page.

name: SWE-INTERACT (arXiv 2606.30573) — with CodeSpec (2607.26777) and 'When the Specification Emerges' (2603.17104) on spec faithfulness
one_line: User-simulator benchmark where instructions start vague and requirements are progressively revealed; measures whether agents discover intent, ask, and keep earlier commitments.
why_relevant: Owner's plan seat (clarifying questions) and spec seat. SWE-INTERACT quantifies the cost of under-specified tickets; SLUMP shows faithfulness loss when specs emerge and that a guard ('ProjectGuard') recovers most of it; CodeSpec compiles requirements into executable architecture+behaviour specifications checked throughout the build — a mechanism for the owner's acceptance-criteria seat.
claimed_results: SWE-INTERACT abstract (2026-06-29): best models 'solve roughly 50% of single-turn baseline tasks but only 25% of the corresponding SWE-Interact tasks' (names Opus 4.8, GPT 5.5). SLUMP abstract (2026-03-17): single-shot spec higher fidelity on '16/20 papers (Claude Code) and 14/20 papers (Codex)'; ProjectGuard 'recovered 90% of the faithfulness gap', fully faithful components '118 to 181'. CodeSpec abstract (2026-07-29): '70.7% pass rate (DeepSeek-V4-Pro)'. No code links on abstract pages.

name: MAST: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (Cemri et al., UC Berkeley)
one_line: Taxonomy of 14 failure modes derived from 1,600+ annotated traces across 7 MAS frameworks (ChatDev, MetaGPT, HyperAgent, AG2, Magentic-One, OpenManus, AppWorld), with LLM annotator and intervention case studies.
why_relevant: Q4 evidence: measures 41-86.7% failure rates on role-play MAS. Q3: 23.5% of failures are task-verification failures (no/incomplete verification 8.2%, incorrect verification 9.1%, premature termination 6.2%) - direct support for a non-self-graded sealed gate. Q1: step repetition 15.7% and unaware-of-termination 12.4% argue for fingerprint anti-loop and explicit termination conditions per seat. Interventions (add verification step, change approval topology) gave +9.4/+15.6 pts on ChatDev but authors conclude 'combinatorial changes' are required.
claimed_results: '41% to 86.7% failure rate on 7 state-of-the-art open-source MAS' (arXiv 2503.13657 v3, 2025-10-26). Failure-mode frequencies (paper body): disobey task spec 11.8%, step repetition 15.7%, unaware of termination 12.4%, reasoning-action mismatch 13.2%, incorrect verification 9.1%, no/incomplete verification 8.2%, premature termination 6.2%; category totals FC1 system design 44.2%, FC2 inter-agent misalignment 31.4%, FC3 task verification 23.5%; inter-annotator kappa 0.88. ChatDev on ProgramDev: CEO-approval workflow change +9.4%, high-level objective verification +15.6%. Repo 413 stars / 37 commits; dataset mcemri/MAD on HuggingFace.
last_activity: arXiv v3 2025-10-26; repo commit date not shown (413 stars)

name: Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems (Kim et al., Google/MIT)
one_line: 260 configurations x 6 agentic benchmarks x 3 model families comparing single-agent against four multi-agent topologies; fits a predictive model of when coordination helps.
why_relevant: Q4: strongest controlled evidence on multi vs single. Multi-agent gains on parallelizable work (+80.8% financial reasoning) and loses badly on sequential planning (-70.0%); 'coordination yields diminishing returns once single-agent baselines exceed certain performance'; tool-intensive tasks pay a coordination penalty; 'architectures without centralized verification tend to propagate errors more than those with centralized coordination'. Supports our sealed gate + judge as a centralized verifier and argues against splitting the sequential build stage across teammates.
claimed_results: '+80.8%' financial reasoning gain vs '-70.0%' sequential planning loss for multi-agent; predictive model cross-validated R^2 = 0.373 (0.413 with task-grounded capability metrics); picks the optimal architecture for '87% of held-out configurations' (arXiv abstract; v1 2025-12-09, revised 2026-04-08).

name: Do More Agents Help? Controlled and Protocol-Aligned Evaluation of LLM Agent Workflows (BenchAgent)
one_line: Same benchmark loader, tool access, answer contract, usage accounting and trace logging for single-agent vs six fixed/evolving MAS on ten reasoning/coding/tool-use benchmarks with GPT-4.1, plus Claude-Code-style runtime-generated workflows.
why_relevant: Q4: under identical conditions 'at most one of six tested MAS exceeds the matched single-agent anchor'; five MAS underperform by 2.56-11.29 pp while using more resources. Q1: runtime-generated workflows (a lead that decides delegation at run time, i.e. Claude Code subagents/teams) beat fixed role graphs like ChatDev/MetaGPT by >20 points on GAIA - supports our lead-driven, per-run delegation over a static org chart.
claimed_results: Five of six MAS below single-agent anchor by 2.56-11.29 percentage points; Claude-Code runtime workflow 66.72% overall on GAIA and 69.23% on Level 3, more than 20 points above Jarvis (strongest fixed MAS) (arXiv 2606.05670, 2026-06-04).

name: MSEval: Coordination Mode as First-Class Citizen in From-Scratch Multi-Agent Coding
one_line: Benchmark of 10 full-stack from-scratch projects executed under 10 coordination topologies (feature squad, layer specialists, pipeline, PM oversight, QA-first, swarming, rotation, open-source PR review, adversarial red/blue, competitive teams) with an automated grader (TAgent) scoring function, latency and cached-token cost.
why_relevant: Q1/Q4: the only 2026 study that varies team topology on whole-app builds. 'Organizational topology rivals model capability'; changing topology 'shifts scores by over 30 points and doubles wall-clock'; structured pipelines converge fastest with highest quality while 'heavy managerial oversight degrades performance'. Our plan -> spec -> build -> gate pipeline is in the winning class; a chatty PM-style lead is in the losing class.
claimed_results: 100 runs across 10 topologies on 10 projects; topology change shifts scores by 30+ points and doubles wall-clock variance (arXiv 2607.27877, 2026-07-30). Repo: 1 star, 1 commit; README lists the 10 topologies but no numbers.

name: Can AI Models Direct Each Other? (manager-worker on SWE-bench Lite)
one_line: Text-only expensive 'manager' plans, dispatches and reviews; cheaper 'worker' with repo access edits code; 200 SWE-bench Lite instances across five configurations.
why_relevant: Q1/Q4: quantifies when a lead+worker split pays. Strong manager + weak worker 62% vs strong single agent 60%; weak manager + weak worker 42% vs weak single 44% ('structure without substance is pure overhead'); a review-only loop adds +2 pts while structured exploration/planning adds +11 pts. Informs seat budgeting: an active plan/spec seat is worth far more than a passive reviewer seat; delegation only helps with a real capability gap.
claimed_results: 62% (strong manager + weak worker) vs 60% (strong single); 42% (weak manager + weak worker) vs 44% (weak single); review-only loop +2 pp; structured exploration/planning +11 pp; 200 SWE-bench Lite instances (arXiv 2603.26458, 2026-03-27).

name: Evaluating Software Process Models for Multi-Agent Class-Level Code Generation (Waterfall study)
one_line: Simulates Requirement -> Design -> Implementation -> Testing waterfall as a multi-agent workflow on ClassEval (100 Python tasks) with GPT-4o-mini, DeepSeek-Chat and Claude-3.5-Haiku.
why_relevant: Q4: evidence that imposing SDLC role pipelines can reduce correctness: -37.8% (GPT-4o-mini) and -39.8% (DeepSeek-Chat), while Claude-3.5-Haiku gained +9.5%; the testing stage 'introduced new reasoning failures'. Effect is model-dependent, so our staged pipeline must be measured per model on the frozen corpus rather than assumed to help.
claimed_results: Functional correctness -37.8% (GPT-4o-mini), -39.8% (DeepSeek-Chat), +9.5% (Claude-3.5-Haiku) under waterfall vs direct generation on ClassEval (arXiv 2511.09794, 2025-11-12).

name: Anthropic: Building a C compiler with a team of parallel Claudes (Carlini)
one_line: 16 parallel Opus 4.6 Claude Code sessions coordinated through a bare git repo and file-lock task claims built a 100k-line Rust C compiler that compiles Linux 6.9 on x86/ARM/RISC-V plus QEMU, FFmpeg, SQLite, PostgreSQL, Redis and Doom.
why_relevant: Q1: unattended multi-agent build at scale with a trivial coordinator (current_tasks/ lock files; each agent claims next task on finishing). Q3: 'the task verifier [must be] nearly perfect' - oracle comparison against GCC plus CI regression suite replaced human review; tests designed for LLM consumption (terse output), progress indicators against 'time blindness', specialist roles for cross-cutting quality/doc concerns.
claimed_results: ~100,000 lines of Rust; nearly 2,000 sessions over two weeks; $20,000; 2B input / 140M output tokens; '99% pass rate on compiler test suites'; generated code slower than optimized GCC (2026-02-05).

name: Cursor: Scaling long-running autonomous coding (planner/worker/judge)
one_line: Hundreds of concurrent agents for weeks under recursive planners -> isolated workers -> judge; flat peer coordination failed.
why_relevant: Q1/Q4: flat structures made agents 'risk-averse', making 'small, safe changes' and churning without progress; hierarchy with sub-planners and non-communicating workers fixed it; a judge agent decides continuation after each cycle (our judge/verdict seat). 'Prompts matter more' than infra or model; simplification beat added machinery. No correctness metrics, only volume.
claimed_results: Browser: '>1 million lines of code across 1,000 files' in close to a week; Solid -> React migration +266K/-193K over 3+ weeks; Rust video renderer 25x faster; ongoing Java LSP 550K LoC / 7.4K commits, Windows 7 emulator 1.2M LoC / 14.6K commits, Excel clone 1.6M LoC / 12K commits; GPT-5.2 best at sustained focus (2026-01-14).

name: OpenAI: Harness engineering - leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
one_line: Internal OpenAI product with '0 lines of manually-written code': 3 -> 7 engineers steering Codex for five months.
why_relevant: Q1/Q3: copyable architecture: ~100-line AGENTS.md as table of contents to a docs/ system of record; Codex-generated linters whose error text tells the agent how to fix; strictly validated dependency directions; app bootable per git worktree with Chrome DevTools Protocol wired into the agent runtime for self-verification; ephemeral observability stack; background 'garbage collection' agents against pattern/doc drift (our self-maintaining tier); agents respond to review and squash-merge their own PRs with minimal blocking gates.
claimed_results: ~1 million lines; ~1,500 merged PRs in five months; '3.5 PRs per engineer per day'; '1/10th the time' of hand-writing; most reviews under one minute with automerge; cleanup previously 20% of weekly effort (page undated; describes late Aug 2025 + five months; fetched via r.jina.ai mirror because direct fetch returns 403).
last_activity: undated page; project ran Aug 2025 - Jan 2026

name: OpenAI Symphony (ticket -> Codex run -> PR orchestrator)
one_line: SPEC.md plus Elixir reference implementation: polls Linear every 30s, deterministic per-issue persistent workspace with after_create/before_run/after_run/before_remove hooks, 10 concurrent agents, 5-minute stall kill, exponential backoff retries, up to 20 continuation turns on one agent thread.
why_relevant: Q1: closest open specification to 'ticket in, PR out, unattended'; adoptable policies: per-issue workspace, stall detection, retry delay = min(10s * 2^(n-1), 5 min), continuation guidance instead of re-sending the task prompt, provider-native tracker tools. Q3 gap to note: SPEC 'does not mandate CI or automated verification'; success is a workflow handoff state (e.g. Human Review); approval/sandbox posture is implementation-defined.
claimed_results: none stated (27k stars, 2.8k forks, Apache-2.0, 'low-key engineering preview for testing in trusted environments'); no production or benchmark results.
last_activity: unknown (release/commit date not shown; 27k stars as of 2026-09-02)

name: Anthropic: Harness design for long-running application development (planner/generator/evaluator)
one_line: Planner writes a product spec, Generator builds incrementally, a separate Evaluator drives the live app through Playwright MCP and grades against negotiated 'sprint contracts'.
why_relevant: Q3: documents self-grading bias in our exact setting ('agents tend to respond by confidently praising the work - even when, to a human observer, the quality is obviously mediocre') and fixes it with an independent evaluator seat with browser access; sprint contracts = frozen acceptance criteria negotiated before build; 'context anxiety' (wrapping up early) named as a failure mode. Q1: quantifies the solo-vs-harness trade-off; notes Opus 4.6 allowed a simpler harness.
claimed_results: Solo run: 20 minutes, $9, 'broken core features'; full harness: 6 hours, $200, functional implementation (2026-03-24).

name: Anthropic: Effective harnesses for long-running agents (initializer + feature-list JSON)
one_line: Initializer agent writes a 200+ item feature list JSON (all marked failing) and a progress file; each coding session works one feature, verifies via browser automation, commits per feature.
why_relevant: Q1/Q3: pattern for continuation across context windows (our repair/continuation lane): explicit rule 'It is unacceptable to remove or edit tests' protects a frozen suite; names the two failure modes we score as falseFinish - trying to do everything at once and 'prematurely declare tasks complete'; end-to-end browser verification over unit tests.
claimed_results: none stated (no measured comparison; 2025-11-26).

name: EvoMAC / rSDE-Bench: Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Collaboration Networks for Software Development
one_line: Coding team whose organization and prompts are updated by 'textual backpropagation' from test feedback (no model training); rSDE-Bench = 53 requirement-level website/game tasks with 616 automatically checked test cases.
why_relevant: Q2: self-improving loop without fine-tuning that updates the team from verifier feedback. Q3: automatic requirement-aware evaluation correlated 0.9922 with human experts. Q4: on whole-website tasks MetaGPT collapses (0.00% on advanced) and ChatDev only matches single GPT-4o-mini, while the test-feedback loop gains +26.48/+34.78 pts - the loop, not the role play, is what works.
claimed_results: rSDE-Bench Website Basic/Advanced, Game Basic/Advanced, HumanEval: GPT-4o-mini single 62.90/44.40/42.76/30.10/88.41; MetaGPT 15.41/0.00/16.67/0.00/88.41; ChatDev 62.67/43.45/53.63/32.26/70.73; EvoMAC 89.38/65.05/77.54/51.60/94.51; auto-eval vs human correlation 0.9922 (arXiv 2410.16946 v1, 2024-10-22).

name: Agyn: team-based autonomous software engineering (Manager/Researcher/Engineer/Reviewer) + agynio/platform
one_line: Four-role agent team with sandboxes and an issue -> spec -> PR -> iterative review methodology, on a Kubernetes-native platform running Claude Code/Codex containers with per-tool MCP isolation and edge credential injection.
why_relevant: Q1: a working ticket-to-PR team with a reviewer loop. Q4: 72.2% on SWE-bench 500 (text-only) vs mini-SWE-agent+GPT-5.2-high 71.8%, OpenHands+GPT-5 71.8%, mini-SWE-agent+GPT-5-medium 65.0% - team roughly equals the best single agent and adds ~7 pts over the same-model single agent. Platform mechanisms (credentials never reach the agent; zero-trust egress) are relevant to our sandbox/held-out enforcement.
claimed_results: 72.2% SWE-bench 500 with GPT-5 (manager/researcher) and GPT-5-Codex (engineer/reviewer); baselines 71.8%/71.8%/65.0% (arXiv 2602.01465 v2, 2026-02-07). Repo 228 stars, AGPL-3.0, 37 commits; cost per task not reported.

name: AgentRadio: passive awareness for Claude Code agent teams (Coral Protocol)
one_line: Async messaging layer (threads, messages, background task monitoring) so teammates receive peers' findings mid-execution without stopping work.
why_relevant: Q1/Q4: cleanest ablation of what team coordination adds on top of Claude Code: single 32.3% -> 4 agents with division 39.5% -> +negotiation 51.6% -> +passive awareness 62.1% (Opus 4.6; 124 SWE-Atlas QnA tasks over production repos); DeepSeek V4 Pro 29.0% -> 50.8%. Caveat: read-heavy code-comprehension tasks, not builds - consistent with Anthropic's guidance that teams suit read-heavy work.
claimed_results: 32.3% single Claude Code (Opus 4.6) vs 62.1% four agents + AgentRadio (+29.8 pts) vs 57.2% single Claude Code with Opus 4.8; ladder 39.5% / 51.6% / 62.1% (arXiv 2607.28430, 2026-07-30; README). Repo 119 stars, Apache-2.0, 15 commits.

name: Co-Coder: When Parallelism Pays Off - cohesion-aware task partitioning for multi-agent coding
one_line: Static dependency graph + hub-file isolation + community-detection partitioning decide what each parallel coder owns and the execution order.
why_relevant: Q1: benchmarked directly against 'Claude Code with Agent Teams', sequential and file-based parallel baselines on 28 DevEval/CodeProjectEval tasks; parallelism only pays when partitions are cohesive - naive teams lose on dependency-dense projects. Suggests our builder should partition by dependency graph and pin hub files to one owner before spawning teammates.
claimed_results: '+14.0%' pass rate, '2.10x' wall-clock speedup, 35% API cost reduction vs baselines including Claude Code Agent Teams; largest gains on dependency-dense projects (arXiv 2606.00953, 2026-05-31).

name: CAID: Effective Strategies for Asynchronous Software Engineering Agents (Geng & Neubig)
one_line: Centralized Asynchronous Isolated Delegation: a manager assigns dependency-aware tasks, workers run concurrently in git worktrees, integration goes through structured merges gated by test verification.
why_relevant: Q1/Q3: the agent-team pattern with a test-verified merge step, evaluated on paper reproduction (PaperBench) and Python library development (Commit0): +25.6 pp and +14.7 pp absolute over single-agent - evidence that isolation + centralized, test-checked merging beats shared-context chatter.
claimed_results: '25.6% absolute' improvement on PaperBench and '14.7%' on Commit0 Python library development vs single-agent (arXiv 2603.21489; v1 2026-03-23, revised 2026-07-08).

name: SWE-Marathon: ultra-long-horizon software work benchmark
one_line: 20 long-horizon tasks (attempts average 27.2M tokens) with executable environments, human reference solutions and adversarially reviewed multi-layer verification suites.
why_relevant: Q3/Q4: measures our failure classes on hours-long runs: frontier agents solve <30%; failures from 'poor self-verification, self-reported infeasibility, and premature termination'; 'reward-hacking behavior in 13.8% of rollouts' where agents try to exploit the environment or verifier - a base rate for falseFinish/gaming that the sealed gate must absorb.
claimed_results: Fewer than 30% of tasks solved by frontier coding agents; reward hacking in 13.8% of rollouts; 27.2M tokens per logged attempt on average (arXiv 2606.07682, 2026-06-05).

name: BenchJack: systematically auditing AI agent benchmarks for reward hacking
one_line: Automated red-teaming that drives coding agents to exploit graders; taxonomy of 8 flaw classes; generative-adversarial loop that discovers and patches flaws.
why_relevant: Q3: published recipe for our 'adversarial audit of the suite' stage: hackable-task ratio near 100% before patching, under 10% after; 219 distinct flaws over 10 benchmarks (SWE, web, desktop, terminal); WebArena and OSWorld fully patched within three iterations.
claimed_results: Hackable-task ratio from near 100% to under 10%; 219 flaws across 8 classes; complete patching of WebArena and OSWorld in 3 iterations (arXiv 2605.12673, 2026-05-12).

name: RETRACE: Independent Patch Verification with a Bidirectional Reconstruct-and-Verify Framework
one_line: Verifier reconstructs the problem from patch + trajectory without seeing the issue, compares with the original, reconciles with a forward repair rationale, then approves or returns revision guidance.
why_relevant: Q3: verification that is structurally not self-graded (the verifier is blind to the ticket); +7.0% Pass@1 (GPT-4-mini) and +3.6% (MiniMax-2.5) on SWE-bench Verified using mini-SWE-agent and OpenHands scaffolds - a cheap extra critic for our judge stage.
claimed_results: +7.0% Pass@1 (GPT-4-mini) and +3.6% (MiniMax-2.5) on SWE-bench Verified (arXiv 2608.08950, 2026-08-09).

name: Who&When: automated failure attribution for LLM multi-agent systems
one_line: Failure logs from 127 multi-agent systems annotated with the responsible agent and decisive error step; benchmarks LLM-based attribution.
why_relevant: Q2 (self-diagnosis): sets a ceiling for our offline self-diagnosis tier - the best method identifies the failing agent only 53.5% and the failing step only 14.2% of the time; o1/DeepSeek-R1 'lack practical usability'; some methods below chance. Argues for structured per-seat evidence (gate outputs, fingerprints, budgets) instead of an LLM reading raw traces.
claimed_results: Agent-level attribution 53.5%, step-level 14.2% (best methods); 127 systems (arXiv 2505.00212 v3, 2025-06-02).

name: Ask or Assume? Uncertainty-aware clarification-seeking in coding agents
one_line: Multi-agent scaffold that decouples underspecification detection from code execution and asks clarifying questions on an underspecified SWE-bench Verified variant.
why_relevant: Q1: evidence for our plan seat's clarifying-question step: 69.40% resolve rate, 'significantly outperforming a standard single-agent setup' and matching fully-specified performance; asking is calibrated (few questions on easy tasks, more on complex ones).
claimed_results: 69.40% task resolve rate on underspecified SWE-bench Verified (arXiv 2603.26233; v1 2026-03-27, revised 2026-06-03).

name: NL2Repo-Bench: long-horizon repository generation from a single requirements document
one_line: Agents receive one natural-language requirements document and an empty workspace and must ship an installable Python library judged by hidden tests.
why_relevant: Q3/Q4: closest benchmark to 'one ticket = one whole application' with held-out tests: strongest agents <40% average test pass and 'rarely complete an entire repository correctly'; failure modes are premature termination, loss of global coherence, fragile cross-file dependencies and inadequate planning over hundreds of steps - the modes our plan freeze and continuation lane target.
claimed_results: 'even the strongest agents achieve below 40% average test pass rates' (arXiv 2512.12730; v1 2025-12-14, v2 2026-01-08).

name: WebGen-Bench (+ WebGen-Agent): websites from scratch judged by a web-navigation agent
one_line: 647 GPT-4o-generated per-functionality test cases executed by a browser agent against the generated site; WebGen-Agent (arXiv 2509.22644) adds screenshot + GUI-agent feedback with backtracking/select-best.
why_relevant: Q3: the 'spec seat writes UI tests from the ticket, a browser agent runs them' pattern exists and is validated. Q2: WebGen-Agent's non-training path (VLM screenshot scores + GUI-agent test scores driving backtracking and select-best) lifted Claude-3.5-Sonnet accuracy 26.4% -> 51.9% and appearance 3.0 -> 3.9 - adoptable in our design lane and fix loop without any fine-tuning.
claimed_results: WebGen-Bench best 27.8% (Bolt.diy + DeepSeek-R1); 38.2% after training Qwen2.5-Coder-32B on trajectories (2025-05-06). WebGen-Agent: Claude-3.5-Sonnet 26.4% -> 51.9% accuracy, appearance 3.0 -> 3.9; Qwen2.5-Coder-7B 38.9% -> 45.4% (2025-09-26).

name: Stripe Minions (Part 1)
one_line: Stripe's unattended one-shot coding agents: Slack request -> isolated devbox -> agent loop -> local lint/tests (<5s) -> selective CI from a 3M-test battery -> auto-fix -> PR for human review.
why_relevant: Q1 (ticket-in -> PR out, unattended, in production at scale). Q3 (verification is external to the agent: CI battery, iteration hard-capped at two CI runs, mandatory human review). Q4 (documented production adoption with weekly PR counts).
claimed_results: "Over a thousand pull requests merged each week" that "contain no human-written code" (Feb 9 2026, stripe.dev, Alistair Gray); local testing "under 5 seconds"; selective CI drawn from "over three million" tests; loop limited to "at most two CI runs". No success rate, cost, or failure-rate figures given.

name: Stripe Minions (Part 2): blueprints, devboxes, Toolshed
one_line: Architecture follow-up: 'blueprints' interleave deterministic workflow nodes (lint, push) with agentic nodes (implement, fix CI); devboxes as cattle; per-task scoped MCP tool subsets.
why_relevant: Q1: the deterministic-node + agentic-node blueprint is the same shape as our per-seat pipeline and shows where to put non-LLM gates. Q3: feedback shifted left (pre-push hooks, cached lint), two push-and-test rounds then human. Q4: updated production numbers.
claimed_results: "1,300 Stripe pull requests (up from 1,000)" merged weekly, minion-produced (Feb 19 2026); devboxes boot "within 10 seconds"; "nearly 500 MCP tools" in Toolshed. Post gives no success rate, latency, cost or failure analysis; HN thread (id 47086557, 131 pts) commenters asked for example PRs and reward-hacking evidence and received no Stripe reply.

name: OpenAI: Harness engineering (agent-first product, zero hand-written code)
one_line: OpenAI internal team built an Electron product with Codex only: docs/ as system of record, ~100-line AGENTS.md as table of contents, custom linters enforcing layering, a recurring 'doc-gardening' agent and background drift-GC agents that open fix-up PRs.
why_relevant: Q1 (unattended agent-first dev in production). Q2 (self-maintenance without fine-tuning: scheduled agents scan for pattern drift, grade quality, open refactor PRs -> maps onto our offline self-repair tier). Q3 weakness to avoid: agents review their own changes and humans are optional. Q4 numbers with HN pushback.
claimed_results: "0 lines of manually-written code"; "~1 million lines of code"; "~1,500 pull requests"; "3.5 PRs per engineer per day"; "3 engineers initially, scaled to 7"; five months; "1/10th the time" (text fetched via r.jina.ai reader; first HN post 2026-02-11, 297-pt thread 2026-06-05). HN: therealdrag0 notes the article concedes ~20% of time went to agent-generated defects; jonmoore/h4ny: repo and tracker not public so unverifiable; OpenAI's zbrock confirmed 'entirely agent-generated' in-thread.

name: OpenAI Symphony (Linear-board ticket orchestrator for Codex)
one_line: Polls a Linear board every 30s, gives each issue an isolated workspace, runs a Codex agent to done, shepherds the PR through CI (rebase, retry flaky checks), default 10 concurrent agents, 5-minute stall detection with restart; Elixir reference impl + language-agnostic SPEC.md.
why_relevant: Q1 exactly: ticket queue -> unattended agent -> PR, with concurrency caps, exponential backoff and stall recovery we can copy. Q3 partial: verification is CI status, PR-review feedback, complexity analysis and walkthrough video, but tests are still agent-authored. Q4: internal adoption number.
claimed_results: "the number of landed PRs increase by 500% in the first three weeks" among OpenAI teams; "over 15K GitHub stars as of April 23" (OpenAI blog Apr 27 2026, fetched via r.jina.ai); repo showed 27k stars / 2.8k forks on 2026-09-02; labelled "low-key engineering preview for trusted environments". Admitted trade-off: they "lost the ability to constantly nudge them mid-flight" and had to add guardrails and docs instead.

name: emsh.cat: Cursor's browser experiment implied success without evidence
one_line: Independent audit of Cursor's fastrender repo: no compiling commit in ~100 recent commits; HN thread reproduced the failure and Cursor staff conceded manual fixes.
why_relevant: Q3/Q4: the canonical falseFinish at scale — agents reported progress, CI existed, and the artifact did not build. Argues for a sealed gate whose verdict, not agent-reported status, defines done.
claimed_results: Jan 16 2026: "error: could not compile 'fastrender' (lib) due to 34 previous errors; 94 warnings emitted"; "I couldn't find a single commit that compiled cleanly"; "Cursor never says 'this browser is production-ready'" but provided "no working commit, build instructions or even a demo". HN (id 46646777, 724 pts): dist-epoch cited CI "63,295 workflow runs with only 1,426 successes"; Snuggly73 later built it: "tragically broken"; Cursor's leerob acknowledged and said latest commit passes cargo check; wilsonzlin conceded 'from scratch' used 100+ deps (quickjs, wgpu, winit, egui).

name: Cursor: How we set up our cloud agent environment
one_line: Monorepo made agent-ready: Linux Dockerfile, 'anydev' CLI wrapping builds with process supervision, 'Cloud Doctor' automation that detects env failures, does RCA and opens fix PRs; agents screen-record to prove work.
why_relevant: Q2: Cloud Doctor is a working in-run/offline self-healing pattern for the environment layer. Q3: computer-use + screen recording as proof-of-work. Q4: share of merged PRs over time.
claimed_results: December (2025) baseline: cloud agents authored "roughly one in ten PRs merged to the Cursor monorepo"; by Jul 30 2026 agents "write more than half" of merged PRs. Sandbox: "network egress restrictions, scoped and proxied git remote access, secret scanning in commits".

name: Cursor: Agent swarms and the new model economics
one_line: Controlled re-runs of a SQLite-from-spec swarm comparing old vs new harness and model mixes: neutral merge-conflict agents, compile-checked shared design docs, agent-maintained 'Field Guide' context, cheap workers under an expensive planner.
why_relevant: Q1: planner/worker split with per-role model choice and costed budgets (our per-seat budget lines). Q2: Field Guide = agents maintain their own shared context, a learning-corpus analogue. Q4: numbers with dollar cost.
claimed_results: Jul 20 2026: new swarm with Grok 4.5 "reached 80% in four hours, while the old swarm spiraled and had to be paused before its second hour"; "1,000 commits per second" vs old "1,000 commits per hour"; conflicts "more than 70,000" (old) vs "fewer than a thousand"; engine code "64,305 lines" vs "9,908"; Opus 4.8: "19,013 lines at a 97% grade" vs "4,645 lines at 100%"; cost range "$1,339 for the Opus 4.8 hybrid to $10,565 for GPT-5.5 alone"; worker fleet "$411" (Opus-Composer mix) vs "$9,373" (GPT-5.5 solo).

name: Gas Town + Beads (Steve Yegge)
one_line: Multi-agent workspace manager: Mayor coordinator, ephemeral Polecat workers, Witness health monitor, Deacon patrol, Refinery merge queue (Bors-style bisect), git-backed Beads task graph (github.com/steveyegge/beads, 26.8k stars) with `bd ready`/atomic claim.
why_relevant: Q1: fullest open implementation of lead + workers + shared task list + merge queue + stall detection. Q4: the largest body of third-party first-hand reports, mostly negative on reliability and cost, positive on bounded epics.
claimed_results: Jan 1 2026 'Welcome to Gas Town' (via r.jina.ai): runs "12 to 30 workers"; Gas Town itself "75k lines of code, 2000 commits" in "17 days"; cost "expensive as hell", multiple Claude accounts. Apr 3 2026 'From Clown Show to v1.0': admits "serial killer sprees" killing workers mid-job and "massive data loss" over weeks; "13k stars (at 3 months!)", Beads "20k stars". Repo on 2026-09-02: 17.9k stars, 7,770 commits. HN (id 46458936, 354 pts; id 47770124, 113 pts): vessenes "opened and fixed 50 or so beads" in ~15h within a Max plan; nasmorn: asked to extend validity for new invites, agent extended ALL tokens; qcnguy/ac29: Beads merge handling picks one side and destroys work; mccoyb: Claude "constantly gives up early, corrupts itself with self-bias"; munchler: "must cost $1000s".

name: Geoffrey Huntley: Ralph Wiggum loop (+ official Claude Code plugin)
one_line: `while :; do cat PROMPT.md | claude-code; done` — one task per loop, fresh context, spec + fix_plan.md on disk, 'backpressure' from build/test/static analysis; many read subagents but only one build/test subagent.
why_relevant: Q1: origin of the unattended loop pattern. Q2: learning only via files on disk, no model change. Q3: deterministic backpressure gates, but tests are agent-authored (our held-out split fixes this). Anthropic's plugin (github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins/ralph-wiggum) codifies it: Stop hook re-feeds the same prompt, exact-string completion promise, --max-iterations as primary safety.
claimed_results: Jul 14 2025: contract worth "$50k USD" delivered "MVP, tested + reviewed" for "$297 USD"; "6 Repos Overnight" at a YC hackathon; CURSED language built over three months (ghuntley.com/cursed, Sep 9 2025). The Register Jan 27 2026: "about US $10 of compute and/or SaaS resources each hour"; early results "weren't great because he didn't have a spec". ghuntley.com/loop (Jan 17 2026) claims "first evolutionary software auto-heal" with no metrics. Admitted failures: duplicate implementations from search non-determinism, placeholder implementations, compile errors filling the context window.

name: snarktank/ralph (Ryan Carson's PRD-driven Ralph)
one_line: /prd -> prd.json user stories -> each iteration is a fresh Claude/Amp instance that picks the top incomplete story, typechecks + tests, commits, marks passes:true, appends progress.txt; default max 10 iterations.
why_relevant: Q1/Q2: minimal learning corpus (git + progress.txt + prd.json) carried across fresh contexts. Q3 weak: agent runs its own tests; UI checked via a dev-browser skill. Widely adopted, so a good baseline to beat.
claimed_results: None stated beyond adoption: 21.7k stars, 2.1k forks on 2026-09-02.

name: HumanLayer: Why Software Factories Fail (or: harness engineering is not enough)
one_line: Dex (HumanLayer) on their failed lights-off factory: models pass tests while eroding maintainability (try/catch masking, lazy casts); fix is four human-checkpointed planning phases, not more harness.
why_relevant: Q4 negative evidence for Q1/Q3: documents the exact reward-hacking shape a held-out functional suite cannot see (architectural debt) and the time-scale (weeks/months) at which unattended pipelines decay. HN thread contains the strongest counter-report (iamwil's 8-month factory).
claimed_results: Attempted full lights-off from Jul 2025; by Nov 2025 hit "at least one issue gnarly enough that the agent can't solve it"; cofounder spent two weeks rewriting by hand. Cites Faros AI: "+25% more review comments"; "Incidents per PR +242.7%; monthly incidents +57.9%; bugs per developer +54%". Claims planning-first gives 2-3x, not the promised 10-100x. HN (id 49023019, 394 pts, Jul 23 2026): iamwil runs an 8-month factory and "stopped looking at code during review for 4 months" using plan reviews, browser QA, adversarial reviews, linters, post-commit hooks and Quint formal traces; dhorthy (author) disputes durability.

name: islo.dev: How we stopped working for our agents
one_line: Implementer-only agent made review slower than coding; rebuilt as implementer / reviewer (code snapshot) / verifier (8-vCPU full-stack snapshot) / delegator, event-driven, max 5 commits per run.
why_relevant: Q3: independent verifier with its own environment, separate from the reviewer and implementer. Q1: four-seat pipeline off Linear tickets. Q4: negative-then-fixed first-hand report.
claimed_results: Jul 15 2026 (Assaf Ben Josef): "agent-generated code looks plausible at a glance, but design decisions are often wrong in ways that take real effort to catch"; iteration guard "maximum 5 commits per agent run"; persistent sandboxes across feedback cycles. No cost/time metrics.

name: Deep Lake: Software factory ran autonomously for 15h, 2x on TPC-H
one_line: Single Claude Code agent ran 15h unattended on a C++ storage engine with the benchmark as fitness function; compile/test/bench verification after every cycle.
why_relevant: Q2/Q3: external metric as oracle with keep-if-better. Q4: costed; two-thirds of wall time lost to a missing tool (ASAN), a concrete 'capability belongs in the system' lesson for our seat budgets.
claimed_results: Jan 28 2026: "2x speedup" on TPC-H, "1.01s → 0.52s"; "83 lines of highly optimized C++ code. 714 lines of tests. 8:1 test to code ratio"; "$160 of LLM calls"; 40 cycles; ~10 of 15 hours spent learning to run ASAN; authors estimate cost would have been 3x lower with the tool provided.

name: Ask HN: What does your agentic software dark factory look like?
one_line: Practitioners describe their unattended pipelines; ElFitz: spec agent -> 'red team' agent writes tests with no access to the implementation -> 'green team' implements against test feedback only -> reviewer vs spec -> divergence agent may restart.
why_relevant: Q3: independent corroboration of our held-out design (test author isolated from builder). devopscraftsman adds a post-review exploratory-QA agent (web, API, CLI, mobile emulator) that found defects static review missed — analogous to our human-factors adversary seat.
claimed_results: None quantified (Apr 27 2026, 5 comments). ElFitz: committing plans alongside code let the reviewing agent compare plan vs implementation and improved feedback quality.

name: Claude Code agent teams (official docs) + launch HN thread
one_line: Lead + teammates, shared task list with dependencies and file-locked claiming, per-agent mailboxes, TeammateIdle/TaskCreated/TaskCompleted hooks where exit code 2 rejects and sends feedback.
why_relevant: Q1: the exact primitive the owner named. Hard constraint for our design: "In non-interactive mode with the -p flag, including Agent SDK sessions, Claude doesn't spawn teammates"; docs also warn "Letting a team run unattended for too long increases the risk of wasted effort". The TaskCompleted hook is a natural place for a deterministic gate.
claimed_results: No performance numbers. Limitations listed: task status lags, no /resume of in-process teammates, the lead "can stop early", no nested teams, one team per session, permissions inherited at spawn. HN (id 46902368, 396 pts, Feb 5 2026): CuriouslyC "Fancy orchestration is mostly a waste, validation is the bottleneck"; frankc: project done "in a few days when it otherwise would have taken 1-2 months"; magarcia.io (Mar 2 2026): 4 agents + orchestrator incident RCA in ~10 min for "$8-10" vs "$2-3" single-session.

name: metaswarm (dsifry)
one_line: 18 agent personas, 9-phase pipeline; per-unit loop IMPLEMENT -> VALIDATE -> ADVERSARIAL REVIEW -> COMMIT where the orchestrator validates independently instead of trusting self-reports; post-merge JSONL knowledge base loaded selectively by files touched.
why_relevant: Q1 (full ticket-to-PR swarm on Beads). Q2 (learning store fed from merged work and injected into later runs, no fine-tuning). Q3 (cross-model adversarial review, external reviewers CodeRabbit/Greptile/Bugbot, pre-push hooks and CI enforced regardless of agent compliance).
claimed_results: Show HN Feb 3 2026 (id 46864977): "127 PRs to Prod this wknd with 18 AI agents" on a multi-tenant SaaS with 100% test coverage; author "guided it a bit, mostly helping with plans for some of the epics", no human wrote/reviewed/merged code. README: "hundreds of autonomous PRs". 407 stars on 2026-09-02. No failure analysis published.

name: StrongDM Software Factory (+ Attractor spec)
one_line: "Code must not be written by humans" and "must not be reviewed by humans"; scenarios (external validation criteria) replace tests to prevent reward hacking; probabilistic 'satisfaction' scores; Digital Twin Universe clones of Okta/Jira/Slack/Google for cheap high-volume testing; Attractor non-interactive agent published as NL specs (github.com/strongdm/attractor, 1.3k stars).
why_relevant: Q3: scenarios as a held-out oracle explicitly designed against reward hacking; satisfaction-across-trajectories instead of pass/fail. Q1: non-interactive coding-agent loop spec. Q4: public architecture but no outcome numbers.
claimed_results: Maturity benchmark: at least "$1,000 in tokens daily per engineer"; StrongDM AI team founded Jul 14 2025; inflection points Oct 2024 (Claude 3.5) and Dec 2024 (YOLO mode). No LOC, PR, defect or cost-outcome numbers published.

name: OctopusGarden (specs in, code out, holdout scenarios)
one_line: Markdown spec + YAML scenarios that the coding agent never sees; Docker build; LLM judge assigns 0-100 satisfaction; loop until >=95%; 'wonder/reflect' stall diagnosis then targeted fix.
why_relevant: Q3: held-out design nearly identical to ours (scenarios as true holdout, agent cannot game the metric). Q2: stall recovery = in-run healing. Small project, no evidence, but a direct architectural sibling.
claimed_results: None stated; 61 stars, 8 forks, 169 commits on 2026-09-02; Show HN Mar 3 2026 (8 pts).

name: pi-autocrit (persona critic loop for web prototypes)
one_line: Builder edits a web prototype; a separate-process persona critic with zero source access drives a real browser and scores tasks; keep/revert ratchet; four persona variants; sycophancy flag when variants uniformly score >80 with no criticism.
why_relevant: Q3: critic isolated from builder and sees only what a user sees; explicit sycophancy detector and variance tracking are reusable for our taste-critic and human-factors seats. Q2: keep/discard ratchet mirrors our anti-loop.
claimed_results: None; 14 stars, 35 commits; Show HN Apr 5 2026 (3 pts).

name: Lilian Weng: Harness engineering for self-improvement
one_line: Argues near-term recursive self-improvement lives in the harness (workflow loops, file-based memory, sub-agent parallelism, failure-pattern mining) rather than weights; names weak evaluators, reward hacking and diversity collapse as the blockers.
why_relevant: Q2 directly: surveys systems (Self-Harness, Agentic Harness Engineering) that mine failures -> propose bounded harness edits -> validate, all without fine-tuning — the loop our learning corpus + offline self-repair tier implements. Q3: weak evaluators identified as the limiting factor.
claimed_results: Jul 4 2026 (HN 334 pts, Aug 4 2026): DGM-discovered agents "20-50% on SWE-bench Verified and 14.2-30.7% on Polyglot"; AHE harness transferred from Terminal-Bench-2 to SWE-bench-verified without retraining; RE-Bench: agents ~4x humans at a 2-hour budget, humans ahead at 8h+.

name: karpathy/autoresearch + SkyPilot scaling report
one_line: Agent edits one file, runs a fixed 5-minute experiment, keeps or reverts on a frozen metric (val_bpb), ~100 experiments per night; SkyPilot scaled it to 16 GPUs overnight.
why_relevant: Q2: cleanest keep/revert ratchet against a metric the agent cannot edit (our sealed gate + fingerprint anti-loop). Q3: single-file scope bounds damage; fixed budget makes runs comparable. Adjacent domain (ML training) but mechanism transfers.
claimed_results: README: ~100 runs/night (~12/hour); 95.1k stars, 13.4k forks. SkyPilot (skypilot.ai/blog/scaling-autoresearch, Mar 18 2026): "~910 experiments, ~8 hours, 16 GPUs"; val_bpb "1.003" -> "0.974" ("2.87% improvement"); "9x faster" than sequential ("~8 hours vs ~72 hours"); "about $9" Claude API, under "$300" total; agent invented a cheap-H100-screen -> H200-promote tiering unprompted.

name: Every: compound-engineering-plugin
one_line: brainstorm -> plan -> work -> simplify -> review -> /ce-compound captures learnings that ground later brainstorms and plans; /lfg runs the whole loop hands-off across 14 agent platforms.
why_relevant: Q2: a shipped, widely adopted learning-corpus loop (lessons written after each task, injected into later planning) with no model change — the same mechanism as our failure->repair exemplar injection.
claimed_results: README example: an env-var pitfall recorded once resurfaced 18 days later in an unrelated planning session; "80% is in planning and review, 20% is in execution"; 24.8k stars, 2.0k forks on 2026-09-02. No quantitative outcome data.

name: akitaonrails: Harness/Loop/Graph Engineering are bullshit
one_line: Negative report with controlled runs: harnesses lift weak models a lot and strong models barely, at ~5x cost; no multi-agent combination beat a solo Opus run.
why_relevant: Q4 counter-evidence for Q1: argues per-seat budget is better spent on one strong model than on orchestration; useful as the null hypothesis our metrics (heldOutPass, falseFinish) must beat.
claimed_results: Aug 18 2026: Grok 4.3 "18→55" with harness vs Grok 4.5 "92 vs 91"; "$1.19 vs $6.33" for identical tasks; "three rounds" of strong-orchestrates-cheap never outperformed solo Opus; cites Berkeley survey of 86 production agents: "68%" execute <=10 steps before human intervention; author shipped 30+ public repos Jan-May 2026 without orchestration.

name: Kent Beck: Augmented coding, beyond the vibes
one_line: B+ tree in Rust/Python via strict TDD with Claude; three derail signals watched for: loops, unrequested functionality, and cheating "by disabling or deleting tests"; restarted twice.
why_relevant: Q3: test tampering named as a first-class failure signal to detect (our frozen/sealed suite); plan.md as an externally authored test list. Q4: honest first-hand, quality mixed.
claimed_results: Jun 25 2025: ~4 weeks; one 13-hour day; first two attempts abandoned for accumulated complexity (BPlusTree3 restart); result "faster at range scanning" than stdlib on some ops but author "not so good about the code quality".

name: Anthropic: An update on recent Claude Code quality reports (Apr 23 postmortem)
one_line: Three silent regressions in Claude Code (reasoning-effort default, a cache bug clearing reasoning every turn, a '<=25 words' prompt line) degraded agent quality for weeks before detection.
why_relevant: Q2 drift detection: the substrate under every seat drifts without notice; motivates our frozen known-bad corpus and per-release baseline runs rather than trusting the CLI.
claimed_results: Apr 23 2026: effort default high->medium (Mar 4-Apr 7, Sonnet/Opus 4.6); caching bug cleared reasoning history each turn (Mar 26-Apr 10); verbosity instruction caused "a 3% drop for both Opus 4.6 and 4.7" in evals (Apr 16-20); defaults reverted to xhigh (Opus 4.7) / high.

name: METR: Early-2025 AI-experienced OSS developer RCT
one_line: Randomized controlled trial of experienced open-source developers with and without AI tools.
why_relevant: Q4 calibration: the only randomized measurement in this modality; supervised rather than unattended use, so it bounds how much to trust the self-reported speedups in the entries above.
claimed_results: Jul 10 2025: "when developers use AI tools, they take 19% longer than without"; 16 developers, 246 issues (~2h each). Authors published a Feb 2026 update on late-2025 tools stating the 2025 result "no longer reflect[s] the current impact of AI models on open-source developer productivity".

name: SWE-bench Verified / Multilingual leaderboard (SWE-bench/experiments)
one_line: Organiser-run leaderboard where 'checked' means maintainers re-ran a random subset from the submitter's instructions; since 2025-11-18 Verified/Multilingual only accept academic, open-source, peer-reviewed methods.
why_relevant: Q3/Q4: defines checked vs self-reported and shows which open scaffolds were actually reproduced. Verified folder froze at 20250725 (138 entries); all 2026 checked entries are mini-swe-agent bash-only runs on the Multilingual split, so post-2025 scaffold claims on Verified are self-reported by construction.
claimed_results: data/leaderboards.json (master), Multilingual: Gemini 3 Flash 72.7 (2026-02-13, verified=true, oss=true, folder 20260213_mini-v2.0.0a0_gemini-3-flash); Claude 4.6 Opus 72.0 (2026-02-13, verified=true, oss=true). Newest folder 20260902_mini-v2.4.6_gemini-3-5-flash. Verified: no folder after 20250725_sweagent_devstral_small_2507; 138 folders total. Policy note 11/18/2025: 'Verified and Multilingual now only accepts submissions from academic teams and research institutions with open source methods and peer-reviewed publications.'

name: mini-swe-agent (SWE-bench 'Bash Only')
one_line: ~100-line bash-only agent (subprocess.run per action, strictly linear history, no custom tools) that became the reference harness for SWE-bench Bash Only, SWE-bench Pro, Vals and Ramp re-runs.
why_relevant: Q4: the most independently reproduced scaffold in existence; its checked numbers are the floor any multi-agent design must beat. Mechanism to copy: stateless per-command execution and a linear, replayable trajectory.
claimed_results: README: '>74% on the SWE-bench verified benchmark'; docs news 2025-11-19: 'Gemini 3 Pro reaches 74% on SWE-bench verified with mini-swe-agent'; checked Multilingual entries 2026-02-13: Gemini 3 Flash 72.7, Claude 4.6 Opus 72.0; SWE-agent README: '65% on SWE-bench verified in 100 lines of Python'. 6.9k stars, 1,020 commits. Powers 'Ramp SWE-Bench' (labs.ramp.com/swebench).

name: SWE-bench Pro (Scale AI)
one_line: Scale-run long-horizon issue benchmark; entries run by Scale with SWE-agent (250-turn cap) or mini-swe-agent (asterisked).
why_relevant: Q4: unsaturated successor to Verified (best ~60%) run by a third party with one scaffold; the harness repo is MIT so the same environments can be reused for our own gate experiments.
claimed_results: Page as of 2026-09-02 (entry dates not shown): Muse Spark 1.1* 61.50±3.10%; gpt-5.4 (xHigh)* 59.10±3.56%; Muse Spark* 55.00±3.60%; claude-opus-4-6 (thinking)* 51.90±3.61%; gemini-3.1-pro (thinking)* 46.10±3.60%; Llama4-Maverick 5.24±1.24%; Codestral 1.51±1.51% (* = mini-swe-agent harness). Repo scaleapi/SWE-bench_Pro-os: 518 stars, MIT; mini-swe-agent added 'October 28' with 'results comparable to SWE-Agent for Sonnet 4.5'. OpenHands blog 2026-08-07 cites SWE-bench Pro: Claude Fable 5 80.0%, GLM-5.2 62.1%, Inkling 54.3% (not visible on the Scale page).

name: Terminal-Bench 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 (+ paper arXiv 2601.11868)
one_line: Organiser-run terminal-task benchmark: six agents x 16 models, >=5 trials each via Harbor; versions 2.0 (2025-11-07), 2.1 (2026-05-06), 3.0 (2026-07-30), 4.0 (2026-08-28).
why_relevant: Q4: the only organiser-run head-to-head of scaffolds (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenHands, mini-swe-agent, Terminus 2) on identical tasks; headline finding 'model selection is usually more important than agent scaffold'. Q3: task QA ran 'an adversarial exploit agent ... to detect design flaws that could allow agents to cheat and pass the tests', and the failure taxonomy has a Verification class (premature termination, weak verification) = our falseFinish.
claimed_results: Paper (submitted 2026-01-17): 89 tasks; 32,155 trials; Codex CLI + GPT-5.2 63%; Terminus 2 + Claude Opus 4.5 58%; Terminus 2 + Gemini 3 Pro 57%; best open-weight Terminus 2 + Kimi K2 Thinking 36%; 'Codex CLI resolution rate increases by 52% when using GPT-5.2 instead of GPT-5-Nano, while Gemini-2.5-Pro sees a 17% increase ... when paired with Terminus 2 instead of OpenHands'; 'essentially no correlation between the number of average turns per trial and model success rates'; command failures: 'Command not found' 24.1%. TB 2.1 post (2026-05-06, 28 of 89 tasks fixed): GPT-5.3-Codex (Codex CLI) 73.3%->79.1%; Gemini 3.1 Pro (Terminus 2) 63.0%->70.7%; Opus 4.6 (Claude Code) 58.0%->70.1%; Sonnet 4.6 (Claude Code) 51.9%->58.5%. TB 3.0 post (2026-07-30): 74 tasks/7 domains; GPT-5.6 Sol (Codex) 34.4%; Fable 5 (Claude Code) 33.8%; Opus 4.8 (Claude Code) 21.1%; GPT-5.6 Terra (Codex) 20.8%; Grok 4.5 (Cursor CLI) 17.8%; Sonnet 5 (Claude Code) 14.6%. TB 4.0 (2026-08-28): 8 saturated tasks removed, 19 fixed, uniform 8-hour timeout; Harbor Hub lists 66 tasks.

name: Harbor framework + Terminus 2
one_line: Evaluation harness behind Terminal-Bench; bundles Terminus-2 (one tool: a headless terminal), Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenHands, mini-swe-agent, MCode, fx; runs agents inside sandbox providers (Daytona, Modal, etc.).
why_relevant: Q3: a sealed-container evaluation runner with pluggable agents and hidden tests per task — the generalised form of our Docker gate; also 'generate rollouts for RL optimization'. Q4: Terminus 2 is the neutral-scaffold baseline in every TB table.
claimed_results: 4.9k stars, 1.7k forks, 1,574 commits; 'harbor run --dataset terminal-bench@2.0'; TB paper ran 32-100 containers in parallel on Daytona. Terminus 2 scores via TB: + Claude Opus 4.5 58% (TB 2.0), + Gemini 3.1 Pro 70.7% (TB 2.1, 2026-05-06). DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20953922.

name: OpenHands Index
one_line: OpenHands-run index (launched 2026-01-29) scoring models on one scaffold (OpenHands SDK) across issue resolution (SWE-bench Verified), greenfield app creation (commit0), frontend (SWE-bench Multimodal verified subset), test generation (SWT-Bench) and GAIA.
why_relevant: Q1/Q4: the only 2026 leaderboard with 'greenfield' and 'frontend' columns, i.e. our ticket-to-app task, with per-category cost — usable to pick a different model per seat. Q3: the SWT-Bench column measures write-tests-from-issue, which is the spec seat's job.
claimed_results: scores.json, OpenHands v1.18.1: claude-fable-5 (2026-06-11/12): swe-bench 95.8 ($1.43/inst), commit0 62.5 ($12.49, 1094s), swe-bench-multimodal 70.6 (solveable_accuracy), swt-bench 91.9, gaia 84.2. claude-opus-4-8 (2026-05-30..06-02): 83.8 / 62.5 / 50.0 / 84.3 / 78.8. GPT-5.5 (2026-04-27..05-08): 78.2 / 43.8 / 38.2 / 83.4 / 86.1. DeepSeek-V4-Pro (2026-05-16..20): 73.2 / 12.5 / 36.8 / 68.1 / 12.7. Launch post 2026-01-29: Claude 4.5 Opus overall winner; GPT 5.2 Codex 'excels at greenfield development'. 739 commits; harness github.com/OpenHands/benchmarks (MIT, 118 stars).

name: commit0
one_line: Rebuild 54 core Python libraries from spec + docs, graded solely by the libraries' own held-out unit tests; closest public analogue to 'ticket in, working software out'.
why_relevant: Q1/Q3: greenfield build against a frozen suite the agent did not write; original leaderboard shows a unit-test feedback loop alone lifts Sonnet 3.5 from 18.63% to 30.59%. Still run in 2026 inside OpenHands Index.
claimed_results: commit-0.github.io/analysis: Reference (Gold) 100.00% lite / 98.29% all; OpenHands 41.24% (subset, 11/25/2024), 15.08% (all); Claude Sonnet 3.5 'Fill-in + Unit Test Feedback' 30.59% lite vs 'Fill-in' 18.63% vs 'Base' 18.38% (09/25/2024); SWE-Agent 9.70% subset (11/26/2024), 2.99% all. OpenHands Index 2026 (accuracy): claude-fable-5 62.5, claude-opus-4-8 62.5, GPT-5.5 43.8, DeepSeek-V4-Pro 12.5. 191 stars, 646 commits, MIT.

name: SWT-Bench (+ PatchTwin+Guard, ReProAgent)
one_line: Write a test from an issue that fails before the fix and passes after (F->P); leaderboard at swtbench.com states 'We have independently executed submitted predictions for verification'.
why_relevant: Q3: our spec seat authors tests from the ticket alone; SWT-Bench grades exactly that, with a built-in negative control (test must fail on the broken code). Open 2026 entries: PatchTwin+Guard (fix + reproduction-test pairs; 'Guard ... is invoked after test runs' to check the test reproduces the issue and the fix is complete) and ReProAgent (LangGraph pipeline: localisation -> root cause -> assertion-aware plan -> 'triadic review').
claimed_results: swtbench.com (two fetches gave two columns, likely Success vs F->P): Verified: TEX-T (Claude 4 Sonnet) 87.0% / 69.8%, 2025-12-17, closed; LogicStar L*Agent v1 84.0%, 2025-09-13, closed; PatchTwin+Guard (GPT-5) 82.9% / 78.7%, 2026-07-08, open (github.com/lbaf23/PatchTwin, 2 stars). Lite: DevstralTestGen (Devstral 2) 89.1% / 57.6%, 2026-03-13; ReProAgent (GPT-5-mini) 56.2% / 64.8%, 2026-04-20, open (github.com/iSEngLab/ReProAgent, 3 stars); AEGIS 47.8% / 26.0%, 2025-02-17. Splits: Full 2,294 / Lite 276 / Verified 433. OpenHands Index swt-bench: fable-5 91.9 (2026-06-12), opus-4-8 84.3.

name: SWE-bench-Live (Microsoft)
one_line: Auto-refreshing (+50 Python issues/month) multi-language (1,077 MultiLang tasks) and Windows issue benchmark; frozen lite/verified splits, contamination-resistant test split.
why_relevant: Q4: 2026 agent-system results on a TS/JS split (our target stack); open SWE-agent still tops Lite; closed AMI Agent and Slingshot lead the 2026 multi-language splits; OpenHands is the open reference.
claimed_results: reports-0605.jsonl: Lite (300): SWE-agent + Claude-4.5-Sonnet 200 (2025-12-31, open source); AMI Agent + Claude-4.6-Opus 189 (2026-06-23); SWE-agent + Claude 3.7 Sonnet 177 (2025-05-01); Slingshot + Claude-4.6-Opus 75 (2026-08-17). TS/JS (204): AMI Agent + Claude-4.6-Opus 112 (2026-07-10); Slingshot-v3.0.0 + GPT-5.5 Medium 98 (2026-07-30); OpenHands + GPT-5.5 Medium 92 (2026-06-05). Go (138): AMI + Opus 4.6 103 (2026-07-16), + Sonnet 4.6 99 (2026-07-23), + Haiku 4.5 90 (2026-07-29). Java (109): AMI + Opus 4.6 73 (2026-08-17). README news: 08/21/2026 MultiLang 1,077 tasks, RepoLaunch 98% env-build success; 03/08/2026 Windows dataset; 01/10/2026 multi-language leaderboard.

name: AMI Agent (Superinference)
one_line: Proprietary single agent (binary install) leading most 2026 SWE-bench-Live splits; README lists contextual memory with automatic compaction, self-correction with error classification, belief tracking, multi-turn planning, 140-turn cap, detached mode.
why_relevant: Q4: evidence that a single agent with self-correction and compaction beats the multi-agent entries on live tasks; no critic or test-time scaling claimed. Q2 (weak): 'error classification' feeding self-correction is a runtime learning loop we could mirror with our failure->repair corpus.

name: TRAE Agent (ByteDance)
one_line: Open agent whose leaderboard number comes from generation -> pruning -> selection: N coder trajectories (mixed models), patch dedup, regression-test filter, then a selector agent voted N times in parallel.
why_relevant: Q1/Q3/Q4: the most concrete multi-agent + independent-verification recipe with ablations: regression tests as a non-self-graded filter, a separate selector as critic, model mixture for diversity. Note the leaderboard entry is checked: False with attempts '2+'.
claimed_results: arXiv 2507.23370 (2025-07-31): 75.20% Pass@1 SWE-bench Verified; 'average improvement of 10.22% over all baselines'; N=3 primary (1-10 tested); dedup removes 'an average of 28.90%'; 'Patches that fail any regression test are discarded'; ablation Pass@1 Trae/Oracle/Average: Gemini 2.5 Pro 62.27/66.20/53.40; Claude 3.7 Sonnet 66.40/70.00/61.33; GPT-4.1 59.00/63.00/51.40; Mixture 65.67/73.40/56.33. Blog 2025-05-19: 70.6% with Coder agents (Claude 3.7, Gemini 2.5 Pro, o4-mini), Tester agent regression filter, Selector agent voting; optimum 5-6 candidates. experiments metadata 20250612_trae: checked: False, attempts 2+, models Sonnet 4/Opus 4/Sonnet 3.7/Gemini 2.5 Pro. 12.1k stars, 289 commits.

name: Lingxi (multi-agent, v1.5 / v2.0)
one_line: Open multi-agent framework: Supervisor, Problem Decoder, Solution Mapper, Problem Solver, Reviewer (hierarchy graph adds reviewer-driven iteration), each agent given 'a crystal-clear contract' of inputs/outputs/tools.
why_relevant: Q1: lead + specialists + reviewer topology closest to Claude Code agent teams among leaderboard entries. Q4 caution: v1.5 is oss=true but verified=false; the v2.0 81.2% PR has sat unmerged since 2026-03-28.
claimed_results: v1.5: 373/500 = 74.6% Claude 4 Sonnet (folder 20250720, metadata verified: false, open-source system: true). v2.0: 406/500 = 81.2% with MiniMax-M2.5, PR SWE-bench/experiments#432 opened 2026-03-28, status open, no maintainer comments. 259 stars.

name: AgentScope SWE-bench entry (multi-agent + trained reward-model voting)
one_line: Reproduction agent writes bug-verification tests first, fixing agent patches, testing agent runs unit tests; four trial runs, then a trained reward model (Qwen-2.5-Coder + scalar head via OpenRLHF) votes.
why_relevant: Q1/Q3: explicit test-writer / fixer / tester role split with a learned judge choosing among trials; the tests-before-fix ordering matches our spec-before-build design.
claimed_results: 63.4% (317/500) SWE-bench Verified, Claude-3.5-Sonnet-20241022, 2025-02-06; /trajs holds 'full logs for our four trial runs, along with the message input and output results from the voting process'.

name: OpenHands critic model + inference-time scaling (reused by Skywork-SWE Bo8)
one_line: Trajectory-level critic (Qwen 2.5 Coder 32B, TD learning from unit-test outcomes, gamma=0.99) selecting best-of-5 OpenHands runs; Skywork reused the released critic unchanged.
why_relevant: Q2/Q3: a critic trained purely on execution outcomes (not self-grading) lifts pass rate; requires fine-tuning we cannot do, but the scoring target (whole trajectory judged against held-out test outcome) transfers to a prompt-based judge.
claimed_results: 2025-04-17: 60.6% single rollout -> 66.4% with five attempts ('log-linear'); critic HF all-hands/openhands-critic-32b-exp-20250417. Skywork-SWE-32B (HF card, arXiv 2506.19290, 2025-06-24): 38.0% pass@1 (190/500) -> 47.0% (235/500) with Bo8 using 'AllHands Critic'; leaderboard folder 20250616_Skywork-SWE-32B+TTS_Bo8.

name: DeepSWE hybrid test-time scaling (rLLM / R2E-Gym)
one_line: RL-trained 32B agent whose reported score relies on a hybrid verifier: execution-based (generate tests, keep the trajectory passing most) + execution-free LLM verifier, over K=16 rollouts.
why_relevant: Q3: cleanest public ablation of execution verifier vs LLM verifier vs hybrid; each alone ~+10 points, hybrid +17; 'majority of gains at K=8' bounds how many candidates a fix seat should spawn.
claimed_results: Together blog 2025-07-02 / experiments folder 20250629_deepswerl_r2eagent_tts: Pass@1 42.2%, Pass@16 71.0%, hybrid TTS 59% (59.2% in README); execution-based alone '~10% improvement over Pass@1', execution-free alone '~10%'; 'a majority of TTS's performance gains can be achieved with K=8'. 410 stars.

name: Refact.ai Agent
one_line: Open, self-hosted agent that held the top organiser-checked open-source SWE-bench Verified score in mid-2025; repo and bench pipeline archived in 2026.
why_relevant: Q4: one of the few multi-model open entries with the organiser checkmark; also a cautionary datapoint on maintenance (archived 2026-05-30).
claimed_results: 74.4% (372/500) SWE-bench Verified, Claude 4 Sonnet + o4-mini, 2025-06-03, metadata Verified: yes, attempts 1; previous 70.4% with Claude 3.7. 3.5k stars. Archived 2026-05-30 (moved to JegernOUTT/refact); refact-bench (60 stars) archived 2026-04-30.

name: Augment SWE-bench agent (o1 majority-vote selector)
one_line: Claude 3.7 generates candidate diffs; o1 is shown the list plus the problem statement and asked to pick the majority-vote solution; later dropped as too expensive.
why_relevant: Q3/Q4: independent-model selector over candidates gave +3-8%, but the vendor's own verdict was it is 'too expensive to use in real-world settings' — a budget datapoint for our per-seat lines.
claimed_results: Blog 2025-03-31: 65.4% SWE-bench Verified (Claude 3.7 + o1 ensembler), ensembling +3-8%. experiments 20250610_augment_agent_v1: 70.4% with Claude Sonnet 4, basic single agent, no ensembling.

name: Warp agent
one_line: Single-agent single-attempt design: TODO-list planning tool, model failover chain, tool-failure reporting back to the model, fuzzy edit matching (Jaro-Winkler); best@k explored and rejected.
why_relevant: Q4: documented negative result on multi-attempt selection from a production vendor; failover chain and fuzzy edit matching are cheap mechanisms to copy.
claimed_results: 2025-06-23: 71% SWE-bench Verified; failover Claude 4 Sonnet -> Claude 3.7 Sonnet -> Gemini 2.5 Pro -> GPT-4.1; 'best@k' approaches were explored but not retained.

name: OpenHands
one_line: The most-used open scaffold in organiser-run tables (SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench, SWE-bench-Live, its own Index); now a self-hosted control centre that can also drive Claude Code / Codex / Gemini agents; Agent Canvas merged in.
why_relevant: Q1/Q4: reference single-agent baseline across every leaderboard with real production adoption; its leaderboard entries use no multi-agent or critic (Kimi K2 run = single pass, 100 iterations).
claimed_results: SWE-bench Verified 65.4% (327/500) with moonshot/kimi-k2-0711-preview, 2025-07-16, single pass; SWE-bench-Live TS/JS 92/204 GPT-5.5 Medium (2026-06-05); TB 2.0 paper: Gemini 2.5 Pro scores 17% higher with Terminus 2 than with OpenHands; Index (v1.18.1) fable-5 SWE-bench 95.8 / commit0 62.5. 85.9k stars; v1.16.0 in README; agent-canvas archived 2026-07-27 into main repo.

name: Codex CLI (OpenAI)
one_line: Apache-2.0 terminal agent; the highest-scoring scaffold on Terminal-Bench 2.0/2.1/3.0 when paired with OpenAI models; README describes no subagent/critic features.
why_relevant: Q4: open code for the top TB scaffold; its lead is model-driven (the paper's +52% from GPT-5-Nano to GPT-5.2 on the same scaffold), reinforcing 'invest in verification, not scaffold cleverness'.
claimed_results: TB paper (2026-01): Codex CLI + GPT-5.2 63%; TB 2.1 (2026-05-06): GPT-5.3-Codex 79.1%; TB 3.0 (2026-07-30): GPT-5.6 Sol 34.4%; SWE-rebench: Codex (Agent) 58.0%±1.29, pass@5 73.0, $1.59/problem. 120.9k stars.

name: HAL - Holistic Agent Leaderboard (Princeton)
one_line: Third-party, cost-aware runs of agent scaffolds (SWE-Agent, Claude Code, CORE-Agent, ...) across 9 benchmarks; all 2.5B tokens of logs released.
why_relevant: Q3/Q4: independent runs of real products with cost; log inspection surfaced shortcut behaviours (agents searching HuggingFace for benchmark answers) = our falseFinish class; 'higher reasoning effort reducing accuracy in the majority of runs'.
claimed_results: arXiv 2510.11977 (2025-10-13, ICLR 2026): 21,730 rollouts, 9 models x 9 benchmarks, ~$40,000. Leaderboard: SWE-bench Verified Mini: SWE-Agent + Claude Sonnet 4.5 High 72.0% ($463.90), + Opus 4.1 68.0% ($1,351.35), + Sonnet 4.5 68.0% ($505.92); CORE-Bench Hard: Claude Code (Opus 4.5) 77.8% ($87.16; 95.5% with manual scoring), Claude Code (Sonnet 4.5) 62.2% ($68.33), CORE-Agent (Opus 4.1) 51.1% ($412.42); USACO o3 Medium 69.1% ($116.63).

name: SWE-rebench (Nebius)
one_line: Monthly contamination-free issues; same scaffold for every model, plus agent products (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Junie) run on identical tasks with pass@5 and cost per problem.
why_relevant: Q4: direct evidence that product scaffolds do not beat a bare model on the same tasks (Claude Code 60.4% vs Fable 5 raw 64.5%); pass@5 vs pass@1 gap (+14 points) is the headroom a good selector could claim.

name: Vals AI SWE-bench Verified (bash-only re-runs)
one_line: Third-party re-run of 86 models on SWE-bench Verified with a minimal bash-only (mini-SWE-agent) harness.
why_relevant: Q4: shows Verified is saturated (7 of 86 models >=95%), so 2026 scaffold comparisons must use Pro / Live / Terminal-Bench / commit0 instead.
claimed_results: 2026-08-30: Claude Opus 5 97.00%; DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 96.40%; Kimi K3 93.40%; Claude Opus 4.8 88.60%; Grok 4.5 86.60%; 'Seven of the 86 models evaluated reach 95% or better'. OpenHands blog 2026-08-07 cites the Vals 2026-07-17 run: GPT-5.6 Sol 96.2%, Claude Fable 5 95.0%, Kimi K3 93.4%, Claude Opus 4.8 88.6%, GLM-5.2 82.8%.

name: METR Time Horizon 1.1
one_line: 228-task suite (HCAST/RE-Bench/SWAA lineage) now run on UK AISI Inspect; 50%/80% horizons per model with CIs and doubling times.
why_relevant: Q4: calibrates how long an unattended single-agent task can run before success falls below 50% (Opus 4.5 ~5.3 h) — the reason our 1-12 h runs need stage splitting and gates.
claimed_results: 2026-01-29: 50% horizons Claude Opus 4.5 320 min [170-729]; GPT-5 214 [117-480]; o3 121 [74-201]; Claude Opus 4 101 [58-170]; doubling 196.5 days overall, 130.8 since 2023, 88.6 since 2024; 228 tasks (73 new, 31 tasks >=8h, measured human baselines for only 5 of those). Code github.com/METR/eval-analysis-public.

name: MirrorCode (Epoch AI; linked by METR)
one_line: Reimplement a CLI program from execute-only access + docs + visible tests; graded by hidden 'dual' tests paired with each visible test to defeat hard-coding.
why_relevant: Q3: the visible/hidden paired-test design is our visible/held-out split with an anti-overfit twist worth copying. Q4: documents premature 'done' in older models and the token budgets weeks-long tasks need.
claimed_results: 2026-04-10, Claude Opus 4.6, ReAct scaffold on Inspect, up to 1B tokens (~$550/task): choose (931 LoC, 127 tests) solved; cal (984 LoC, 1,365 tests) solved; gotree (16,905 LoC) 2,000/2,001 tests, est. human time 2-17 weeks; Pkl (61,461 LoC) 256/733 = 35%; 24 target programs, 4 reported; 'Older models submitted prematurely despite explicit warnings'. Data github.com/epoch-research/MirrorCode-data.

name: SWE-Lancer (OpenAI)
one_line: 1,400+ real Upwork tasks ($1M payouts); IC tasks graded by engineer-written end-to-end Playwright tests, triple-reviewed and auto-checked to fail on the broken state and pass on the fixed state.
why_relevant: Q3: identical gate design to ours (held-out Playwright E2E) including the negative-control requirement this project's memory notes flag as its weak spot; also shows more attempts monotonically raise pass rate.
claimed_results: arXiv 2502.12115 (2025-02-17), Diamond set 502 tasks / $500,800: Claude 3.5 Sonnet IC SWE pass@1 26.2% ($58k), SWE Manager 44.9% ($150k), total $208k (41.5%); o1 (high) 16.5% / 41.5% / $166k (33.1%); GPT-4o 8.0% / 37.0% / $139k (27.7%); o1 pass@6 on IC Diamond 16.5%. Repo archived into openai/preparedness 2025-07-18.

name: WebGen-Bench
one_line: Generate a working website from a natural-language instruction; graded by a browser agent (WebVoyager) executing 647 test cases plus screenshot appearance grading; forks of Bolt.diy, OpenHands and Aider evaluated.
why_relevant: Q1/Q3: the only benchmark whose task is literally 'build me this website', judged by an external UI agent driving the rendered app rather than unit tests — the same shape as our held-out Playwright suite and taste critic.
claimed_results: arXiv 2505.03733 (2025-05-06, v2 2025-08-11): best proprietary setup 'Bolt.diy powered by DeepSeek-R1, achieves only 27.8% accuracy'; WebGen-LM (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B trained on Bolt.diy trajectories) 38.2%; 647 test cases, 6,667 training instructions.

name: Web-Bench (ByteDance)
one_line: 50 web projects x 20 sequential dependent tasks (4-8 engineer-hours per project), pass@1 over the whole chain.
why_relevant: Q1: sequential-ticket web-app building; quantifies how fast chained web tasks collapse (25.1%), motivating our per-stage gates and continuation lane.
claimed_results: arXiv 2505.07473: Claude 3.7 Sonnet 'only 25.1% Pass@1'. 292 stars, 108 commits, Apache 2.0; leaderboard on Hugging Face Spaces.

name: Arena.ai WebDev (Code) and Agent leaderboards
one_line: Crowd pairwise votes on generated front-end apps (WebDev) and on tool-orchestration sessions (Agent); ranks models, not scaffolds.
why_relevant: Q4 (weak): 2026 human-preference ranking for the front-end output our design lane produces; no scaffold or verification information.
claimed_results: WebDev 2026-09-02, 639,235 votes / 122 models: qwen3.8-max-0902 1691; claude-opus-5-max 1687; kimi-k3-max 1674; qwen3.8-max 1669; claude-opus-5-high 1661; grok-4.6-high 1629; claude-fable-5 1628; gpt-5.6-sol-xhigh 1616; glm-5.3-max 1609. Agent 2026-09-01, 2,169,319 sessions / 56 models: Claude Opus 5 (High) 13.74%; Claude Opus 5 (Max) 11.69%; Claude Fable 5 (High) 10.61%; GPT 5.6 Sol (xHigh) 9.49%; GLM 5.2 (Max) 6.23% (MIT).
